items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Warm up adaptive verification budget kernel at startup
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adaptive verification's draft-budget kernel (`_assign_draft_token_budget`, `torch.compile(dynamic=True)`) never runs at startup. Dynamo therefore compiles it during serving: on the first trimmed step, and again for each specialization it meets later. This PR compiles those specializations at startup.

## Claims

- No budget-kernel compiles during generation (main: 2 per run).
- Adaptive throughput +10% at concurrency 16, matching fixed verification again.
- About 1 s extra startup.

## Validation

`pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -v` → 18 passed (RTX 5000 Ada). The new test checks that no recompile happens under `fail_on_recompile`. It fails with `warmup()` stubbed out, and with an int32 `idx_mapping`.

`pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` passes locally, including mypy.

GSM8K 1-shot, `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7`, 7 speculative tokens, probabilistic drafts, concurrency 16, 128 prompts, RTX 5000 Ada, `TRITON_ATTN`. Main and this PR alternated:

| | Output tok/s, median (range) | Compiles during generation | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed verification (n=2) | 1,909 | – | 0.828 |
| Adaptive, main (n=5) | 1,738 (1,615–1,753) | 2 | 0.82–0.84 |
| Adaptive, this PR (n=5) | 1,914 (1,710–1,921) | 0 | 0.820 |

An earlier RTX 3090 run (Qwen3.5-0.8B) showed the same: −7.9% before, no loss after.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

Compiles were counted with `TORCH_LOGS=dynamo`, as `start tracing _assign_draft_token_budget` lines between the two markers. "Main" runs used this branch with `vllm/` checked out at `HEAD~1`.

```python
import json
import sys

from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import evaluate_gsm8k_offline
from vllm import LLM

mode, conc = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-4B",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "dspark",
        "model": "deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 7,
        "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
        "enable_adaptive_verification": mode == "adaptive",
    },
    max_num_seqs=conc,
    max_model_len=4096,
    enable_prefix_caching=False,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
    attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN",
)
print("=== GENERATE START ===", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
result = evaluate_gsm8k_offline(llm, num_questions=8 * conc, num_shots=1)
print("=== GENERATE END ===", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
print("RESULT", json.dumps({"mode": mode, "conc": conc, **result}), flush=True)
```

</details>

## Details

- Startup never reaches the kernel: `warmup_kernels` disables adaptive verification, and cost profiling never trims. Dynamo then specializes on a full batch (duck-sized to `confidence_probs`), a single request, and a budget of 1.
- `warmup()` runs batch sizes {1, max−1, max} × budgets {1, 2}. It uses the manager's real buffers and `prepare_inputs`' int64 `idx_mapping` (#60736), since guards check dispatch keys and dtypes. It's skipped on the `profile_only` pass, whose buffers are torn down.
- Not a duplicate: #59976 skips adaptive verification; #58340 only adds metrics.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks
items.body:
## Purpose

Adaptive DSpark derives its verification budget from rank-local confidence state. Small differences across TP ranks can therefore produce different total budgets or per-request boundaries, causing divergent execution layouts and possible collective hangs.

This change makes rank 0 authoritative for both values:

- broadcast the selected draft budget;
- broadcast partial-allocation capacities before building request boundaries.

The adaptive policy remains enabled and unchanged. Related to #54011. I found no open PR implementing this TP-consensus fix.

## Test Plan

- Unit coverage for TP1/2/4/8 with deliberately different rank-local confidences.
- Real NCCL TP2 and TP4 tests on H100s with Qwen3-4B and the official `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` draft.
- Natural adaptive rank tracing, GSM8K correctness, and concurrency-128 serving stress.

## Test Result

- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -q`: 33 passed in the CUDA validation environment.
- `pre-commit run --files ...`: passed all applicable hooks.
- Injected rank drift: original code produced 20 consensus mismatches at both TP2 and TP4; patched code produced 0. Each run covered 120 compiled allocation cases and CUDA-graph boundary replays.
- Natural adaptive execution remained active: TP2 had 568 partial-budget steps; TP4 had 559. Budget and request-boundary traces matched exactly across all ranks.
- Patched TP2 and TP4 each completed 2,304/2,304 requests at observed concurrency 128 with no request failures or hangs.
- GSM8K completed all 1,319 samples with no invalid or empty responses. TP2: 86.20% original vs 86.43% patched; TP4: 85.75% vs 85.44% (net -4 answers, treated as finite-sample variation rather than equivalence proof).

The original issue's TP8/H20/DeepSeek-V4 environment was not available for end-to-end validation.

@LucasWilkinson @benchislett @zihanlin-ai @DingYinfan — would appreciate your review, especially of the TP-consensus boundary. Thanks!

AI assistance was used for test orchestration and review; I reviewed the changes and validation results.

items.title: [ROCm][Spec Decode] Enable adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3
items.body:
## Summary

PR adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3 on ROCm. Part of the adaptive DSpark backend expansion (#51303): each model needs varlen-capable sparse kernels before adaptive verification can redistribute draft tokens across requests
It was validated end to end with amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 and nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark on MI325.

Scope: only the ROCm Triton indexer and sparse-decode paths gain ragged decode support. The CUDA and AITER MiniMax M3 backends still report device/CPU query-length mismatch as unsupported, so adaptive verification stays disabled there. With adaptive verification off, the uniform decode path is unchanged.

## Changes

- MiniMax M3 indexer and sparse attention (ROCm Triton): device-side ragged decode metadata; both AMD index-score launch policies, the fused top-k selector, and sparse decode map packed query tokens to requests from device `query_start_loc`.
- `kernel_paged_attention_2d`: return for `query_len != 1` (previously `> 1`). FULL cudagraph replay can pad the request dimension with zero-length rows, which fell into the decode path and read one row past the logical query buffer.
- Rejection sampler: adaptive verification allows the regular chunked path for batches with no draft tokens, whose logits layout isnever compacted.
- Warmup: synthetic draft rows are bounded by the same rejection-sampler budget used at runtime, so large `max_num_seqs` configs nolonger fail at startup.
- Adaptive verification overhead: confidence D2H copies use a non-blocking ring, and only TP rank 0 computes the draft budget, thenbroadcasts it.
- DSpark config: prefer speculators-format top-level confidence-head fields and fall back to NVIDIA's legacy `dflash_config` fields.


Token-to-request mapping uses upstream's `compute_token_to_req_indices`, a device-side binary search over `query_start_loc`. It doesn't depend on `max_query_len` and handles zero-length rows and the padding tail.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs (adaptive verification, MiniMax M3 DSpark, token-to-request mapping, paged-decode zero-length). The closest is #52893, which skips AITER sparse PA under spec decode; this PR adds ragged decode to the Triton path instead.

## Testing

On MI325:
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`: 138 passed, 1 skipped.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py`: all passed.
- `test_prefix_prefill.py::test_contexted_kv_attention` (`chunked_prefill_paged_decode`, source build of this branch): 128 passed, 256 skipped.

- Stress test of the ragged index top-k and sparse decode kernels at serving-sized batches: 60 random batches of 380–512 requests (1–8 query tokens each, up to 4K context, zero-length padding rows), reference-checked every 10th batch: all passed.

## End-to-end results 

MI325, `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark` drafter with its default confidence head, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, FULL cudagraphs, default memory settings, `--max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 512`. Fixed vs adaptive verification on the same build.

GSM8K, full test set (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 64):

| Checkpoint | TP | Fixed | Adaptive |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` | 2 | 0.8196 | 0.8226 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` | 4 | 0.8779 | 0.8711 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` (BF16) | 8 | 0.8704 | 0.8688 |

Repeated MXFP8 runs vary by about ±0.01 for both modes (fixed 0.860–0.878 over 6 runs, adaptive 0.867–0.879 over 9 runs). One earlyadaptive MXFP8 run scored 0.801; it did not reproduce in 9 later runs and is still being investigated.

Sonnet 550 in / 150 out / 200 shared prefix, ignore EOS, output tok/s (adaptive gain vs fixed):

| Concurrency | MXFP4, TP=2 | MXFP8, TP=4 | BF16, TP=8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 649.96 → 674.59 (+3.8%) | 2241.79 → 2166.80 (−3.3%) | 3451.90 → 3327.16 (−3.6%) |
| 256 | 882.77 → 930.58 (+5.4%) | 2560.18 → 2605.40 (+1.8%) | 4005.66 → 4063.85 (+1.5%) |
| 320 | 965.59 → 1020.85 (+5.7%) | 2643.30 → 2733.47 (+3.4%) | 4099.15 → 4268.66 (+4.1%) |
| 380 | 1013.94 → 1071.63 (+5.7%) | 2686.83 → 2778.46 (+3.4%) | 4190.48 → crash (see below) |
| 420 | 1040.76 → 1102.05 (+5.9%) | 2713.55 → 2692.00 (−0.8%) | 4263.58 → crash |
| 500 | 1089.06 → 1146.61 (+5.3%) | fixed OOM → 1929.71 | 4228.05 → crash |

The gain shrinks as verification gets cheaper: TP=4 and TP=8 leave little verify cost for adaptive budgeting to save. MXFP8 fixed verification at concurrency 500 runs out of memory allocating the full verification logits (1.6 GB) at the default `--gpu-memory-utilization`; adaptive verification bounds that allocation and completes all requests.

### Known issue: BF16, TP=8, adaptive, concurrency ≥ 380

The adaptive BF16 server aborts with `HW Exception by GPU node-N ... reason: GPU Hang` under sustained load at concurrency 380–420 (reproduced twice; fixed verification is stable at the same load, MXFP4 TP=2 and MXFP8 TP=4 adaptive are stable through concurrency 500). The ragged MiniMax kernels pass the stress test above. Most likely root cause fix in #56831 - this is well-known issue at this point. Need to run TP=8 test with this PR applied).

## Earlier results (before rebase)

MXFP4 target with the `olka-fi/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4-DSpark` drafter, TP=2, same Sonnet workload, 3–5 minute steady-state runs; 9,040 requests, none failed.

| Concurrency | Fixed tok/s | Adaptive tok/s | Gain | Fixed median TPOT | Adaptive median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 299.82 | 330.13 | +10.1% | 381.78 ms | 342.55 ms |
| 256 | 413.86 | 479.84 | +15.9% | 500.45 ms | 406.09 ms |
| 320 | 471.08 | 573.31 | +21.7% | 570.16 ms | 446.81 ms |
| 380 | 488.89 | 603.86 | +23.5% | 615.22 ms | 478.64 ms |
| 420 | 528.18 | 658.30 | +24.6% | 645.89 ms | 489.64 ms |
| 500 | 568.84 | 731.51 | +28.6% | 667.91 ms | 521.15 ms |

items.title: [Spec Decode] Expose adaptive verified draft token count
items.body:
## Purpose

Expose the actual draft-token verification budget when adaptive verification is enabled. The existing draft counter counts proposals, which may be longer than the prefix sent to the target verifier.

This PR adds:

- `vllm:spec_decode_num_verified_draft_tokens_total` and the verified count in server logs.
- `vllm:spec_decode_num_verified_draft_tokens_per_pos_total{position="..."}`, with zero-based positions. A verified prefix of length 3 increments positions 0, 1, and 2; the sum across positions equals the scalar verified count.
- Documentation and unit tests for verified-token accounting.

Both verified counters are exposed only with adaptive verification enabled. They exclude bonus tokens and use the same request filtering as proposal accounting, including excluding results for already-finished requests. With async scheduling and structured outputs, grammar-invalid positions can still be physically verified, so verified counts can exceed grammar-adjusted proposal counts.

MRV2 reports per-request verified lengths through the async output-copy path. The per-position extension reuses the same CPU integers as the scalar counter, adding no further GPU kernel, D2H copy, or synchronization. It adds up to K CPU list increments per observed request, a K-entry stats vector, and K counter updates per observed batch. Overhead has not been benchmarked.

This extends the existing verified-token accounting in this PR. Related #54748 records the scheduler-selected K, including no-draft steps; it measures a different stage from the verifier's actual admitted prefix.

## Validation

CPU-only tests ran from this PR's full Python source on Linux/Python 3.12.3 with PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 and native artifacts reused from the existing vLLM 0.32.1rc1.dev183+g7e3d55956 environment. No GPU serving or model evaluation was run for the appended CPU counter change.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py -v
```

```text
============================== 21 passed in 2.41s ==============================
```

Using a local Hugging Face cache containing OPT-125M config/tokenizer files:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  HF_HUB_CACHE=/opt/pr58340_per_position_20261022/hf-cache OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
    -k "spec_decoding_stats or adaptive_verification_stats_count_actual_budget" -v
```

```text
====================== 11 passed, 196 deselected in 4.34s ======================
```

Coverage includes different prefix distributions with the same verified total, zero/missing verified counts, AV-disabled metric gating, stats serialization, grammar-invalid positions, and finished-request filtering. The new position assertions fail on the preceding commit because the per-position verified field is absent.

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/spec_decode/metrics.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  docs/features/speculative_decoding/acceptance_metrics.md
```

All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, Markdown lint, test tethering, and mypy for Python 3.10. The commit hooks also passed.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Cap varlen decode graph requests at the draft pass capacity
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #62939. With DSpark adaptive verification, startup crashes when `max_num_seqs * num_query_per_req` exceeds `max_num_batched_tokens`. The issue's command (Qwen3-8B, `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`) on main:

```
Assertion `index out of bounds: 0 <= tl.broadcast_to(tmp29, [XBLOCK, R0_BLOCK]) < 40960` failed.
...
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 1133, in capture_model
    self._dummy_run(**batch)
...
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

`_dummy_run` caps requests at `max_num_batched_tokens // num_query_per_req` so the draft pass fits its buffers (#56448). But adaptive verification's startup profiling replays varlen decode graphs padded to `max_num_seqs` requests, and the drafter drafts for every padded slot: 256 * 7 query rows against 512-row buffers (#58984 clamps this only for DP > 1). This PR pads those graphs only up to the same cap, which the scheduler already enforces (#59468); configs where the cap does not bind are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #62939; #53970 takes a different route, growing the drafter buffers and the default budget.

## Validation

1x A100-80GB, base 6ee316eaea, Qwen3-8B + `dspark_qwen3_8b_block7`, `TRITON_ATTN`:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| the issue's `vllm serve` command | device-side assert at startup | starts, answers a chat request |
| 96 greedy chat requests at 512 | - | all complete, acceptance length 3.73 |
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 1792` (cap does not bind) | 51 varlen decode graphs | identical |

```
$ pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py::test_dspark_adaptive_verification_with_small_token_budget
main:    1 failed (Engine core initialization failed, same assert)
this PR: 1 passed
$ pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py \
    tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
65 passed
```

The new CPU test fails if either the request cap or its matching token bound is reverted. The e2e test runs in the nightly `Spec Decode AL DSpark` job and is skipped on ROCm, where it is untested.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Profile adaptive verification tail on a schedulable batch shape
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54046.

`AdaptiveVerificationManager.batches_to_profile` seeds the cost tables from dummy runs at every captured size plus a doubling tail up to `max_num_batched_tokens`. The tail sizes are handed to `_dummy_run` as a bare token count, which splits them evenly over `min(num_tokens, max_num_seqs)` requests, and `InputBatch.make_dummy` splits evenly again.

With `max_num_seqs=128` and `num_speculative_tokens=7` that times the 16384-token tail as **128 requests of 128 queries each**, all carrying `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN` of context. A fully occupied decode step is `128 * (1 + 7) = 1024` tokens, so every tail sample above 1024 measures a shape the scheduler cannot produce -- and those samples are exactly what `set_initial_cost_curves` fits the verify curve to and extrapolates beyond.

The fix shapes the tail as the mixed step it has to be:

- The surplus over the decode ceiling can only be prefill, so it is cut into chunks sized by `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN` (already the profiler's stand-in for a sequence length).
- The prefill slots come out of the request budget; the remaining slots stay decode requests of exactly `1 + num_speculative_tokens` queries, and their freed tokens go back to the chunks.
- The split is threaded through `_dummy_run` -> `execute_model` -> `InputBatch.make_dummy`.

For the example in the issue (`max_num_batched_tokens=16384, ctx=8192, max_num_seqs=128, k=7`) the profiled 16384-token step becomes 126 decode requests of 8 queries plus 2 prefill chunks of 7688, instead of 128 x 128.

Scope is deliberately narrow:

- **Captured sizes keep the even split.** Those runs have to match the descriptor their graph was captured with.
- **`make_dummy` only honours an explicit split when cudagraph dispatch did not pad or reshape the batch**; otherwise the shape belongs to the descriptor and the even split is used, exactly as today. `_dummy_run`'s even split and `make_dummy`'s are identical, so passing the caller's split through is a no-op for every existing dummy-run caller.
- `get_uniform_decode_token_count` already returns `None` for a non-uniform batch, so a mixed profiling batch cannot be dispatched into a uniform decode graph.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "54046 in:body"` -- no results.
- Searched open PRs for `adaptive verification profile` and for `batches_to_profile`. The only nearby open PR is #52233, which caches the calibrated curves across boots; it does not change which shapes get profiled, so the two are orthogonal (they touch the same two files and may need a trivial rebase).

## Test Plan

```bash
# New + existing unit coverage for the profiled shapes
python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -q

# Regression over the dummy-run / cudagraph paths this threads a split through
python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py -q
```

Plus an on-GPU probe that drives a mixed decode/prefill dummy batch through the V2 runner (`facebook/opt-125m`, `max_num_seqs=8`, `enforce_eager`), recording what `InputBatch.make_dummy` actually built.

## Test Result

Hardware: NVIDIA RTX A6000, Ubuntu, CUDA 13.

**Unit / regression:** `55 passed` across the six files above, including the three new tests.

The new tests are discriminating: reverting only the `batches_to_profile` wiring (leaving the tests untouched) fails
`test_profiled_tail_batches_are_shapes_the_scheduler_can_produce` with `assert None is not None`.

**On-GPU shape probe** (identical `num_tokens`, only the split differs):

| dummy run | what `make_dummy` built |
| --- | --- |
| today's even split | `num_reqs=8, num_tokens=256, split=[32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32]` |
| explicit mixed split | `num_reqs=8, num_tokens=256, split=[2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 122, 122]` |

The mixed batch forwards without error and ordinary generation is unaffected afterwards
(`llm.generate("The capital of France is")` -> `' on par-and-par with Venezuela'`).

**Model evaluation:** not applicable -- this changes only the batch shapes timed during startup calibration. It does not touch sampling, the verification kernels, or any token the model emits; the generation check above confirms the serving path is unchanged. The behavioural effect is on the seeded verify cost curve, and hence on the draft budgets adaptive verification chooses.

`tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_mode.py` has 14 failures on this machine, but they reproduce identically on unmodified `main` (verified by swapping the four changed files back and re-running), so they are environmental and unrelated.

Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0, the pinned pre-commit revision) clean on all four files.

`mypy` over the three changed source files reports 6 errors, all of which reproduce on unmodified `main` (7 there); the one that disappears is `input_batch.py: Need type annotation for "num_scheduled_tokens"`, now that the parameter carries an explicit annotation. No new type errors.

---

AI assistance was used in preparing this change. Every line was reviewed and the tests above were run and inspected by me.

items.title: [WIP][Spec Decode] Drafter early exit in a CUDA graph WHILE node
items.body:
Autoregressive drafters (MTP, EAGLE) can stop drafting on the GPU without a host sync, so async scheduling is preserved. With VLLM_DYN_DRAFT set, the captured FULL decode graph runs draft steps 1..k-1 inside one CUDA graph WHILE node; a Triton kernel decides after each step whether the batch's expected gain from the next draft position (from the acceptance estimator's confidences) clears a threshold that adaptive verification derives from its cost model each step ("cost"), or never stops ("full").

Adaptive verification still admits as many drafts as the CPU budgeted, since the CPU-built batch layout depends on it; admitted drafts at positions the drafter skipped are verified as placeholders through the invalid-draft path, so outputs are unchanged, and the acceptance estimator is graded only on drafted positions.

The loop body's TP collectives run on a split pynccl communicator with graphUsageMode=1, since NCCL's default graph mixing adds event nodes that a conditional body may not hold, and the body syncs vLLM's cached current stream with the capture stream.

items.title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Add speculator hooks for non-chain verification and draft suspension
items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds five optional hooks to Model Runner V2's `BaseSpeculator`, so a speculator can verify drafts that are not a chain (a tree, for example), choose how many drafts each request verifies, and stop drafting when speculation stops paying off at large batch sizes. Each hook defaults to today's behavior, and the runner calls a per-step hook only when the speculator overrides it, so built-in speculators run as before.

Model Runner V2 verifies drafts as a chain, and only built-in adaptive verification can change how many drafts a step verifies. A tree verifier needs to rewrite positions and attention inputs before the target forward, supply its own rejection sampler, and move the accepted path's KV and recurrent state afterwards. A speculator that finds drafting no longer helps needs a way back to plain decode. The hooks sit at points where the runner already branches.

Builds on #62962; review the last 4 commits. Together the two let an out-of-tree speculator run tree verification on hybrid models.

## Claims

- `make_rejection_sampler(sampler)` lets the speculator supply the verifier. The default keeps the chain `RejectionSampler`, and `ModelState.custom_sampler` still takes precedence.
- `prepare_verify_inputs(input_batch, model_inputs, *, dummy_run)` runs before the target forward (in capture and dummy runs too), after positions, slot mappings and attention metadata exist. A tree verifier rewrites positions in place and stages what its attention backend reads.
- `post_accept(input_batch, sampler_output, num_sampled, num_rejected)` runs after sampling, before `num_computed_tokens` advances and before `propose`. A tree verifier moves the accepted path's KV and recurrent state to the slots the next step expects.
- `verify_budget(req_ids, num_draft_tokens)` returns how many of its scheduled drafts each request verifies this step, and the rest count as rejected. The runner trims the batch on the host before dispatch, so the token count and decode width that select the CUDA graph follow the budget. Built-in adaptive verification keeps precedence when enabled.
- `suspend_drafting(num_reqs, req_ids)` is asked once per scheduled batch when the speculator sets `may_suspend_drafting`. When it returns True, pending verification drains and the batch's requests decode with the target alone until they finish, on target-only attention metadata and decode CUDA graphs, without draft KV. A zero draft count behaves differently, because it still extends the draft KV.

## Validation

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed below.

All GPU rows ran Qwen3.8-27B at TP4 on 4x B300 with Model Runner V2 and greedy sampling. The MTP row ran this PR's code with #62962 underneath on `main` at `3dbf2b6c0c`. The other rows were measured on the previous base (`56e67b46a3`) with #62962 and #62961 underneath, on an earlier revision with the same hook bodies, whose runner called every hook on every step. The speculator rows served 88 SPEED-Bench first turns with up to 512 new tokens, one fresh server and one run per row, and their throughput is generated (output) tokens per second over the wall-clock time of the run.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| MTP (built-in, so no hook is called), 33 prompts at batch 1, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | Greedy outputs identical to the same build without this PR and #62962 (33 of 33), no sync errors, and the same mean acceptance length as without them |
| Out-of-tree tree speculator (custom sampler, verify-input and accepted-path hooks, `verify_budget`), 8 and 64 concurrent requests, measured on the previous base (`56e67b46a3`) | 3026 and 8391 output tok/s, against 1672 and 7378 without speculation |
| Chain speculator whose `suspend_drafting` stops drafting from 36 requests, 64 concurrent, measured on the previous base (`56e67b46a3`) | 63 drafts in 92,903 generated tokens, so the batch decoded with the target alone |
| Suspended decode, 8 and 64 requests of 128 tokens, full graph and eager, measured on the previous base (`56e67b46a3`) | Outputs identical to no speculation with no draft calls, at 0.92x the throughput of plain decode at 8 requests and 0.86x at 64 (full graph) |

The new tests check that the runner builds the chain sampler unless the speculator supplies one and calls only the hooks a speculator overrides (none for built-ins). They check that `verify_budget` trims the batch before dispatch, keeps prefill rows, and is not asked without drafts or with adaptive verification. They check that suspension sticks to each request, drains pending verification, uses its own metadata and graphs, calls no draft or verify hook, and rejects unsupported configurations. The changed runner tests cover KV-sharing layers in the target layer set, graph teardown for suspended decode, and its metadata without speculative state.

On CPU on this base (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, one pytest process per file), with #62962 underneath, the touched files and the attention, KV-cache and worker files they depend on pass 800 tests against 731 on `main` (`3dbf2b6c0c`), with no new failures. The 15 failures are the same on both trees, 7 in `test_gpu_model_runner.py` and 8 CPU-builder cases in `test_group_head_counts.py`. On B300 on `40210d8317`, the same files passed 599 tests with no failures, including all 31 in `test_gpu_speculator_verify_hooks.py`. `pre-commit` (mypy included) passes on this range.

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref bc393e71536fc9718743c653d4e396707fe924f3 --to-ref HEAD
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_speculator_verify_hooks.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

## Not a duplicate

I ran the duplicate-work searches from `AGENTS.md` §1 (open PRs, with keywords for custom rejection samplers, tree verification hooks, verify budgets and suspending drafting). No open PR adds these Model Runner V2 hooks. These are related, and this PR uses no code from them:

- #53426 skips the draft forward at zero draft tokens for MTP and DFlash, as an operator opt-in. `suspend_drafting` is a decision the speculator makes per batch, and it also stops draft KV extension.
- #58340 reports the number of drafts verified under adaptive verification. The same metric would apply to `verify_budget`.
- #62682 adds approximate verification as a built-in rejection-sampling method. `make_rejection_sampler` lets an out-of-tree speculator supply its own sampler, and the two work side by side.

## Details

- The sampler contract is `RejectionSampler.__call__`'s (`sampled_token_ids`, `num_sampled`, `num_rejected`, and logprob rows in sampled-token order).
- The runner detects overrides once, when it builds the speculator, by comparing each hook on the speculator's class with `BaseSpeculator`'s.
- `suspend_drafting` and `verify_budget` take and return host data only (request ids and counts) and must not read device tensors.
- Suspended decode runs with synchronous scheduling and either eager execution or full decode graphs. When a speculator opts in, the runner rejects prefix caching, KV transfer, DBO, context, data or pipeline parallelism, and recurrent replay or recovery. Draft weights and KV capacity stay allocated.
- Non-chain verification with pipeline parallelism is outside this PR.
- Size: +396 / -48 non-test lines, 695 test lines and 19 docs lines.

items.title: [Spec Decode] Verify in head dtype and drop the FP32 chunk workaround
items.body:
## Purpose

Speculative decoding expands each request into multiple verification positions. Whenever
any active logits processor is present, the target rejection verifier currently
materializes an FP32 processing canvas of shape `[num_verification_tokens, vocab_size]`.
The production path bounds the transient allocation with a 1 GiB chunk, which in turn
forces a cap on the total logits adaptive verification may schedule per step.

This PR makes the target verifier explicitly opt into storing and processing logits in
the LM head dtype (BF16/FP16), and deletes the FP32 canvas, the chunk iterator, and the
adaptive cap:

- temperature is applied in FP32 when the rejection kernels, top-k/top-p, and the
  processed-logprob scorer load the logits; it is never written back to the stored
  logits;
- top-k/top-p computes its boundary in FP32 and writes back only the mask; penalties are
  computed in FP32 and written back to the head dtype with a single rounding; exact mask
  processors keep their original semantics;
- raw reporting keeps an original head-dtype snapshot only when a processor would
  overwrite the input; processed reporting reads the processed stored logits;
- the adaptive cost tables, selection formula, grammar mapping, and zero-budget contract
  are unchanged; only the hard cap that existed to serve the FP32 chunk is removed;
- the PyTorch top-p fallback's softmax and cumulative sum are pinned to FP32, since
  head-dtype target logits make the previously latent BF16 accumulation path reachable;
- speculative decoding fails closed on any nonzero `min_p`, and custom
  `logprob_token_ids` reporting is wired up.

The regular sampler, non-speculative decoding, and zero-draft steps keep the existing
FP32 processing path.

<details>
<summary>Supported sampling processors and reporting behavior</summary>

All supported processors below avoid materializing a full-vocabulary FP32 verifier canvas. This
PR does not change which processors are supported by speculative decoding.

| Sampling parameter / processor | Property | Supported in Spec Decode | Effect on stored logits | Head-dtype precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| temperature | Distribution scaling | Yes (unchanged) | None; consumers scale on load | Computed in FP32 |
| top_k / top_p | Selection mask | Yes (unchanged) | Preserve kept values; mask others with `-inf` | Exact |
| repetition / frequency / presence penalties | Value transformation | Yes (unchanged) | Rewrite affected values | One BF16/FP16 rounding |
| allowed_token_ids / min_tokens / bad_words | Hard token mask | Yes (unchanged) | Write `-inf` masks | Exact |
| thinking_token_budget | Forced-token override | Yes (unchanged) | Write a dtype-safe sentinel | Semantically exact |
| structured-output grammar mask | Hard token mask applied before verification | Yes (unchanged) | Write `-inf` masks | Exact |
| min_p | Probability filter | No (unchanged) | — | Any nonzero value fails validation |
| logit_bias | Additive value transformation | No (unchanged) | — | One BF16/FP16 rounding |

Raw and processed logprobs are reporting modes rather than logits processors. Raw reporting reads
a pre-processor head-dtype snapshot when stored logits may be modified. Processed reporting reads
the processed stored logits and applies temperature in FP32 on load. Adaptive-verification output
logprobs were enabled upstream by #52242 (merged 2026-08-25); this PR is rebased on top of it and
preserves its device-tensor boundary reporting through the head-dtype scorer.

</details>

Penalties are the only path that writes back to the stored logits lossily: the processor
still computes in FP32, but the result is rounded to BF16/FP16 once. Please pay
particular attention to the penalty-only, stochastic, and `top_k=1` results under
**Numerical fidelity and model quality** below. We did not find an implementation that
preserves FP32-equivalent penalty output without either reintroducing full-vocabulary
FP32 storage or adding significant extra scans/latency; this PR therefore keeps this
numerical trade-off explicit rather than claiming processed penalty logprobs are bitwise
FP32.

### Why this is not a repeat of #48641

#48641 removed the same FP32 copy and was reverted in full three days later by #49033
over a never-root-caused DP+EP+MTP hang. Beyond removing the copy, #48641 also changed
the numerics: it applied temperature by **writing the scaled values back into the
stored head-dtype logits**, for the regular sampler and the speculative verifier
alike. Every such write-back costs an extra BF16/FP16 rounding, and every downstream
consumer — rejection statistics, top-k/top-p, logprob reporting — then reads the
already-rounded, temperature-scaled values. Whether or not that contributed to the
hang, it is a real precision hazard, and this PR is built specifically to remove it:

- stored logits always keep their pre-temperature values; temperature is applied in
  FP32 registers at every load site and never touches storage;
- top-k/top-p computes its boundary in FP32 and writes back only `-inf` masks — kept
  logits are bit-identical to what the LM head produced;
- the only remaining lossy write-back is penalties, which is quantified and
  guardrailed under **Numerical fidelity and model quality** below;
- the scope is the speculative verifier only; the regular sampler keeps its FP32 path.

On the risk side, a permanent e2e test covers both #49033's pure-greedy control path
and an active path that actually enters the head-dtype verifier, in the same
distributed engine. That test guards the risk quadrant; it does not claim to reproduce
or explain the root cause of the original hang.

### Related work

- **#53090** (open) fuses only a temperature-only fast path; other processors or
  processed logprobs still fall back to the FP32 canvas, so it cannot delete the
  chunking or the adaptive cap. This PR covers every currently legal
  processor/reporting combination.
- **#50910** (merged) already adopted the "store in head dtype, upcast to FP32 and
  divide by temperature on load" contract on the draft side; this PR aligns the target
  verifier to the same contract.
- **#47808**'s `max_total_logits` cap exists only to guarantee the FP32 verifier lands
  in a single safe chunk; this PR removes that premise and does not change the adaptive
  verification algorithm.
- **#40704** is porting n-gram drafting to Model Runner V2; until it lands, n-gram
  still falls back to Model Runner V1, so the custom `logprob_token_ids` e2e request
  temporarily covers Eagle only.
- **#52242** (merged 2026-08-25, while this PR was in flight) lifted the
  adaptive-verification output-logprobs restriction. This PR is rebased on top of it:
  the device-side `cu_num_generated_tokens` boundaries it introduced are kept and flow
  through the head-dtype scorer unchanged, and removing the chunked path also removes
  the stale-layout hazard its `_verify_in_chunks` assert defended against. If
  **#52477** lands first, the grammar-mapping tests will need a rebase update.
- One acceptance criterion of **RFC #42259** is that the MRV2 path should not
  materialize avoidable full-vocabulary temporaries; the FP32 canvas this PR deletes is
  exactly such a temporary.

## Test Plan

1. Run the focused CUDA test matrix for sampling-parameter validation, sampler state,
   thinking budget, top-k/top-p, rejection sampling, adaptive verification, and the
   logprob numerical oracles and head-dtype penalty path.
2. Run the complete `test_spec_decode_logprobs` matrix across 3 speculative model setups and all
   4 `LogprobsMode` values, comparing emitted tokens and raw/processed logprob outputs with the
   non-speculative reference.
3. Run the DP2+EP+MTP regression twice. In the same distributed engine, exercise both the
   pure-greedy #49033 control signature and an active-sampling request that enters the head-dtype
   verifier; require each wave to draft and match the non-speculative output.
4. Benchmark `RejectionSampler.__call__` with BF16 logits, `K=7`, `V=129280`, and
   `R={8,256,512}` across temperature, top-p, penalties, combined processors, and logprob
   reporting. Compare p50 latency and per-call CUDA peak allocation with the FP32-canvas control.
5. Run a paired 1319-question, 5-shot GSM8K A/B evaluation covering the default path,
   penalties-only, stochastic top-p with penalties, and `top_k=1`; compare accuracy, invalid
   outputs, and acceptance length.

<details>
<summary>Repository test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/test_sampling_params.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py \
  tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_token_logprobs_apply_virtual_temperature
```

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -vv -s \
  tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_spec_decode_logprobs
```

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -vv -s \
  'tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_mtp_parallel_load.py::test_deepseek_mtp_load_dp[dp2]'
```

</details>

## Test Result

### Correctness and path coverage

- The targeted GPU suite passed with `231 passed, 2 skipped` (reported from the run; that console
  log was not kept). It covers every supported sampling processor, raw/processed reporting,
  adaptive verification, thinking budget and the head-dtype penalty path.
- The full public-model `test_spec_decode_logprobs` matrix passed all 3 model setups × 4
  `LogprobsMode` combinations (`12 passed`). Spec and non-spec runs returned identical emitted
  token IDs, logprob token IDs and ranks. Raw scores were bitwise equal; the largest processed-score
  difference was `0.08334`.
- The DP2+EP+MTP surrogate passed twice consecutively with a minimum spec/non-spec token match ratio
  of `1.000`. Both the pure-greedy wave matching the #49033 incident signature and the active
  sampling wave produced draft tokens, so the test covers both the control path and the new
  head-dtype verifier in the same distributed engine.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed for all 19 changed Python files.

These results verify that the optimization is reached in production paths while preserving token
selection and logprob reporting contracts; they do not rely only on isolated kernel tests.

### Verifier memory and latency

The benchmark uses BF16 logits with `K=7`, `V=129280` and `R=512` (4096 verification rows), which
crosses the old approximately 2076-row chunk boundary. The control is the same candidate with the
head-dtype verifier disabled, so the comparison isolates this PR's verifier mode while keeping the
PyTorch top-p correctness fix on both sides.

| Processor | FP32 canvas p50 (ms) | Head dtype p50 (ms) | Per-call peak allocated |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| temperature | 5.054–5.103 | 0.979–1.093 | 1023.20 → 2.33 MiB |
| top-p | 31.178–31.219 | 25.846–26.057 | 1023.20 → 2.33 MiB |
| penalties | 11.960–12.025 | 5.316–8.148 | 1023.20 → 2.33 MiB |
| penalties + top-p | 39.058–39.361 | 30.424–34.095 | 1023.20 → 2.33 MiB |

The measured processor cases reduce the per-call allocation from 1023.20 MiB to 2.33 MiB and
improve p50 latency in every case; temperature-only is approximately five times faster. Processed
logprob reporting similarly falls from 1032.44 MiB to 20.68 MiB. This demonstrates that the FP32
canvas is removed rather than moved behind a different chunk boundary.

Raw reporting with a mutating processor is the intentional exception: preserving pre-processor
values still requires an approximately 1010 MiB BF16 snapshot, for a total around 1030.66 MiB. The
claim is therefore the removal of the verifier FP32 canvas and its local memory/latency cost, not a
general end-to-end throughput improvement.

### Numerical fidelity and model quality

Mask-only processors remain exact because kept logits are never rewritten. Temperature and top-p
processed scores have maximum finite errors of `1.91e-6` and `2.13e-4` against the FP32-input
reference, with no rank differences. Raw-reporting digests are bitwise identical between base and
head-dtype runs.

Penalties are the only lossy stored-processor path. Their FP32 calculation is rounded once on
writeback to BF16/FP16; the penalty + top-p oracle measures a maximum finite score error of
`0.0203`. We therefore evaluated all penalty-enabled combinations on the full 1319-question,
5-shot GSM8K set, in addition to the default control:

| Case | Sampling | Base | Head dtype(PR)   | Accuracy Δ | Acceptance length (base/head) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| standard | greedy; neutral penalties(off)  | 82.942% | 82.942% | 0.000 pp | 4.2015 / 4.1509 |
| penalties-only | greedy; penalties on | 82.259% | 81.577% | −0.682 pp | 4.0394 / 4.0341 |
| stochastic | `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9`; penalties on | 79.075% | 79.606% | +0.531 pp | 3.9586 / 3.9658 |
| `top_k=1` | `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9`; penalties on | 82.259% | 81.653% | −0.607 pp | 3.9686 / 3.9878 |

The standard control produced identical output token sequences and correctness for all 1319
questions. Invalid counts were unchanged in every paired run. The three penalty-enabled,
fixed-seed accuracy deltas stay within ±0.682 percentage points, while their acceptance lengths
remain close to base. These are quality guardrails rather than a claim of statistical equivalence;
together with the FP32 oracle they bound the observed effect of the intentional head-dtype penalty
writeback.

## Duplicate check

Checked RFC #42259 and open PRs by issue number and relevant area keywords on 2026-08-24, and
re-checked on 2026-08-25. The only directly overlapping open PR is #53090; the scope difference is
described above.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for implementation, test design, GPU experiment orchestration and drafting
this description. The human submitter reviewed lines, resolved rebase conflicts and
ran the tests above, and can explain and defend the change end to end.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

items.title: [Spec Decode] Replace torch.compile'd AV draft-budget selection with a Triton kernel
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Replace adaptive verification's `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` draft-budget selection with a single-launch Triton kernel, JIT'd once in `warmup_kernels`. This removes the mid-serving compile stalls and cuts the host cost of every budget-binding step about 6x.

Related: #62539 fixes the same stall by pre-compiling the Dynamo specializations at startup. This PR instead removes the compile, which also removes the launch overhead it never paid for (details below). Credit to #62539 for the root cause and for spotting the `max_num_reqs` duck-sizing specialization.

## Claims

- No budget-kernel compiles during serving: one Triton JIT at warmup (0.45 s warm cache, 1.0 s cold) instead of 4–5 Dynamo graphs compiled on the first trimmed steps (1.8–4.7 s per process).
- Host time per budget-binding step drops from 76–90 µs (compiled) to ~15 µs. GPU time drops from 85–100 µs to 22–30 µs at typical batch sizes.
- Qwen3-4B + DSpark, GSM8K, concurrency 16 (H200): adaptive verification goes from 4,783 to 6,803 output tok/s (median), on par with #62539 (6,756; within run-to-run noise). Accuracy unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py` gives 24 passed on H200. The new GPU tests check the kernel against a torch global top-k reference: K ∈ {3, 8}, {1, 2, 300} requests (300 crosses a block boundary), budgets from 1 to total − 1. A ties test checks that exactly `draft_budget` drafts are admitted. They run in the existing `V1 Spec Decode` (H200 MIG) job. `pre-commit run` passes, including mypy.

**End to end, Qwen3-4B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7`.** Setup: 7 speculative tokens, probabilistic drafts, GSM8K 1-shot, 128 prompts, concurrency 16, 1×H200. All arms use the same build at `d561af5df`, run in alternation. Compiles are counted the same way as #62539: `TORCH_LOGS=dynamo` `start tracing _assign_draft_token_budget` lines during generation.

| Arm | Runs | Output tok/s, median (range) | Compiles during generation | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed verification | 3 | 6,507 (6,117–6,837) | – | 0.81–0.82 |
| Adaptive, main | 3 | 4,783 (3,072–5,541) | 2–3 | 0.83–0.84 |
| Adaptive, #62539 | 3 | 6,756 (6,735–6,785) | 0 | 0.83–0.84 |
| Adaptive, this PR | 3 | 6,803 (6,594–6,864) | 0 | 0.83–0.84 |

The script is the one from #62539, without `attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN"`. A separate run of this PR with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed with no errors (6,910 tok/s, accuracy 0.836).

**End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark.** Setup: TP4 + EP, H200, random 8K-token prompts. The metric is the warmup bench's worst TTFT (16 requests, concurrency 4, issued right after startup):

| | main | this PR | no adaptive verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| K=3 | 2,424 ms | 866 ms | 824 ms |
| K=8 | 1,815 ms | 789 ms | – |

Steady-state TTFT, TPOT, KV capacity and CUDA-graph memory are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Kernel microbenchmark (H200, median µs per call, host / GPU)</summary>

Host time is wall time across the Python call with no sync. GPU time is CUDA events around the call. `idx_mapping` is int64, as in `prepare_inputs`.

| num_reqs | budget | eager | torch.compile | Triton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 93 / 102 | 79 / 88 | 15 / 22 |
| 16 | 20 | 98 / 106 | 88 / 97 | 15 / 23 |
| 64 | 64 | 91 / 99 | 84 / 93 | 15 / 23 |
| 256 | 300 | 91 / 100 | 84 / 93 | 15 / 24 |
| 1024 | 2000 | 90 / 104 | 85 / 99 | 15 / 37 |

(K=3. K=5 and K=8 are similar, except Triton GPU time at 1,024 requests rises to 49 µs and 67 µs.)

First-call cost of the compiled version: 3.0 s cold (1.4 s with a warm Inductor cache), plus 0.45–0.64 s (0.11–0.16 s warm) for each of the `num_reqs == 1` / `draft_budget == 1` specializations. The Triton kernel compiles once, and later shapes, including 1 request with budget 1, run in under 0.1 ms.

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause.** `warmup_kernels` runs with adaptive verification off, and cost profiling never trims, so the compiled budget function first ran on a live trimmed step. It then recompiled for each 0/1 specialization (and for `num_reqs == max_num_reqs`, per #62539).
- **Why not keep the compile.** The op is about six tiny kernels and is bound by host launch overhead. Compiled it saves only ~0–20 µs over eager, and it still costs ~80 µs of host time on every binding step. It runs eagerly in `prepare_inputs`, outside any CUDA graph, so that cost lands on the step's host critical path whenever the host is the bottleneck.
- **Kernel.** A single program does three passes:
  1. Survival prefix products, stored as float bits. Values are non-negative, so int order matches float order; ineligible slots store −1.
  2. A binary search on the bits for the `draft_budget`-th largest value.
  3. Per-request counts above the threshold, with ties handed out in request order.

  Survival is non-increasing along a request, so per-request counts fully describe the winners, as before. With distinct values the result is identical to the old top-k. On exact ties, top-k's choice was already unspecified.
- **Specialization.** `num_reqs` and `draft_budget` are `do_not_specialize`, so the one JIT in `warmup_budget_kernel()` covers every shape. The kernel needs a `max_num_reqs × K` int32 scratch buffer.
- **Tradeoffs.** The binary search takes 31 sequential passes over `num_reqs × K` slots, so GPU time grows with very large batches (67 µs at 1,024 requests and K=8). That's still below the old path, and negligible next to a step at that batch size. I couldn't test ROCm or XPU here, where adaptive verification is also used. The kernel uses only standard Triton ops (`bitcast`, `cumsum`, `debug_barrier`, a scalar `while`).

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Ignore Anthropic thinking budgets the server cannot enforce
items.body:
## Overview

Since #58613, `/v1/messages` maps `thinking={"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N}` to `thinking_token_budget`, which the engine rejects unless a reasoning parser with reasoning start/end tokens is configured. Every Anthropic request with extended thinking enabled therefore fails on servers without one: no `--reasoning-parser`, or a parser without those tokens such as `openai_gptoss`. This ignores `budget_tokens` in that case, as the endpoint already does for `display`, and logs a one-time warning.

## Claims

- `/v1/messages` with `thinking.type="enabled"` succeeds on servers that cannot enforce a thinking budget, as it did before #58613.
- Servers that can enforce it (a reasoning parser with start/end tokens) still apply `budget_tokens`.
- No change for `disabled`, `adaptive` or absent `thinking`.

## Validation

Real server on `34ac4f96a3` (Qwen3-0.6B, RTX 4090, `--enforce-eager`). Request: `{"max_tokens": 2048, "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 1024}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi."}]}`.

| Server | Build | Non-streaming | Streaming |
|---|---|---|---|
| no `--reasoning-parser` | `main` | HTTP 400: `thinking_token_budget is set but reasoning_config is not configured...` | only an `error` event |
| no `--reasoning-parser` | this PR | HTTP 200, `end_turn` | full event sequence |
| `--reasoning-parser qwen3` | this PR | HTTP 200, `end_turn` (budget applied) | full event sequence |

Tests:

- New `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py::TestThinkingConfig::test_enabled_ignores_budget_the_server_cannot_enforce`.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`: 113 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

## Details

`AnthropicServingMessages._handle_thinking` set `req.thinking_token_budget = thinking.budget_tokens` unconditionally, and `InputProcessor._validate_params` raises `VLLMValidationError` when `thinking_token_budget` is set and `reasoning_config` is `None` or disabled. `reasoning_config` only exists with `--reasoning-parser`, and stays disabled for parsers without reasoning start/end strings (e.g. `openai_gptoss`, `granite`, `minimax_m2_append_think`). Because `budget_tokens` is required for `type: "enabled"`, Anthropic clients had no way to request extended thinking from such servers.

The handler now computes `_thinking_budget_supported` from `vllm_config.reasoning_config` once, and passes it to `to_chat_completion_request` for `/v1/messages` and `count_tokens`. The parameter defaults to `True`, so the scale-out render path and existing callers keep their behavior.

An alternative is to keep returning 400 with a clearer message (#57830 rewords the engine error). Ignoring matches how the endpoint treats other thinking settings it cannot honor and the behavior before #58613; happy to switch if maintainers prefer an error. This overlaps in area with RFC #58647.

Not a duplicate: I found no issue or PR for this 400 (searched "budget_tokens", "anthropic thinking enabled", "thinking_token_budget reasoning_config", "reasoning_config is not configured"). #61984 changes the render path's disabled-thinking effort, and #59180 is `count_tokens` parity.

AI assistance was used to find this bug, write the fix and the test, and run the validation shown above.

items.title: [Core] Add defer mode for long prefills
items.body:
## Purpose

Adds `--long-prefill-token-threshold-defer`, off by default. Instead of capping each long prefill at `long_prefill_token_threshold`, long prefills take turns:
- one long prefill per step;
- it runs after the waiting requests, with the leftover budget, if that is at least the threshold;
- one that sat out its turn runs first the next step.

**Why:** with context parallelism, each step costs a fixed amount, plus an amount for each request in it that grows with its context. On H200 (GLM-5.3, PCP8×DCP8, 8192 tokens per step) that is about 230 ms fixed, plus about 335 ms for a request at 1M context. Splitting the budget pays these costs more often. Under load the adaptive threshold also splits short cached prompts, which cuts throughput just when the queue is longest.

## Results

Agent X ([Weka trace](https://huggingface.co/datasets/semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126)) with GLM-5.3 at 1M context on 16× H200: PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 decode. This commit on an earlier main, all arms in one run, 20 minutes per point. Adaptive = threshold 2048 + adaptive; defer = threshold 2048 + defer.

| concurrency | arm | requests | TTFT p50 | p95 | p99 |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | adaptive | 1186 | 1.3 s | 7.2 s | 105 s |
| 32 | no threshold | 1205 | 1.3 s | 7.7 s | 44 s |
| 32 | defer | 1176 | 1.4 s | 29.9 s | 66 s |
| 48 | adaptive | 464 | 1.7 s | 510 s | 559 s |
| 48 | no threshold | 762 | 2.6 s | 276 s | 326 s |
| 48 | **defer** | 744 | 3.7 s | **198 s** | **264 s** |

- **Under load (concurrency 48):** defer completes 60% more requests than adaptive, matches no threshold on throughput, and has the best tail.
- **Concurrency 32:** within run-to-run noise. A repeat of defer reached 1227 requests with p95 6.5 s, the best of all c32 runs. Variants that ran long prefills oldest-first or one at a time were worse (p95 32–35 s): medium prompts got stuck behind the largest one.
- **Noise:** the same arm varies by up to ±24% in requests between runs at concurrency 48.
- **Accuracy:** gsm8k is the same in all arms (0.728–0.740).

## Test plan

`pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k long_prefill`

items.title: [SpecDecode] Preserve reject-only residual verifier padding
items.body:
## Summary

- Keep the real one-token prompt tail through Mamba scheduling alignment, then restore the synthetic speculative width before allocation.
- Track reject-only synthetic drafts separately from GPU-safe placeholder token IDs and restore their `-1` sentinel only for rejection sampling.
- Skip uniform residual padding for adaptive DSpark, which already uses a variable verification budget and variable-length decode graphs.
- Select target-verifier FULL graphs only when every request carries the complete verifier draft layout, and describe dummy captures with the same topology.

## Motivation

#54012 enabled FlashInfer native-CP MLA verification, but the failures exposed here are backend-independent. When a new request with one remaining prompt token joins a running speculative-verification batch, vLLM pads it to `1 + num_speculative_tokens` so the target batch remains uniform.

Two independent correctness problems occur in that path. Applying Mamba alignment to the padded width can clip the synthetic verifier shape, and the GPU input path replaces negative placeholder IDs with embedding-safe values before rejection sampling, allowing synthetic drafts to be treated as real proposals. Adaptive DSpark should not enter this fixed-width padding path at all because it deliberately reallocates a variable draft budget.

Target-verifier FULL graphs also capture model-wide branch topology, not only tensor dimensions. A same-shaped short prefill must not select a verifier graph when it lacks the complete draft-token layout. Uniform dummy captures must carry equivalent verifier metadata so distributed and idle ranks select the same graph topology.

## Commit structure

1. Align residual verifier padding after Mamba splits.
2. Preserve synthetic draft rejection sentinels and exclude them from acceptance accounting.
3. Skip uniform padding for adaptive verification.
4. Select FULL graphs by verifier topology.

## Relationship to existing work

This is a follow-up to #54012, not an attention-backend change. #53694 avoids a redundant DP synchronization before draft prefill but does not distinguish target-verifier graphs from same-shaped short-prefill execution. I searched open vLLM PRs and issues for `pad_spec_decode`, residual verifier padding, invalid draft sentinels, verifier graph topology, and same-shaped short prefills and found no directly overlapping fix. #51508 addresses stale zero-accept recurrent-state rows rather than first-decode residual padding, rejection-sampler sentinel loss, or verifier graph selection.

## Tests

Passed locally:

- `uvx ruff check` on all changed Python files.
- `uvx ruff format --check` on all changed Python files.
- `uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python -m py_compile` on all changed Python files.
- `git diff --check`.

Focused pytest and model evaluation are pending because this local worktree does not contain the vLLM runtime/test dependencies. This PR is intentionally opened as a draft. Before marking it ready, I will run the focused scheduler, rejection-sampler, adaptive-verification, and CUDA-graph dispatch tests, then report a mixed-batch Kimi-K3 DCP/EAGLE acceptance and correctness evaluation.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to inspect the current upstream data flow, adapt the internal fixes to TP batch sharding and the post-#53694 DP-sync path, write the initial patches and regressions, and run static validation. The submitter will review every changed line and run the required runtime tests and model evaluation before requesting final review.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Reject prefill caps smaller than an intact item
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #62031.

Reject a nonzero long-prefill cap smaller than the configured maximum multimodal item when item chunking is disabled. This replaces an accepted configuration that can permanently stall contended requests with an actionable startup error.

## Claims

- Validate the cap alongside the existing maximum-item versus batch-budget check.
- Cover fixed and adaptive caps; retain disabled-cap, equal/larger-cap, chunkable-input, and disabled-modality behavior.
- Preserve the scheduler, hard budgets, whole-item guard, and fairness policy. Defaults remain unchanged.

## Validation

On macOS arm64, Python 3.11.2, PyTorch 2.14.1, Transformers 5.19.0:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' PYTHONPATH=. \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

**269 passed in 50.67 seconds** on publication commit `776389ac699bdc3761cf596dd7ae8e6236a6da35`, based on upstream `8a6c0449b36e7aba29c2a6b1720ca3c08cfafa32`, including nine new cases. Before/after regressions were also checked at base `642c18d64c4cb6db3ded8fbe1786718cd4005fcb`: four rejection cases fail on unchanged production code and five valid controls pass. The five-file target patch is byte-identical after rebasing. The default commit hooks, sign-off hook, and current-head hook rerun pass, including mypy, Markdown lint, and CI test tethering; git diff --check passes. Existing CPU CI covers the tests. After removing the temporary CPU inference dependency, all nine new cases also pass in isolation with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1; these flags avoid a DNS failure in the existing public-model configuration lookup.

At base `642c18d`, real CPU MRV1 inference was checked with a seeded local tiny LLaVA checkpoint, four image tokens, float32, and batch budget 128. Both image requests were queued while scheduling was paused, then resumed together to guarantee contention.

| Check | Baseline | Patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cap 2, two queued image requests | Startup accepted; generation stalls until the 30-second watchdog | Intended ValueError at startup, reporting cap 2 and item maximum 4 |
| Cap 0, same requests | Both complete | Both complete; identical output tokens |
| Cap 4, same requests | Both complete | Both complete; identical output tokens |

Each valid run produces eight greedy tokens per request. The initial unpaused baseline run completed because overlap was not guaranteed; it is not counted as a stall reproduction.

Both inference checkouts temporarily included the same CPU slot-mapping compatibility change from [open PR #61151](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61151), head 5e0ac9d76f4ddbfa8290f488cebca39645ff81a5. Its two native tests pass locally. Without that dependency, both versions fail in the same pre-existing CPU fallback. The dependency was removed after testing and is excluded from this PR.

GPU/MRV2, HTTP serving, and pretrained-model quality were not tested. No post-rebase inference rerun is claimed; the inference matrix is attributed to base `642c18d`.

## Details

The scheduler caps proposed prefill work before checking whole-image boundaries. If the cap is below an intact item, the boundary guard schedules zero tokens. With multiple eligible requests, the cap stays active and the same state repeats. The baseline remained stuck for 1,000 scheduling passes. Adaptive fair share can also stay below the item size.

The fix adds a 12-line check to compute_mm_encoder_budget, following its existing batch-budget validation. The error tells users to disable the cap with zero or raise it sufficiently. The optimization guide and field documentation explain that validation uses the configured maximum item size, even if a particular request is smaller or alone. Encoder-decoder configuration already resets the threshold to zero.

This matches the fail-fast approach proposed in the [review of #52412](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52412#pullrequestreview-5407246881), while preserving the merged boundary fixes in [#52412](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52412) and [#59721](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59721). The proposal itself has not received maintainer approval.

Tradeoff: conservative startup rejection. A low cap that would work for one request, small images, or light adaptive contention is rejected because later requests could make it unschedulable. Default cap zero and configurations allowing item chunking are unaffected. No performance or output-quality improvement is claimed.

Duplicate searches on October 16, 2026 found no matching open cap-validation fix. [#59030](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59030) changes waiting-queue requeueing. [#61733](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61733) validates whole prompts when chunked prefill is disabled after startup; this validates a multimodal item's per-request cap in configurations that still allow chunked text prefill.

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, tests, and preparation. Publication was authorized by the human submitter. The automated validation commands described above were run by Codex; no human-executed validation is claimed. The commit includes AI attribution and the submitter's DCO sign-off.
