items.title: [Core] FlowPrefill: adaptive sub-chunk preemption for v1 Scheduler
items.body:
## Purpose

Implements **FlowPrefill** - adaptive sub-chunk preemption for long prefill requests in vLLM v1 (Q2 2026 roadmap item: "avoid excessive preemption, prefill HoL blocking", #39749, now closed).

**Problem:** In vLLM's v1 scheduler, long prefill chunks monopolize GPU time for 50–200 ms, causing decode TPOT spikes when new decode requests arrive mid-prefill. There is no mechanism to yield GPU mid-chunk - the entire chunk must complete before decodes can be serviced.

**Solution:** `FlowPrefillMixin` integrates CUDA event checkpoints at sub-chunk granularity. A non-blocking `Event.query()` detects decode pressure (queue depth ≥ `preemption_decode_threshold`). When pressure is detected at a checkpoint boundary, the scheduler suspends the current prefill and resumes from that token position in the next scheduling cycle, preserving all allocated KV blocks and adding zero `.synchronize()` calls.

**Result — real server A/B** (Qwen3-1.7B, `vllm bench serve`, concurrency=4, random dataset; full methodology and the starvation bug this required fixing are below):

| Config | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| No FlowPrefill (plain scheduler) | 449.84ms | 417.72ms | 990.66ms |
| FlowPrefill, with `preemption_max_suspend_ms` bound | 411.73ms | 427.04ms | 778.79ms |

**FlowPrefill beats the plain scheduler on every TTFT metric** (mean -8.5%, P99 -21.4%) on this workload.

**Key design decisions:**

- **Zero-overhead when disabled:** `FlowPrefillMixin` activates only when `SchedulerConfig.preemption_granularity` is not `None`. Default `None` preserves 100% of existing behavior — no code path change.
- **MRO-safe mixin:** `class Scheduler(FlowPrefillMixin, SchedulerInterface)` - placed first in MRO so hooks can be cleanly overridden.
- **Pre-allocated event pool:** `CudaEventPool` pre-allocates 256 `torch.cuda.Event` instances at init time, avoiding per-scheduling-step allocation overhead.
- **Cooperative suspension:** `PrefillCheckpointState` tracks the suspension position and KV block count; the scheduler resumes by feeding tokens from `[checkpoint_pos : checkpoint_pos + granularity]` with existing KV cache intact.
- **Starvation bound (`preemption_max_suspend_ms`, default 50ms):** see "Bug found during benchmarking" below — without this, a suspended prefill can starve indefinitely under sustained decode load.

**Files changed:**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` | `PrefillCheckpointState`, `CudaEventPool`, `FlowPrefillMixin`; `Scheduler` wires hooks in `__init__` and `schedule()` |
| `vllm/config/scheduler.py` | `preemption_granularity: int \| None = None`, `preemption_decode_threshold: int = 1`, `preemption_max_suspend_ms: int = 50` fields |
| `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` | `--preemption-granularity` CLI argument |
| `tests/v1/core/test_flowprefill.py` | 21 unit tests (no GPU required) covering all code paths, including forced-resume-at-timeout and no-resume-before-timeout |

This PR does not duplicate any existing open PR - verified against the current vllm-project/vllm PR list.
Related: vLLM Q2 2026 roadmap, FlowPrefill paper (arXiv Feb 2026).

> **AI assistance disclosure:** This PR was co-authored with Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Claude Code). I have reviewed all changed lines end-to-end and can explain any part of the implementation.

## Bug found during benchmarking, and the fix

`preemption_decode_threshold` gated both suspend (`depth >= threshold`) and resume (`depth < threshold`) with no hysteresis gap. Under sustained decode load, queue depth can stay `>= threshold` indefinitely, so a checkpointed prefill never resumes — inflating TTFT instead of improving it. This didn't show up in the unit tests (mocked events, no real queue-depth dynamics) — only a real server benchmark surfaced it.

**Fix:** added `preemption_max_suspend_ms` (default 50ms) as a starvation bound — a suspended checkpoint force-resumes on its next eligible step once it's waited this long, regardless of decode pressure.

## Test Plan

```bash
# No GPU required - FlowPrefill scheduler tests use mocked CUDA events

# 1. FlowPrefill unit tests (21 tests)
PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_flowprefill.py -v --tb=short

# 2. Full scheduler regression suite
PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q --tb=short

# 3. Real server A/B (see below)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B ...
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 4 ...
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests** — 21/21 passed (19 original + 2 new covering the starvation-bound fix).

**Scheduler regression suite** — 71/102 passed, 31 pre-existing failures. All 31 failures (`test_ec_connector_*`, `test_eagle3_mm_encoder_cache_with_shift`, `test_schedule_multimodal_requests`, `test_schedule_partial_requests`, `test_no_mm_input_chunking`, `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_*`) are confirmed pre-existing on upstream main — reproduced with identical output by checking out main and running the same suite. Zero regressions introduced by this PR.

| Suite | Before (main) | After (this PR) | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test_flowprefill.py` | N/A (new file) | 21/21 ✅ | +21 |
| `test_scheduler.py` | 71/102 (31 pre-existing fails) | 71/102 | 0 regressions |

**Real server A/B benchmark** (Qwen3-1.7B, `vllm bench serve`, concurrency=4, random dataset) — this is the result that actually matters, and it's why the starvation-bound fix above exists:

| Config | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| No FlowPrefill (plain scheduler) | 449.84ms | 417.72ms | 990.66ms |
| FlowPrefill, unbounded suspend (the bug above) | 969.43ms | 655.17ms | 2256.12ms |
| FlowPrefill, with `preemption_max_suspend_ms` bound | 411.73ms | 427.04ms | 778.79ms |

Without the bound, FlowPrefill made TTFT more than 2x worse than the plain scheduler. With the bound, it beats the plain scheduler on every TTFT metric (mean -8.5%, median +2.2% within noise, P99 -21.4%).

**Behaviour Table:**

| `preemption_granularity` | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `None` (default) | Identical to upstream — `FlowPrefillMixin` adds no overhead, no code path change |
| `256` (example) | Checkpoint every 256 tokens; decode pressure triggers suspension at next boundary, force-resumes after `preemption_max_suspend_ms` regardless of pressure |

**Hardware:** Linux/WSL2, RTX 3070Ti (sm_86), PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124, CUDA 13.3

## Open question on scope/fit

This PR was written against the Q2 2026 roadmap item "avoid excessive preemption, prefill HoL blocking" (#39749, now closed). I noticed vllm-project/vllm#37308 (the closest real-world HoL-blocking report) traces its root cause to CPU-side engine-loop scheduling stalls rather than GPU-level prefill monopolization — a different layer than what this PR's CUDA-event checkpointing addresses. Happy to discuss whether this is still a fit for the Q3 "Scheduler refactoring" direction (#48168) or if it should be scoped differently.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR: implements FlowPrefill adaptive sub-chunk preemption for v1 Scheduler; zero-overhead when disabled (default).
- [x] The test plan: pytest tests/v1/core/test_flowprefill.py -v (no GPU needed); regression run on full tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py; real server A/B via vllm bench serve.
- [x] The test results: 21/21 new tests pass; all 31 scheduler failures are pre-existing on upstream main — zero regressions; real A/B shows a genuine TTFT win after fixing a starvation bug the benchmark itself surfaced.
- [ ] Documentation update: no user-facing doc changes needed until the feature graduates from experimental. `--preemption-granularity` CLI flag is self-documenting; field docstrings in `SchedulerConfig` cover the API.

</details>

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Reject prefill caps smaller than an intact item
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #62031.

Reject a nonzero long-prefill cap smaller than the configured maximum multimodal item when item chunking is disabled. This replaces an accepted configuration that can permanently stall contended requests with an actionable startup error.

## Claims

- Validate the cap alongside the existing maximum-item versus batch-budget check.
- Cover fixed and adaptive caps; retain disabled-cap, equal/larger-cap, chunkable-input, and disabled-modality behavior.
- Preserve the scheduler, hard budgets, whole-item guard, and fairness policy. Defaults remain unchanged.

## Validation

On macOS arm64, Python 3.11.2, PyTorch 2.14.1, Transformers 5.19.0:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' PYTHONPATH=. \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

**269 passed in 50.67 seconds** on publication commit `776389ac699bdc3761cf596dd7ae8e6236a6da35`, based on upstream `8a6c0449b36e7aba29c2a6b1720ca3c08cfafa32`, including nine new cases. Before/after regressions were also checked at base `642c18d64c4cb6db3ded8fbe1786718cd4005fcb`: four rejection cases fail on unchanged production code and five valid controls pass. The five-file target patch is byte-identical after rebasing. The default commit hooks, sign-off hook, and current-head hook rerun pass, including mypy, Markdown lint, and CI test tethering; git diff --check passes. Existing CPU CI covers the tests. After removing the temporary CPU inference dependency, all nine new cases also pass in isolation with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1; these flags avoid a DNS failure in the existing public-model configuration lookup.

At base `642c18d`, real CPU MRV1 inference was checked with a seeded local tiny LLaVA checkpoint, four image tokens, float32, and batch budget 128. Both image requests were queued while scheduling was paused, then resumed together to guarantee contention.

| Check | Baseline | Patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cap 2, two queued image requests | Startup accepted; generation stalls until the 30-second watchdog | Intended ValueError at startup, reporting cap 2 and item maximum 4 |
| Cap 0, same requests | Both complete | Both complete; identical output tokens |
| Cap 4, same requests | Both complete | Both complete; identical output tokens |

Each valid run produces eight greedy tokens per request. The initial unpaused baseline run completed because overlap was not guaranteed; it is not counted as a stall reproduction.

Both inference checkouts temporarily included the same CPU slot-mapping compatibility change from [open PR #61151](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61151), head 5e0ac9d76f4ddbfa8290f488cebca39645ff81a5. Its two native tests pass locally. Without that dependency, both versions fail in the same pre-existing CPU fallback. The dependency was removed after testing and is excluded from this PR.

GPU/MRV2, HTTP serving, and pretrained-model quality were not tested. No post-rebase inference rerun is claimed; the inference matrix is attributed to base `642c18d`.

## Details

The scheduler caps proposed prefill work before checking whole-image boundaries. If the cap is below an intact item, the boundary guard schedules zero tokens. With multiple eligible requests, the cap stays active and the same state repeats. The baseline remained stuck for 1,000 scheduling passes. Adaptive fair share can also stay below the item size.

The fix adds a 12-line check to compute_mm_encoder_budget, following its existing batch-budget validation. The error tells users to disable the cap with zero or raise it sufficiently. The optimization guide and field documentation explain that validation uses the configured maximum item size, even if a particular request is smaller or alone. Encoder-decoder configuration already resets the threshold to zero.

This matches the fail-fast approach proposed in the [review of #52412](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52412#pullrequestreview-5407246881), while preserving the merged boundary fixes in [#52412](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52412) and [#59721](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59721). The proposal itself has not received maintainer approval.

Tradeoff: conservative startup rejection. A low cap that would work for one request, small images, or light adaptive contention is rejected because later requests could make it unschedulable. Default cap zero and configurations allowing item chunking are unaffected. No performance or output-quality improvement is claimed.

Duplicate searches on October 16, 2026 found no matching open cap-validation fix. [#59030](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59030) changes waiting-queue requeueing. [#61733](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61733) validates whole prompts when chunked prefill is disabled after startup; this validates a multimodal item's per-request cap in configurations that still allow chunked text prefill.

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, tests, and preparation. Publication was authorized by the human submitter. The automated validation commands described above were run by Codex; no human-executed validation is claimed. The commit includes AI attribution and the submitter's DCO sign-off.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks
items.body:
This carries #56831 by @CedricHwong forward to current main. That PR has been idle since 09-14 and no longer passes CI after the rebase. Cedric's commit is kept unchanged, with his authorship. The two commits on top address the review comments on that PR.

Adaptive verification (DSpark) picks the per-step draft budget on the host from rank-local stale confidences, then picks which slots to keep on the device from rank-local live confidences. If TP ranks disagree on either one, they run different batch layouts: different token counts, or equal totals with different request boundaries. That breaks the collectives that follow and can hang them (#54011). This PR makes TP rank 0 authoritative:

1. `get_num_tokens`: `draft_budget` is broadcast with `broadcast_object` (shm MessageQueue, host only).
2. `reallocate_drafts`: on steps that trim, the per-request `capacities` are broadcast from rank 0 before `cu_num_logits` / `query_start_loc` are built.

Both conditions around (2), `draft_budget == 0` and `draft_budget < scheduled drafts`, depend only on the broadcast budget and scheduler-provided counts. Every TP rank therefore takes the same branch, and the collective cannot be entered unevenly.

### Changes vs #56831

- **Test updates for current main.** #56888 renamed `async_copy_to_gpu` to `async_tensor_h2d`; the old monkeypatch no longer resolved, giving 12 failures, and `cpu.yaml` runs `-x`. #55939 made `tests/v1/spec_decode` type-checked, so the test now narrows `_batch_budget` before indexing it.
- **`capacities` now goes over the TP group's PyNCCL communicator when it is enabled**, and falls back to `GroupCoordinator.broadcast` otherwise (`VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL`, XPU, CPU).
  - **Why not `GroupCoordinator.broadcast`:** it uses `torch.distributed` on the device group. On CUDA no other TP collective touches that group, and vLLM passes no `device_id`, so its NCCL communicator would be created on the first trimmed serving step, after the KV cache was sized. Measured on MI355X with a cold device group: +105 ms / +1.0 GiB per GPU at TP2, and +224 ms / +1.7-1.8 GiB per GPU at TP4.
  - **Why not `device_communicator.broadcast`:** it raises when PyNCCL is disabled on CUDA, and on XPU it passes the group-local `src` where torch expects a global rank.
  - **Speed:** PyNCCL is also faster per call: about 6 us vs 32 us host enqueue, and 12-14 us vs 25-26 us GPU time.
- A test case covers the PyNCCL-disabled fallback.

Scope: this covers TP, which also covers DCP. With PCP > 1, each PCP rank's TP group has its own leader, and AV + PCP is not gated today; that is a follow-up.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, plus `mypy` / `ruff` via the pre-commit pins.
- Multi-rank CPU harness: real gloo groups, the real `GroupCoordinator` and the real `AdaptiveVerificationManager`. TP 2/4/8, with injected per-rank confidence drift from 1 ULP to large.
- MI355X microbenchmark of both collectives, using vLLM's real TP group (`init_distributed_environment` + `initialize_model_parallel`) at TP2/TP4.
- MI355X end to end:
  - Model: Qwen3-4B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` with `enable_adaptive_verification: true`, V2 model runner, ROCM_ATTN.
  - Workload: 600 GSM8K CoT prompts, output 512, greedy.
  - A/B: main vs this PR, conc 1/16/64, 4 interleaved rounds per arm.
  - Divergence check: an instrumented main that all-gathers every rank's locally computed budget, capacities and confidences on every step.

## Test Result

- **Unit tests:** 49 passed. mypy and ruff are clean. With both collectives removed, the 9 TP>1 cases that need consensus fail.
- **Multi-rank harness:** 0 mismatches on this branch at every world size and drift level.
  - Without the fix, a single fp32 ULP is enough to change the layout. Mismatching steps per 1000 at TP 2/4/8 (capacities or boundaries):
    - 1-16 ULP: 0-2
    - 1e-4 relative: 2-9
    - 1e-2 relative: 65-382
  - Most mismatches have equal totals across ranks but different request boundaries.
- **Per-step cost, MI355X, p50 (p90), slowest rank:**

| | TP2 | TP4 |
|---|---|---|
| `broadcast_object(budget)`: every step that has drafts, host only | 6.7 us (7.5) | 7.9 us (8.2) |
| `capacities` broadcast: trimmed steps only. Host enqueue + in-stream GPU time; does not depend on num_reqs from 1 to 256 | 6.2 + 12.4 us | 6.5 + 14.0 us |
| Worst-case total for a trimmed step, with no overlap | ~25 us | ~29 us (p90 ~32) |

  That is 0.2-0.6% of a 5-15 ms decode step, about the cost of two of the TP all-reduces each step already does. With the original `GroupCoordinator.broadcast`, a trimmed step costs about 64-68 us.
- **End to end at TP2: no measurable regression.** Each delta is within about 1.2 standard deviations; run-to-run CV is 0.2-0.6%.

| conc | output tok/s, main | output tok/s, this PR | delta | TPOT p50, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 721.0 ± 4.1 | 727.7 ± 10 | +0.9% | 1.311 → 1.314 ms |
| 16 | 5489 ± 12 | 5493 ± 15 | +0.1% | 2.755 → 2.763 ms |
| 64 | 10590 ± 50 | 10585 ± 19 | -0.1% | 5.615 → 5.629 ms |

  Acceptance length is unchanged (±0.7%). There were 0 failed requests in 24 runs. The `capacities` broadcast fired on about 97% of c16/c64 steps and about 7% of c1 steps.
- **Natural divergence was not observed on this setup.**
  - Instrumented main ran 8434 steps at TP2 and 7886 steps at TP4: 0 budget, capacities or confidence mismatches.
  - A separate DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MI355X serving trace ran about 478k AV steps, also with 0 mismatches.
  - Here the confidence inputs are bitwise identical across ranks, because the custom all-reduce sums in a fixed rank order. Divergence needs rank-asymmetric numerics, such as rank-order-dependent reductions, non-deterministic kernels, or the TP8 H20 DeepSeek-V4 setup in #54011.
  - The fix is cheap insurance against that: per the numbers above, about 7 us host per step plus about 19 us per trimmed step.

Co-authored with @CedricHwong (original fix, #56831). Supersedes #56831.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Profile adaptive verification tails as mixed batches
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #54046.

Adaptive verification profiles token counts beyond the cudagraph capture limit by distributing them across dummy requests. With `max_num_seqs=128` and seven speculative tokens, a real decode request contributes eight query tokens, so a fully occupied decode step contains at most:

```text
128 * (1 + 7) = 1024 tokens
```

Tail samples above 1024 tokens cannot be uniform decode batches. Previously, however, a 16384-token sample was profiled as 128 requests with 128 query tokens each, producing a shape the scheduler cannot generate for speculative decoding.

This change profiles tail samples as schedulable mixed decode/prefill batches.

For the configuration reported in the issue:

```text
max_num_batched_tokens = 16384
max_num_seqs           = 128
num_speculative_tokens = 7
profile_context_len    = 8192
```

the 16384-token profile becomes:

```text
126 decode requests * 8 tokens
2 fresh-prefill requests * 7688 tokens
```

## Changes

- Keep captured token sizes unchanged so their dummy runs continue to match their cudagraph descriptors.
- Convert only tail sizes above the decode ceiling into mixed decode/prefill batches.
- Account for the decode tokens freed when a request slot becomes prefill.
- Allow small request budgets to produce a schedulable prefill-only tail instead of falling back to an invalid uniform shape.
- Carry the explicit per-request split through the existing scheduler output.
- Give context only to decode rows.
- Mark trailing rows as fresh prefill and construct their positions accordingly.
- Size dummy block tables for the longest decode or prefill sequence.
- Preserve the existing even split when no explicit profile shape is supplied.
- Fall back to the existing dummy shape if cudagraph dispatch pads or reshapes the batch.

## Tests

Hardware:

```text
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
CUDA-enabled PyTorch environment
```

Regression command:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py
```

Result:

```text
54 passed, 14 warnings
```

Additional checks:

```text
py_compile: passed
ruff check 0.14.0: passed
ruff format --check 0.14.0: passed
```

The CUDA regression test verifies the explicit split, decode-only context, fresh-prefill metadata, positions, sequence lengths, and KV block-table coverage.

A full DSpark model-serving evaluation was not run because the corresponding large-model environment was not available on this single-GPU host. This change affects startup profiling shapes and does not modify sampling or verification kernels.

## Related work

#54065 addresses the same reported issue. This implementation additionally:

- keeps the prefill rows context-free instead of applying dummy decode context to every row;
- accounts for freed decode tokens when sizing prefill chunks;
- covers small request budgets that require a prefill-only tail.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during investigation, implementation and test. Every changed line and the reported test results were reviewed.

items.title: [Spec Decode] Support the Liquid LFM2.5-VL DSpark drafter
items.body:
## Overview

Enable `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-3B` with its official DSpark drafter, reusing vLLM's existing dense DSpark implementation.

## Claims

- Normalize the draft architecture, interleaved RoPE flag, and confidence-head layout before model inspection.
- Expose trained LFM2 target features through the VL wrapper and include speculative history in ShortConv cache planning.
- Add focused regression tests and a documented usage example.

## Validation

**30 tests passed** with repository fixtures enabled. All selected pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and CI test tethering.

Validated on one H100 80GB, MRV2, BF16, TP=1, K=9, eager; async scheduling, adaptive verification, and prefix caching disabled.

| Workload | Baseline tok/s | DSpark tok/s | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Full MMSpec: 600 samples / 723 turns | 73.87 | 202.77 | 2.74x time ratio; 31.33% acceptance, mean acceptance length 3.82 |
| Text: 3 warmup passes / 5 measured passes | Median 89.31 (89.02–90.01) | Median 258.18 (247.93–262.34) | 2.89x median time ratio; all 25 request pairs matched |

MMSpec is one unwarmed pass including image encoding, prefill, and request overhead. Loading/downloads are excluded. The output cap was 512; 12 turns reached it in each mode. 722/723 turns matched exactly; one BF16 replay reproduced a top-score tie with different greedy selection. Gold-answer accuracy was not scored.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and pinned versions</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py tests/model_executor/test_lfm2_aux_hidden_states.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2.py vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_vl.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py tests/model_executor/test_lfm2_aux_hidden_states.py docs/features/speculative_decoding/dspark.md docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md
```

GPU validation harness and commands: https://gist.github.com/haror1/bf4c18968bff28f174cebba26922760d

Target: `35a118d938ce6d123ac2d371649f24a8efb69058`; draft: `af77e9306a26e8625fde74d2a3051ab6d21bd955`; MMSpec: `290486861eabd746075ca776adb66175636c1fc0`. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.95.05. Greedy sampling with the target chat template; separate processes with uncontrolled GPU placement/clocks. Unit tests emitted 14 Torch deprecation warnings. Upstream pre-commit is gated by contributor/label eligibility; full Buildkite CI awaits a reviewer trigger.

</details>

## Details

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Profile adaptive verification tail on a schedulable batch shape
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54046.

`AdaptiveVerificationManager.batches_to_profile` seeds the cost tables from dummy runs at every captured size plus a doubling tail up to `max_num_batched_tokens`. The tail sizes are handed to `_dummy_run` as a bare token count, which splits them evenly over `min(num_tokens, max_num_seqs)` requests, and `InputBatch.make_dummy` splits evenly again.

With `max_num_seqs=128` and `num_speculative_tokens=7` that times the 16384-token tail as **128 requests of 128 queries each**, all carrying `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN` of context. A fully occupied decode step is `128 * (1 + 7) = 1024` tokens, so every tail sample above 1024 measures a shape the scheduler cannot produce -- and those samples are exactly what `set_initial_cost_curves` fits the verify curve to and extrapolates beyond.

The fix shapes the tail as the mixed step it has to be:

- The surplus over the decode ceiling can only be prefill, so it is cut into chunks sized by `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN` (already the profiler's stand-in for a sequence length).
- The prefill slots come out of the request budget; the remaining slots stay decode requests of exactly `1 + num_speculative_tokens` queries, and their freed tokens go back to the chunks.
- The split is threaded through `_dummy_run` -> `execute_model` -> `InputBatch.make_dummy`.

For the example in the issue (`max_num_batched_tokens=16384, ctx=8192, max_num_seqs=128, k=7`) the profiled 16384-token step becomes 126 decode requests of 8 queries plus 2 prefill chunks of 7688, instead of 128 x 128.

Scope is deliberately narrow:

- **Captured sizes keep the even split.** Those runs have to match the descriptor their graph was captured with.
- **`make_dummy` only honours an explicit split when cudagraph dispatch did not pad or reshape the batch**; otherwise the shape belongs to the descriptor and the even split is used, exactly as today. `_dummy_run`'s even split and `make_dummy`'s are identical, so passing the caller's split through is a no-op for every existing dummy-run caller.
- `get_uniform_decode_token_count` already returns `None` for a non-uniform batch, so a mixed profiling batch cannot be dispatched into a uniform decode graph.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "54046 in:body"` -- no results.
- Searched open PRs for `adaptive verification profile` and for `batches_to_profile`. The only nearby open PR is #52233, which caches the calibrated curves across boots; it does not change which shapes get profiled, so the two are orthogonal (they touch the same two files and may need a trivial rebase).

## Test Plan

```bash
# New + existing unit coverage for the profiled shapes
python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -q

# Regression over the dummy-run / cudagraph paths this threads a split through
python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py -q
```

Plus an on-GPU probe that drives a mixed decode/prefill dummy batch through the V2 runner (`facebook/opt-125m`, `max_num_seqs=8`, `enforce_eager`), recording what `InputBatch.make_dummy` actually built.

## Test Result

Hardware: NVIDIA RTX A6000, Ubuntu, CUDA 13.

**Unit / regression:** `55 passed` across the six files above, including the three new tests.

The new tests are discriminating: reverting only the `batches_to_profile` wiring (leaving the tests untouched) fails
`test_profiled_tail_batches_are_shapes_the_scheduler_can_produce` with `assert None is not None`.

**On-GPU shape probe** (identical `num_tokens`, only the split differs):

| dummy run | what `make_dummy` built |
| --- | --- |
| today's even split | `num_reqs=8, num_tokens=256, split=[32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32]` |
| explicit mixed split | `num_reqs=8, num_tokens=256, split=[2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 122, 122]` |

The mixed batch forwards without error and ordinary generation is unaffected afterwards
(`llm.generate("The capital of France is")` -> `' on par-and-par with Venezuela'`).

**Model evaluation:** not applicable -- this changes only the batch shapes timed during startup calibration. It does not touch sampling, the verification kernels, or any token the model emits; the generation check above confirms the serving path is unchanged. The behavioural effect is on the seeded verify cost curve, and hence on the draft budgets adaptive verification chooses.

`tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_mode.py` has 14 failures on this machine, but they reproduce identically on unmodified `main` (verified by swapping the four changed files back and re-running), so they are environmental and unrelated.

Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0, the pinned pre-commit revision) clean on all four files.

`mypy` over the three changed source files reports 6 errors, all of which reproduce on unmodified `main` (7 there); the one that disappears is `input_batch.py: Need type annotation for "num_scheduled_tokens"`, now that the parameter carries an explicit annotation. No new type errors.

---

items.title: [Spec Decode] Cache adaptive verification profiles
items.body:
## Purpose

DSpark adaptive verification profiles target-forward and drafter costs at every captured and eager-tail shape during each engine boot. The calibration is deterministic for a fixed model, runtime, backend, hardware, and serving configuration, but it currently runs five replays per shape every time.

This PR adds an opt-in persistent cache for the exact calibrated draft and verification curves. Enable it with:

```bash
export VLLM_ENABLE_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CACHE=1
```

Cache entries live under `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/adaptive_verification/`.

## Why this is not a duplicate

I searched open and closed PRs for `adaptive verification cache`, `adaptive verification profile`, `DSpark profile cache`, and the proposed environment variable. No existing PR persists these curves.

- #47808 introduced adaptive verification and its startup calibration; it intentionally recalibrates on each boot.
- #50919 adds worker-level runtime timing observability, not persistent startup-profile reuse.
- #47131 and #48692 implement related adaptive verification policies, not caching.

## Design

Cache reuse is fail-closed:

- Rank 0 atomically saves the exact median curves already broadcast by `set_cost_curves`.
- The cache key includes an immutable model identity (resolved remote revision or local config/index digest), GPU identity and compute capability, TP/PP/DP/DCP, vLLM/PyTorch/FlashInfer/CUDA/HIP/cuDNN versions, resolved attention/KV and quantization kernel implementations, K, KV dtype, scheduler limits, CUDA graph mode/capture grid, and profile context.
- Entries carry a schema version, their full fingerprint inputs, strictly validated positive curves, and a SHA-256 payload checksum.
- All TP ranks must independently produce the same fingerprint.
- A hit runs two full-CUDA-graph sentinel replays. Both target and drafter timings must resolve to exact cached curve points and remain within a deliberately generous 0.4x-2.5x range on every TP rank.
- Any missing revision/index, I/O error, corruption, version mismatch, heterogeneous TP fingerprint, or sentinel anomaly falls back to the existing full profile and refreshes the cache.

The feature is disabled by default. Cold-start behavior and the cost-table construction are unchanged; a valid hit passes the same curves through the existing `set_cost_curves` path. This does not change token sampling or output correctness.

## Startup impact

For the DeepSeek-V4 DSpark configuration that motivated this change (12 captured shapes, 8 eager-tail shapes, 5 replays each), a cold calibration performs 100 dummy runs while a warm hit performs 2 sentinel runs: 98% fewer profiling runs.

In a saved TP2 DGX Spark startup log, graph capture plus adaptive calibration took 353 seconds, with approximately 340 seconds after DSpark graph capture attributable to the calibration phase. The projected warm graph/profile phase is about 13-15 seconds. These are projected warm-cache savings from the observed cold log; this branch has not yet been benchmarked end-to-end on that GPU, so the PR remains draft.

## Test plan

Passed:

```text
/Users/carlos/exo/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/v1/spec_decode tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification_cache.py
# 4 passed

/Users/carlos/exo/.venv/bin/ruff check <all changed Python files>
# All checks passed

/Users/carlos/exo/.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q <all changed Python files>
git diff --check
# passed
```

The focused tests cover exact round trips/fingerprint misses, payload corruption, schema-version rejection, and sentinel point/mode/timing rejection.

I also attempted the pre-existing `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py` suite. It could not collect in this macOS development environment because the partial environment lacks the full vLLM test dependency set (`einops` was the final reported missing dependency after installing `tblib`, `pyzmq`, `cbor2`, and `openai` into a temporary target). No output/model evaluation was run because this is an opt-in startup-only change that reuses exact calibrated inputs and fails closed; a warm/cold GPU startup comparison is still required before marking the PR ready.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to port the implementation, write tests, and prepare this description. I reviewed every changed line and confirm that I understand the design and can defend the implementation. A warm/cold GPU validation is still required before moving this PR out of draft.

items.title: PR Title: [Feature] EWSJF: Adaptive Scheduler for Mixed-Workloads (30-50% Throughput Gain)
items.body:
**Summary**  
This PR introduces EWSJF (Effective Workload‑based Shortest Job First), an adaptive request‑level scheduler designed to eliminate Head‑of‑Line (HoL) blocking in mixed workloads that combine short interactive queries with long batch requests.

The design aligns with RFC #24484 on mitigating HoL blocking and RFC #24484 on pluggable scheduler interfaces.

By grouping requests into performance‑homogeneous queues and applying a density‑weighted scoring function, EWSJF improves both throughput and tail latency compared to the default FCFS scheduler.

**Key Results**  
Benchmarks (Llama‑2‑13B, NVIDIA A100, Poisson arrivals):

- Token Throughput: +30% to +54%  
- TTFT (Short Requests): Up to 4× reduction  
- GPU Utilization: ~65% → ~80%

Full technical report: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21758

**Implementation Details**  
EWSJF runs upstream of the execution engine and includes:

- Refine‑and‑Prune Partitioning: Dynamically groups requests by prompt length to avoid oversized queues.  
- Context‑Aware Scoring: Balances urgency, fairness, and SJF‑style efficiency.  
- Bayesian Meta‑Optimizer: Continuously tunes scoring weights based on workload shifts.

**Test Plan**  
A new benchmark script (`benchmarks/benchmark_ewsjf.py`) simulates mixed workloads.

Reproduction steps:

```
# 1. Generate mixed dataset (80% short, 20% long)
python tools/generate_workload.py --type mixed --count 10000

# 2. Run benchmark with EWSJF
python benchmarks/benchmark_serving.py --scheduler ewsjf --dataset mixed_workload.json
```

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep DSV4.1 sparse prefill out of FULL cudagraphs
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #59970. Fixes #62417. The five DSV4.1-specific sparse metadata builders declare `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, so with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` prefill and mixed batches get FULL-graph captured even though their prefill metadata is not graph-safe, and the engine dies with an illegal memory access once adaptive verification runs mixed batches at concurrency. Downgrade them to `UNIFORM_BATCH` and report the speculation width as the varlen decode bound, mirroring the reviewed pattern from #59751.

## Claims

- Prefill and mixed batches leave FULL capture for all five builders named in #59970: `DeepseekV4FlashMLAMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekV4FlashInferSparseMLAMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekSparseSWAFlashInferMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekSparseSWAFlashMLAMetadataBuilder`, `CompressorMetadataBuilder`. `FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend` inherits the same builder, so it is covered too.
- FULL varlen decode graphs are kept for uniform batches sized up to 1 + num_speculative_tokens, so DSpark adaptive verification keeps its decode graphs.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -q
```

82 passed on CPU. The 10 new parametrized cases pin, per backend and num_speculative_tokens in {0, 7}, that support resolves to `UNIFORM_BATCH`, that decode widths up to the speculation width stay graph-eligible, and that one token wider is rejected with the reported bound. Changed-file pre-commit (ruff-check, ruff-format) passed.

Not run: the B300 (SM103) end-to-end reproducer from the issue, no compatible hardware available here, and CI does not exercise these builders. The change only narrows what FULL graphs capture: prefill moves to the piecewise path that the issue's adaptive-verification-off and FULL_DECODE_ONLY arms already exercise for 30+ minutes under load, so no batch that was not captured before becomes captured.

## Details

Root cause, from the issue's arm table: adaptive verification on + FULL_AND_PIECEWISE hits the IMA 4/4 within a minute; verification off in the same mode is stable; verification on with FULL_DECODE_ONLY is stable. The failing ingredient is prefill inside FULL graphs. Each affected builder now also overrides `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` to return `max_decode_query_len(vllm_config)` (1 + num_speculative_tokens on MRV2), the same width the V2 runner uses when it builds varlen decode replays.

Not a duplicate of #59751: that PR changes only the generic `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` for #59681, while the DSV4.1 model wires its own five builders, which the #59970 reporter calls out explicitly. Checked the issue thread and open PRs referencing #59970 before starting; nothing else covers them.

items.title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Do not schedule ahead of an uncapped lone prefill chunk
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #60476. Since #57951 a lone long prefill runs uncapped chunks of `max_num_batched_tokens`, and with async scheduling (or `max_concurrent_batches > 1`) the next chunk is scheduled while the current one is still executing. A request that arrives mid-prefill therefore sits through up to two full uncapped steps before `long_prefill_token_threshold` can engage again. This change stops the batch queue from scheduling ahead of a chunk that ran uncapped under the lone-request exemption, so the cap re-engages right behind the in-flight chunk.

## Claims

- A request arriving during a lone uncapped long prefill is now seen by the scheduler before any further chunk is committed: worst-case head-of-line wait drops from about two uncapped steps to the remainder of the in-flight one.
- The #57951 exemption is unchanged: a request that stays alone still prefills at full `max_num_batched_tokens`.
- No effect when `long_prefill_token_threshold` is 0 (default), when the exemption does not fire (more than one eligible request), or for steps within the configured threshold (e.g. decode), so single-stream decoding keeps schedule-ahead pipelining.

## Validation

Scheduler level, run locally on CPU:

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k long_prefill
```

Four tests pass: flag set for an uncapped lone chunk, flag clear for a within-threshold step, flag clear with multiple eligible requests, flag clear when the adaptive floor binds without the exemption. Red/green was checked by stashing the source changes (all four fail without them) and restoring.

Engine level: new `test_engine_core_no_schedule_ahead_of_uncapped_lone_prefill` in `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py` drives a real EngineCore with a 2-deep batch queue, a 12-token prompt, `max_num_batched_tokens=10`, threshold 5:

- the first chunk is scheduled uncapped (10 > 5) and flagged;
- the next `step_with_batch_queue` call pops that batch instead of scheduling a second chunk behind it (before this change it scheduled ahead and the queue reached depth 2);
- after a second request is added, the very next schedule caps it to 5 tokens and co-schedules the first request.

This machine has no CUDA and that module is CUDA-only, so the engine test was not run locally; it is expected to run in CI. The gate was verified locally by driving `EngineCore.step_with_batch_queue` with a mocked engine: with a flagged batch queued, `schedule()` is not called; with an unflagged batch it is; on unpatched code `schedule()` is called in both cases.

`DummyExecutor` and `make_request_with_max_tokens` move from `test_engine_core_concurrent_batches` to module scope so both engine tests share them; that test's body is unchanged.

## Details

Root cause: #57951 zeroes the effective threshold when `running + waiting <= 1`. The predicate is evaluated at schedule time, but with a batch queue the schedule for step N+1 runs while step N still executes. A newcomer that lands between the two schedules is invisible to both, so two uncapped chunks of `max_num_batched_tokens` each get committed before the threshold can re-engage. At deep context one such chunk takes seconds (the issue logs show about 10 s of extra wait at a 65536-token budget), which is exactly the head-of-line blocking the flag exists to prevent.

The queued chunk is already launched, so it cannot be re-capped. The only place to restore the #57951 contract ("as soon as any other request is present, the threshold applies") is to never schedule ahead of an uncapped lone chunk. When `Scheduler.schedule()` sees the exemption actually let a chunk exceed the configured threshold, it marks the batch via the new `SchedulerOutput.has_uncapped_lone_prefill`; `EngineCore.step_with_batch_queue` then skips scheduling a new batch and blocks on the queued one first, so the next schedule observes any arrival that drained in the meantime.

Tradeoff: behind an uncapped lone chunk the GPU idles for one schedule + launch (milliseconds per multi-second chunk) instead of having the next chunk ready. Only configurations that set `long_prefill_token_threshold` pay this, and only while a lone long prefill is actually running uncapped.

Alternatives considered: re-capping the queued chunk (impossible, it is launched at schedule time); bounding the exempted chunk size or making the exemption opt-in (both weaken the lone-TTFT benefit of #57951, which this keeps intact). The remaining wait of up to one in-flight uncapped chunk is inherent to the exemption and matches its documented intent.

Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses the exemption / schedule-ahead interaction (checked #60476 comments, plus open PRs for "long prefill threshold", "lone prefill", and "60476 in:body"). #57427 (partial-prefill concurrency limit) and #58420 (SRPF) are separate mechanisms.

items.title: [Perf] Add an adaptive prefill delayer for data-parallel serving
items.body:
## Purpose

  When a large prefill is scheduled on only one DP engine, that engine performs a
  much longer model iteration while the other engines wait for it to finish. This
  creates uneven iteration times and delays ongoing decode requests.

  This PR adds an optional adaptive prefill delayer. It coordinates large prefill
  work onto the same engine steps across DP ranks, reducing iterations where one
  rank is doing prefill while others are decoding. Decode continues while prefill
  is delayed, with bounded fail-open and recovery behavior to guarantee progress.

  ## Test Plan

  Tested DeepSeek-V4 using:

  ```bash
  vllm serve "$MODEL" \
      --trust-remote-code \
      --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
      --block-size 256 \
      --no-enable-prefix-caching \
      --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
      --data-parallel-size 8 \
      --enable-expert-parallel \
      --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
      --prefill-schedule-interval 1 \
      --enable-adaptive-prefill-alignment \
      --prefill-alignment-max-delay-passes 30 \
      --prefill-alignment-target-step-lead 2 \
      --max-model-len 16384 \
      --max-num-batched-tokens 2048
  ```

  Added unit tests for coordinated release, delay limits, capacity release,
  missing acknowledgments, and DP-wave resets.

  ## Test Result

  ```text
  10 passed in 9.68s
  Ruff checks passed
  All changed files are formatted
  ```

items.title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Suffix decoding speculator for Model Runner V2
items.body:
## Overview `method="suffix"` today needs Arctic Inference, runs on the CPU, forces Model Runner V1 and disables async scheduling. With this PR it runs on Model Runner V2 with a GPU speculator, with async scheduling and without Arctic; V1 keeps using Arctic. This is the "suffix" item in #47172. The speculator builds on `ngram_gpu` (#40704) and borrows from #52097 (thanks @zip95297). Related fix on main: #61509 (adaptive verification's startup profiling was counted as CUDA graph memory). ## Claims - `method="suffix"` runs on Model Runner V2: GPU-resident, no host sync on the propose path, async scheduling, no Arctic dependency. V1 is unchanged except for the default `num_speculative_tokens` (below). - Acceptance is on par with Arctic: 1.937 tokens per step vs Arctic's 1.923 (k=8) and 1.948 (k=24) on a 21K-request replay. - With adaptive verification, throughput matches or beats Arctic on V1 at every concurrency for Qwen2.5-7B (offline and online serving) and for Qwen2.5-1.5B from concurrency 64 up; at 1.5B concurrency 8 and 32 Arctic is ahead (below). Without adaptive verification, verifying every slot loses from concurrency 32 up, as with `ngram_gpu`. - GSM8K accuracy matches no speculation. - `num_speculative_tokens` now defaults to 8 for suffix decoding (was `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth`, 24), because V2 verifies every slot. - Seeded sampled requests are reproducible regardless of the rest of the batch, also with adaptive verification. ## Validation **Tests** ```bash pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_speculator.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py # 46 passed pytest tests/test_config.py -k "speculative or suffix or heterogeneous or model_runner" # 50 passed pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram_gpu.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py # 31 passed pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/ngram_suffix/test_ngram_suffix.py -k suffix # 3 passed ``` The e2e tests ran with the CI model's weights (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) on one L4: - The V2 GSM8K correctness test passes (76.3%). At the old default k=24 it ran out of memory: V2 profiles one logits row per request, while every step computes 1 + k. - The V2 cross-request test gives 0.74 → 4.47 accepted tokens per draft on the repeated pass. With Qwen2.5-1.5B it's 1.32 → 5.12, and 1.28 → 1.28 with the corpus off, which the test's `second > 2 * first` check rejects. - The Arctic acceptance test (V1) passes. **Runtime checks** - **No new host syncs:** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` with and without adaptive verification, including seeded requests and ingestion. - **TP=2:** corpus, index, statistics and drafts are identical on both ranks after 312 requests, with and without adaptive verification, on the default ring and on a 2,048-token ring where bursts of up to 48 finished requests wrap over themselves. - **Seeded requests:** a seeded request alone vs in a 64-request batch gives identical output 4/4, with and without adaptive verification (before this change, 1/4 with it). **Acceptance.** Replay of 21,299 greedy Qwen2.5-1.5B requests with 5.1M output tokens (UltraChat, Alpaca, GSM8K, Spec-Bench, code edit, rewrite and templated JSON), in waves of 64, with a 1M-token corpus and k=8. Mean tokens per step. Arctic runs via `arctic_inference` and also sees responses still being generated. The kernel matches the replay on all 1,280 sampled drafts. | Drafter | All | Code edit | Rewrite | Templated JSON | |---|---|---|---|---| | Own history only | 1.651 | 5.50 | 4.74 | 1.65 | | **This PR** | **1.937** | 5.45 | 4.69 | 4.25 | | Exact corpus search + same vote (upper bound) | 1.956 | 5.45 | 4.69 | 4.28 | | Arctic (V1), k=8 | 1.923 | 5.12 | 4.07 | 3.89 | | Arctic (V1), k=24 | 1.948 | 5.89 | 4.37 | 4.11 | **Throughput.** Offline `LLM.generate` on this PR's final code. Output tokens/s relative to no speculation. - **Setup:** concurrency = `max_num_seqs`; prompts from a pinned pool with the replay's category mix (its GSM8K and Spec-Bench prompts also appear in the replay); greedy, `max_tokens=256`, k=8. - **Backends:** FlashAttention 2, except adaptive verification on `TRITON_ATTN`, which is compared against no speculation on `TRITON_ATTN`. - **Runs:** one per point; runs with another process on the GPU were discarded and rerun. | Model | Concurrency | `ngram_gpu` | Arctic (V1) | This PR | This PR + adaptive verification | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2.5-7B | 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 | 1.28 / 1.14 / 0.73 / 0.52x | 1.31 / 1.29 / 1.24 / 1.03x | 1.46 / 1.32 / 0.82 / 0.59x | **1.39 / 1.36 / 1.24 / 1.18x** | | Qwen2.5-1.5B | 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 | 1.45 / 1.25 / 0.84 / 0.55 / 0.50 / 0.44x | 1.41 / 1.43 / 1.17 / 1.00 / 0.91 / 0.82x | 1.66 / 1.47 / 0.97 / 0.64 / 0.56 / 0.52x | **1.56 / 1.29 / 1.15 / 1.05 / 0.99 / 0.91x** | - **Where Arctic wins:** 1.5B at concurrency 8 and 32, by 11% and 5% in absolute tok/s. Adaptive verification trims too much there (open question 2). - **Backend difference:** at 1.5B concurrency 128 / 256, `TRITON_ATTN` without speculation is 1.13 / 1.21x faster than FA2. Against the FA2 baseline the other columns use, adaptive verification is 1.12 / 1.10x. - **With #61509:** the 7B KV cache with adaptive verification grows from 21–46K to 50–70K tokens. 7B throughput becomes 1.38 / 1.32 / 1.30 / 1.15x, within run-to-run noise except at concurrency 32. **Online serving** (`vllm bench serve`, Qwen2.5-7B, prompts not in the 256-request warm-up, up to 256 output tokens, `--generation-config vllm`). Output throughput vs no speculation: | Config | Concurrency 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 | |---|---| | `ngram_gpu` | 1.26 / 1.11 / 0.73 / 0.53x | | Arctic (V1) | 1.42 / 1.37 / 1.24 / 1.10x | | This PR | 1.49 / 1.35 / 0.87 / 0.65x | | **This PR + adaptive verification** (vs no-spec on `TRITON_ATTN`) | **1.44 / 1.44 / 1.30 / 1.23x** | Median TTFT at concurrency 1 is 125 ms with this PR (with or without adaptive verification) and with `ngram_gpu`, vs 73 ms without speculation and 74 ms for Arctic on V1, which runs without async scheduling. That is about one decode step, so it's a V2 spec-decode cost rather than a suffix one.
GSM8K, workloads and correctness checks **GSM8K** (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, all 1,319 questions, 5-shot, `max_num_seqs=128`). Accuracy matches within noise (binomial SE about 1 point); at this load speculation doesn't speed it up: | Config | Greedy | Temperature 0.7 | Wall time (greedy) | |---|---|---|---| | No speculation (FA2) | 83.0% | 81.7% | 193 s | | No speculation (`TRITON_ATTN`) | 83.4% | 82.3% | 156 s | | Arctic (V1) | 83.4% | 83.2% | 252 s | | This PR | 82.8% | 83.6% | 387 s | | This PR + adaptive verification (`TRITON_ATTN`) | 82.9% | 81.6% | 157 s | **Workloads.** Offline, throughput vs no speculation (adaptive verification vs no-spec on `TRITON_ATTN`). Concurrency 32, except long context: | Workload | This PR | + adaptive verification | Arctic (V1) | |---|---|---|---| | VLM: Qwen2.5-VL-3B, 360 distinct camera frames, templated JSON reports and captions | 1.38x (3.18 tok/step) | 1.50x | 1.56x | | RL rollouts: Qwen2.5-1.5B, GSM8K, n=8, temperature 1 | 0.94x | 1.40x | 1.16x | | Multi-turn chat: Qwen2.5-7B, UltraChat history | 0.78x | 1.15x | 1.03x | | RAG + summarization: Qwen2.5-7B, Spec-Bench | 0.86x | 1.16x | 1.10x | | Long-context decode: 24K-token prompts, concurrency 3 | 1.38x | 0.29x; **1.46x with #61509** | 1.19x | At long context, adaptive verification's startup profiling cost the KV cache 1.9 GiB (43K instead of 80K tokens), so prefixes were evicted and re-prefilled. #61509 fixes that accounting on main. **Correctness** (this PR's final code; greedy outputs vs no speculation, 48 distinct prompts; fp32 Qwen2.5-0.5B on `TRITON_ATTN`, since FA2 has no fp32): | Check | This PR | + adaptive verification | `ngram_gpu` | |---|---|---|---| | Plain greedy | 45/48 | 45/48 | 46/48 | | Repetition/frequency/presence penalties | 43/48 | 44/48 | 43/48 | | Structured outputs (JSON schema, regex, choice), `max_tokens=2`, logprobs | identical | identical | regex 11/12, rest identical | | Stop strings with `min_tokens`; `ignore_eos` to 300 tokens | 48/48; 45/48 | 47/48; 45/48 | 47/48; 45/48 | | 24 distinct 800–1,800-word prompts with chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=512`); 8 prompts ending 40 tokens before `max_model_len` | 24/24, 8/8 | 24/24, 8/8 | 24/24, 8/8 | | Preemption (small KV cache, 144 requests, 355–509 preemptions) | 128/144 | 125/144 | 126/144 | - **Baseline noise:** two no-spec runs, async vs sync scheduling, differ on 1/48 plain prompts. - **Logprobs:** deltas on identical outputs are at most 5e-3, the same as `ngram_gpu`. - **Sampling** (Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16, temperature 1, top-p, top-k, n=16, each method with its own seed): total-variation distance of per-position token marginals vs a no-spec run is 0.153 / 0.079 / 0.131. A second no-spec run gives 0.161 / 0.059 / 0.128, `ngram_gpu` 0.148 / 0.056 / 0.131. Seeded requests reproduce 4/4. - **Aborts** (`vllm serve`, 48 streams aborted mid-generation): the server stays healthy. Greedy requests sent afterwards match those sent before 8/8 without adaptive verification. With it, 7/8 in fp32 (one flip at a 0.0004-nat near-tie) and 2/8 in bf16 7B: the number of verified slots changes the batch shapes.
## Details **How it works** - **Own history:** the longest suffix match within the request's prompt and output, up to `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth`. Same kernel layout as `ngram_gpu`. - **Cross-request corpus:** finished responses go into a GPU token ring (`suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens`, default 1M). A hash index on each request's last 2 and last 4 tokens returns up to 16 candidate positions. Each is verified and extended to its full suffix match, so the index is only an entry point for suffix matching, and hash collisions or overwritten documents only cost a candidate. - **Frequency vote:** for each candidate match length, the candidates matching at least that long vote on the continuation, as in SuffixDecoding. The highest-scoring chain wins, ties going to the longer match; then the longer of the own-history and corpus matches wins. - **Adaptive verification** (`enable_adaptive_verification`): per-slot confidences, learned online by source, match length and position, let the runner trim slots that aren't worth verifying. - **Seeded requests** (explicit `seed`, temperature > 0) draft only from their own history, and adaptive verification verifies all of their slots. Under sampling, both the drafts and the number of verified slots change which tokens are drawn. Greedy requests keep the corpus. - **Ingestion:** one GPU program per (document, block). Each program replays the batch's placement to find its offset and skips positions that a later document of the same batch overwrites. Every position is written by exactly one program, so the result is exact and order-independent even when a burst is larger than the ring. A 256 × 4,096-token burst at the default 1M ring takes 0.58 ms. - **TP consistency without collectives:** finished ids are ingested in sorted order, index inserts use `atomic_max` over `(document << 32 | position)`, and the statistics are integer counters. - **Memory at the defaults:** 36 MB (4 MB corpus plus a 32 MB index). Suffix decoding also keeps the runner's token history on the GPU (`max_num_seqs × max_model_len × 4` bytes, e.g. 32 MiB at 256 × 32K).
How a corpus lookup works (diagram) ``` Request history: ... "report" "the" "camera" "at" "the" "north" "gate" └──── last 4 ────┘ └─ last 2 ┘ 1) LOOK UP hash(last 4), hash(last 2) -> buckets, 8 slots each (slot = newest occurrence in each of the last 8 documents) 2) EXTEND BACKWARDS each candidate against the request (up to 24 tokens): request: report the camera at the north gate corpus: log: the camera at the north gate -> match length 6 stale or colliding candidate -> length 0, dropped 3) VOTE + DRAFT candidates matching >= L tokens vote on the next k tokens; the chain with the highest summed probability wins 4) COMPARE with the longest match in the request's own history; the longer match wins, empty slots get the last token ``` Ingestion when a request finishes: `[last 3 prompt tokens | response]` is appended to the ring, and each position with at least 2 (4) tokens before it in the document is indexed under them: `table[hash][doc % 8] = max(existing, (doc, pos))`.
**Why a hash index** | Index | Propose cost (L4) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Suffix tree (Arctic, V1) | CPU, per request | Host sync, so no MRV2 or async scheduling | | Suffix array (#52097) | 1.3–4.5 ms as an eager library call (prototype measurement on a shared L4); #52097 reports 0.4–1.9 ms with its CUDA-graph path (L20, k=16) | Background rebuilds, epochs and a CPU collective for TP | | Brute-force GPU scan | 0.3–1.2 ms at batch 128 (prototype measurement) | Exact; cost grows with batch × corpus | | **Hash index + vote (this PR)** | **11–35 µs** GPU time for batch 1–256 (CUDA-graph microbenchmark), the same at 1M and 4M corpus tokens. As the engine runs it (eagerly): 89–95 µs per step at 4K context for batch 1–256, 231 µs at 128K context with 32 requests (`ngram_gpu`: 75–78 and 111 µs) | No rebuilds. The index alone is within 0.4% of an exact longest-match search; with the vote, about 1% below exact search + vote | One difference from Arctic: corpus matches need at least 2 tokens (so `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth` must be at least 2 for the corpus), while own-history matches can be 1. Storing the last 3 prompt tokens with each response lets a response's first tokens be drafted from the corpus. **Taken from #52097 and @zip95297's MRV2 port** (`zip95297/vllm-dev`, branch `zip95297/suffix-gpu-mrv2`): GPU cross-request matching with no host sync; an `on_requests_finished` hook in `finish_requests` that ingests from `RequestState` and skips preempted requests (from the MRV2 port); sorting finished ids for TP consistency; the replay-based acceptance evaluation. **Changes outside the speculator** - `SpeculativeConfig`: suffix's default `num_speculative_tokens` is `min(8, suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth)` on both runners. On V1 it caps Arctic's dynamic draft length; set 24 for the previous V1 behavior. - `AdaptiveVerificationManager.pinned_requests`: optional drafter hook. Pinned requests keep all their scheduled drafts and the budget is chosen around them. Only suffix decoding sets it (seeded sampled requests); other drafters are unaffected. - `warmup.py`: drafters with a `reset_state` method reset after MRV2's kernel warmup, so the warmup requests don't stay in the corpus. - `model_runner.py`: `set_sampling_states`, `on_requests_finished` and (with adaptive verification) `add_request` hooks, each called only if the speculator defines it; dense `all_token_ids` for suffix. **Limitations** - The corpus is shared across requests regardless of `cache_salt` or LoRA adapter, like Arctic's global tree on V1 (documented; set `suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens: 0` to isolate). - Adaptive verification needs full CUDA graphs and an attention backend that replays variable-length decode batches. On L4 that is `TRITON_ATTN`: vLLM's FA2 backend declares uniform-batch support only. Until #61509 lands, its startup profiling also costs KV capacity, which matters at long context. - Under async scheduling a finished request can carry up to about 2k+1 tokens past the stop point into the corpus. ## Open questions 1. **Adaptive verification by default?** It is what makes suffix decoding pay off from concurrency 32 up. It isn't on by default here because it fails at startup on backends that can't replay variable-length decode graphs (FA2, the pre-Hopper default), so a default needs a fallback to off. Happy to add that here, or in a follow-up. 2. **Low-concurrency trimming.** Adaptive verification trims too much at low concurrency on small models: Qwen2.5-1.5B at concurrency 8 is 1.29x with it vs 1.47x verifying every slot (7B: 1.36x vs 1.32x). Tune it here (for example with a more optimistic prior) or later? 3. **Corpus default.** 4M tokens adds about 2–3% acceptance, but the index grows from 32 MB to 128 MB. 4. **Tokens past the stop point.** Pass the scheduler's final length down to ingestion? 5. **Arctic-only options** (`max_spec_factor`, `min_token_prob`) are ignored on V2 (documented). Warn as well? ## Follow-ups - Exclude filler slots from spec-decode metrics for GPU drafters (as #52097 does on V1 and its MRV2 branch does; see also #44056 and #50518). With adaptive verification, trimmed slots are still counted as drafted. - Index responses while they're still being generated. That may be why Arctic is ahead on the templated VLM workload. - CUDA-graph the propose path (@zip95297's bucketized draft graphs). - aarch64 benchmarks. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
**Not duplicating existing work:** the only other suffix decoding drafter PR is #52097 (`suffix_gpu` on V1), whose author is collaborating here; searches for "suffix decoding", "suffix_gpu" and "SuffixSpeculator" find no other MRV2 implementation. AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, prototype, write and test this change. cc @njhill @zip95297 @benchislett @TheEpicDolphin

items.title: [v1][kv-transfer] Prioritize remote KV polling in scheduler
items.body:
Add an experimental scheduler path to prioritize remote KV transfer admission and polling before scheduling regular decode work.

In disaggregated prefill/decode deployments, a decode request that needs remote KV blocks can sit behind already-running decode steps. Since the KV connector only starts or observes transfer progress when a scheduler step reaches the connector metadata path, this can inflate TTFT by one or more decode-step boundaries even when the actual NIXL transfer is short.

This change adds an opt-in environment flag,
VLLM_KV_TRANSFER_PRIORITY_POLL, that makes the scheduler run a KV-transfer focused step when all of the following hold:

- KV transfer is enabled for the scheduler.
- There is active decode work in the running queue.
- A waiting or skipped request has KV transfer parameters.
- The scheduler is not paused.

When enabled, the scheduler skips regular running-request decode scheduling for that step and scans waiting/skipped requests for remote KV transfer candidates. Non-KV candidates are preserved by moving them to the step-local skipped queue, while KV candidates may be admitted into WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS so the connector can start or poll the remote load.

This is intentionally gated because it trades decode throughput for lower TTFT. In Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8 disaggregated tests, the policy reduced TTFT by roughly 13-19% for concurrency >= 2. The best observed point was concurrency=4, where TTFT improved by ~19% with negligible ITL impact and slightly higher system throughput. At higher concurrency, unthrottled priority polling increased ITL and reduced system throughput, indicating that follow-up work should add rate limiting or adaptive gating before making this policy a default.

The flag is off by default, preserving existing scheduling behavior.




## Purpose
This PR adds an opt-in scheduler policy for disaggregated KV transfer
workloads. When VLLM_KV_TRANSFER_PRIORITY_POLL=1, the V1 scheduler can
prioritize waiting requests that need remote KV transfer over regular
running decode work for a scheduler step. This helps reduce TTFT caused by
remote KV load admission/polling being delayed behind decode step
boundaries.

The behavior is disabled by default. Initial experiments show meaningful
TTFT improvements, but also reveal a throughput tradeoff at high
concurrency, so this is introduced as an experimental opt-in path rather
than a default policy.

## Test Plan

## Test Result
Observed Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8 disaggregated results:
- concurrency=2: TTFT avg 403.23ms -> 325.01ms, system TPS 45.73 -> 44.22
- concurrency=4: TTFT avg 412.68ms -> 332.75ms, system TPS 89.14 -> 90.93
- concurrency=8: TTFT avg 405.13ms -> 349.82ms, system TPS 174.47 -> 163.27
- concurrency=16: TTFT avg 413.99ms -> 346.66ms, system TPS 336.07 -> 309.06
---

items.title: [SpecDecode] Preserve reject-only residual verifier padding
items.body:
## Summary

- Keep the real one-token prompt tail through Mamba scheduling alignment, then restore the synthetic speculative width before allocation.
- Track reject-only synthetic drafts separately from GPU-safe placeholder token IDs and restore their `-1` sentinel only for rejection sampling.
- Skip uniform residual padding for adaptive DSpark, which already uses a variable verification budget and variable-length decode graphs.
- Select target-verifier FULL graphs only when every request carries the complete verifier draft layout, and describe dummy captures with the same topology.

## Motivation

#54012 enabled FlashInfer native-CP MLA verification, but the failures exposed here are backend-independent. When a new request with one remaining prompt token joins a running speculative-verification batch, vLLM pads it to `1 + num_speculative_tokens` so the target batch remains uniform.

Two independent correctness problems occur in that path. Applying Mamba alignment to the padded width can clip the synthetic verifier shape, and the GPU input path replaces negative placeholder IDs with embedding-safe values before rejection sampling, allowing synthetic drafts to be treated as real proposals. Adaptive DSpark should not enter this fixed-width padding path at all because it deliberately reallocates a variable draft budget.

Target-verifier FULL graphs also capture model-wide branch topology, not only tensor dimensions. A same-shaped short prefill must not select a verifier graph when it lacks the complete draft-token layout. Uniform dummy captures must carry equivalent verifier metadata so distributed and idle ranks select the same graph topology.

## Commit structure

1. Align residual verifier padding after Mamba splits.
2. Preserve synthetic draft rejection sentinels and exclude them from acceptance accounting.
3. Skip uniform padding for adaptive verification.
4. Select FULL graphs by verifier topology.

## Relationship to existing work

This is a follow-up to #54012, not an attention-backend change. #53694 avoids a redundant DP synchronization before draft prefill but does not distinguish target-verifier graphs from same-shaped short-prefill execution. I searched open vLLM PRs and issues for `pad_spec_decode`, residual verifier padding, invalid draft sentinels, verifier graph topology, and same-shaped short prefills and found no directly overlapping fix. #51508 addresses stale zero-accept recurrent-state rows rather than first-decode residual padding, rejection-sampler sentinel loss, or verifier graph selection.

## Tests

Passed locally:

- `uvx ruff check` on all changed Python files.
- `uvx ruff format --check` on all changed Python files.
- `uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python -m py_compile` on all changed Python files.
- `git diff --check`.

Focused pytest and model evaluation are pending because this local worktree does not contain the vLLM runtime/test dependencies. This PR is intentionally opened as a draft. Before marking it ready, I will run the focused scheduler, rejection-sampler, adaptive-verification, and CUDA-graph dispatch tests, then report a mixed-batch Kimi-K3 DCP/EAGLE acceptance and correctness evaluation.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to inspect the current upstream data flow, adapt the internal fixes to TP batch sharding and the post-#53694 DP-sync path, write the initial patches and regressions, and run static validation. The submitter will review every changed line and run the required runtime tests and model evaluation before requesting final review.

items.title: [Core][DP] Add a DP-global prefill gate for prefill_schedule_interval
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Draft, to settle the mechanism first. This overlaps draft #51199 (adaptive prefill delayer for DP serving), which targets the same lockstep problem with per-rank delay budgets and acknowledgments; we would like maintainers to pick one approach before either is reviewed in detail. It builds on #54627 (`prefill_schedule_interval` outside DP).

With `--prefill-schedule-interval N` (PSI), DP ranks admit new prefills only every N steps, except that a rank whose last release could not drain its queue (`prefill_capacity_bound`) releases on every step. Under sustained load that exception sets the step shape: a backlogged rank runs a long mixed step on most off-cadence steps while the other ranks, with nothing to prefill, run decode and then wait for it in the lockstep EP collectives. On DP8/EP8 + MTP1, 8x MI355X, PSI 8, chat-like 8k-class prompts at c=1024, 82% of wall time was in mixed steps (median 720 ms vs 81 ms decode-only), and 12-13% of all rank-time was spent waiting on another rank's prefill.

## Claims

- New `SchedulerConfig.prefill_release_min_dp_ranks` / `--prefill-release-min-dp-ranks K` (default 0 = off). With PSI > 1 and K > 0, off-cadence steps release prefills on every rank if at least K DP ranks have prefill work, and defer them on every rank otherwise, including capacity-bound ranks. Cadence steps are unchanged.
- The count is one CPU `SUM` all-reduce of an int32 over the DP group per step, in `_has_global_unfinished_reqs`. With K = 0 or PSI = 1 nothing changes and no collective is issued.
- On 8x MI355X: +10.5% tok/s/GPU at matched interactivity on chat-like prompts (out-of-tree equivalent, older vLLM), about +2% on random 8k/1k on main, with median TTFT at c1024 roughly halved on main. Scheduling only; gsm8k unchanged.

## Validation

Chat-like prompts, an equivalent out-of-tree patch on an older vLLM with our runtime stack, same node, PSI 8, `max_num_batched_tokens` 6144, 8k/1k-class, closed loop, 3×c prompts per rung. Total (input + output) tok/s/GPU @ tok/s/user (1000 / median TPOT):

| arm | c1024 | at 6.03 tok/s/user (interpolated) | median TTFT, c1024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| PSI 8, no gate | 6,535 @ 6.45 | ~6,658 | 10.2 s |
| K=4 | 6,705 @ 6.53 | dominated, stopped | |
| K=6 | 6,774 @ 6.67 | 6,980 (+4.8%) | 8.6 s |
| K=8 | 7,022 @ 7.12 | 7,355 (+10.5%) | 11.6-13.0 s |

K=8 replicate on a second node with other seeds: 7,328 at 6.03. With K=8, rank-time waiting on another rank's prefill fell from 16.3% to 2.8%. gsm8k on gated servers (5 runs, K=6/8): 0.948-0.954.

This branch on main `155488d853`, random 8192/1024 (not chat-like), `--api-server-count 1`, no out-of-tree runtime patches, two seeds per rung. On = `--prefill-release-min-dp-ranks 8`, off = flag omitted, same install (both arms also carry the companion DP load-balance PR):

| rung | on (seed 1 / seed 2) | off (seed 1 / seed 2) | throughput | interactivity | median TTFT on / off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c256 | 4,385 @ 20.47 / 4,356 @ 19.94 | 4,306 @ 21.56 / 4,159 @ 21.32 | +3.3% | -5.8% | 15.4, 13.4 s / 19.8, 21.7 s |
| c1024 | 5,530 @ 5.39 / 5,567 @ 5.40 | 5,447 @ 5.70 / 5,363 @ 5.45 | +2.7% | -3.2% | 18.0, 15.6 s / 35.0, 30.9 s |

At a fixed concurrency the gate trades interactivity for throughput. At matched interactivity (gated frontier c896 5,470 @ 6.10 and c1024 interpolated at the ungated points) the ungated runs are 1.2% and 3.2% below, about +2%. Acceptance length 1.99 in every run, no engine errors.

Unit tests (new): `test_dp_prefill_gate_counts_ranks_every_step` and `test_dp_prefill_gate_throttle_decision` (5 cases) in `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py`; `test_throttle_dp_global_gate_ignores_capacity_bound` and `test_has_prefill_work` in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`.

<details>
<summary>commands and output</summary>

Rebased on main `0ad6ec839`, CPU-only, offline host. `test_engine_core.py` skips on non-CUDA platforms and loads an HF tokenizer at import, so it ran from a local copy with those two lines removed. Selected: the new tests plus the existing throttle / `prefill_schedule_interval` / `dp_sync` / gating tests.

```
# with this change
19 passed, 265 deselected, 1 warning in 12.50s

# scheduler.py, interface.py and core.py reverted to main (config option kept)
FAILED tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_throttle_dp_global_gate_ignores_capacity_bound
FAILED tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_has_prefill_work - AttributeError...
FAILED tests/v1/engine/test_zz_core_copy.py::test_dp_prefill_gate_counts_ranks_every_step
FAILED tests/v1/engine/test_zz_core_copy.py::test_dp_prefill_gate_throttle_decision[4-4-9-False]
4 failed, 15 passed, 265 deselected, 1 warning in 12.62s
```

Full `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: 1 failure, `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, which also fails on main. ruff, typos, SPDX and mypy (3.11 hook) are clean.
</details>

## Details

**Where the count runs.** `_has_global_unfinished_reqs` is reached once per step by every rank with the same `step_counter`, including idle ranks. A first prototype all-reduced at the start of `_process_engine_step` and deadlocked at c=1024: an idle rank runs that method without reaching the step-end sync, so the gloo sequence shifted.

**Prefill work.** New `SchedulerInterface.has_prefill_work()`, defaulting to "any waiting request". `Scheduler` excludes blocked waiting requests and includes running requests still mid-prompt.

**Guards kept.** A rank with no decode work to protect never defers, so a throttled step is never an empty step. The scheduler ignores `prefill_capacity_bound` only when the gate is on.

**Why an integer.** At c1024, K=4 < K=6 < K=8 = dp_size. If K = dp_size is always best a boolean would do; we kept an integer for deployments with more skewed per-rank load, which we did not test.

**Not tested.** This branch alone on hardware (only stacked with our other open branches, above), a chat-like A/B on main, multi-node DP, `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` and elastic EP (the count uses the current `dp_group`, which elastic EP reinitializes). The per-step all-reduce cost was not measured separately; it is included in the numbers above.
