items.title: [Bugfix] MiniMax-M3: structured output silently ignored with thinking enabled (scheduler reasoning-end gate never fires)
items.body:
## Purpose

Structured output (`response_format: json_schema` / `json_object`) is **silently ignored** for MiniMax-M3 whenever thinking is enabled (`chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking_mode": "enabled"}`): the server returns HTTP 200 with unconstrained prose. Cause: the scheduler's structured-output gate can never observe the end of reasoning.

`StructuredOutputManager.should_advance` calls `is_reasoning_end_streaming` on its request-local parser. `MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end_streaming` early-returns `False` while `_reasoning_active_streaming` is set — but that flag is only ever cleared by `extract_reasoning_streaming`, a frontend/detokenizer method the scheduler never calls. With `thinking_mode: "enabled"` the flag initializes `True`, so:

- detection never fires → `reasoning_ended` never latches,
- `should_fill_bitmask` stays `False` forever → the grammar never engages,
- the request completes normally, making the failure invisible to clients.

Related failure family: #34650, #39130 (reasoning gates silently disabling structured output).

## Fix

Evaluate the reasoning-end predicate over the token history **before** the frontend streaming-state early return.

Two subtleties, both encoded in the regression tests:

1. **Ordering, not containment.** `input_ids` spans prompt+output, and the M3 chat template's `<thinking_instructions>` block embeds literal `<mm:think>` / `</mm:think>` text inside the prompt. A naive "history contains end marker" check fires at step 0, engaging the grammar immediately — which suppresses thinking entirely and (because no `</mm:think>` is ever emitted) makes the frontend parser classify the whole JSON as `reasoning`, leaving `content` empty. The correct predicate is `is_reasoning_end`'s ordering rule: last end marker *after* last start marker — the template's trailing `<mm:think>` prefill keeps it `False` until the model truly closes the block.
2. **Incremental scan.** The scheduler calls this per token; a full-history `rfind` per call is O(history) and measurable on long-context requests (M3 supports 1M). The parser now caches the last-seen marker positions and scans only unseen tokens (with a marker-length overlap), resetting if the sequence shrinks (fresh stream reusing the parser).

Frontend streaming extraction is unchanged — the state flags still gate the adaptive-mode heuristics; once a block truly ends, the marker check fires identically to before.

## Verification

- 28/28 parser unit tests, including 6 new regression tests: scheduler calling pattern (single-token deltas), spec-decode-style multi-token windows, **prompt-scaffolding marker text**, split-marker incremental scan, scan-cache reset, and **rejected-draft cache poisoning** (second commit: cached marker positions are re-verified against the current tokens, since the bitmask path probes with simulated sequences containing scheduled draft tokens — a rejected marker draft must not end reasoning; observed live at ~1/15 structured requests under batched EAGLE3 load before the fix, 45/45 clean after). The scheduler-pattern, scaffolding, and rejected-draft tests fail on the unpatched parser.
- Live end-to-end on a production TP8 B300 deployment (v0.25.1 overlay) serving MiniMax-M3 with EAGLE3 speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens: 3`): before the fix, 10/10 `thinking + json_schema` requests returned unconstrained markdown; with this fix (combined with the pre-commit boundary filter — see note), 10/10 returned schema-valid JSON in `content` with genuine reasoning in `reasoning`, streaming and tool calling intact, spec decode confirmed active via `/metrics`.

## Note on speculative decoding

This fix makes the boundary *detectable*; under spec decode the boundary step can still commit post-marker tokens sampled before the mask engaged. #43424's pre-commit grammar filter handles that leak — the two compose (without this fix, that filter can never trigger for MiniMax-M3, since detection is what arms it). On v0.25.1-era code we also needed the exact boundary index stored at pre-commit time; on main, #43388's `new_token_ids`-based window in `should_advance` already provides the equivalent.

Happy to add the observed-but-preexisting cleanup separately: `accept_tokens` logs `ERROR ... Please file an issue` for draft-token rejections that the reasoning-boundary bitmask path explicitly tolerates — a dry-run `validate_tokens` in that path would silence expected noise.

items.title: [Feature][AuxOutput] Add Profile-based indexer replay for sparse models
items.body:
## Overview

Extend the raw Indexer Replay foundation in #49555 with Profile-described sparse
selection formats and model-specific adapters. Implements the remaining formats
from #47280 and depends on #49555; merge that PR first.

## Claims

- Describe model identity, producer/consumer layer mappings, selection semantics,
  fixed storage widths and codec versions in `AuxOutputProfile`.
- Add DeepSeek V4.1 compressed coordinates, GLM-5.3 KPool, Qwen4Exp QSA,
  Step5 per-KV-group regions and HY-V4 model hooks.
- Add lossless Pool/QSA decoding and optional packed delivery with profile
  metadata. Keep the raw `indexer_topk` API supported for uniform decoded shapes.

These are implementation claims; real model/backend correctness is not yet validated.

## Validation

Ruff check/format on all changed Python files and diff whitespace checks pass.
The complete implementation was preserved before splitting, then restored on top
of the raw foundation. The generic SHM budget helper stays in the base memory module;
no additional scheduler, request lifecycle or SHM writer is introduced here. Routed rows, Indexer rows and their metadata are extracted in one call using shared row/range validation; focused mypy on the shared artifact buffer, capturer and connector/worker also passes.

Per user instruction, pytest, model evaluation, GPU/H20 E2E, synchronization and
performance tests remain deferred. Full pre-commit/mypy and Rust fmt/build/test
have not passed or were not completed in this environment; automatic commit
hooks are skipped. Historical results from the old slot-based PR do not apply.

After human review, run:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_indexer_capture.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/ tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py
python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py
pre-commit run --files <changed-files>
```

## Details

This is a planned dependent split of #49555, not a competing implementation.
Duplicate checks read #47280/comments and open related Indexer Replay PRs. The
base PR now contains ordinary raw-int32 replay; this PR adds formats that
need metadata to interpret, expand or group their selections.

DeepSeek V4's ordinary raw C4A capture is already in #49555. This follow-up
adds optional Profile metadata to that existing adapter; it does not introduce
the V4 capture path. Compression of KV coordinates alone needs no replay codec.

**Review only this second part:**
[incremental comparison](https://github.com/Ronald1995/vllm/compare/indexer-topk...codex/indexer-profile-models).
GitHub requires this upstream PR to target `main` because the upstream repository
does not contain the fork's `indexer-topk` branch. Its Files changed therefore
includes the prerequisite until #49555 merges. Rebase after that merge before
requesting maintainer review. Do not merge this PR first.

Profiles distinguish token IDs, compressed-cache coordinates, ordered Pool/Block
selections, count columns, causal tails and grouped Region IDs. Packed mode avoids
expansion through HTTP; raw mode decodes on final output assembly. Heterogeneous
source shapes require packed output. AMD QSA keeps its raw selection format.
V4.1's decoder replay retains capture rows when Indexer is the only AuxOutput.

Current AuxOutput PP/DCP/PCP, adaptive-verification and remote-PD restrictions
remain. MiniMax-M3 has been audited but has no adapter. Rust receives the engine
wire fields; Rust HTTP delivery remains unsupported. GPU graphs, real TP/DP,
model quality and overhead need later evidence. SHM retains immutable first-writer
semantics. See `docs/training/indexer_replay.md` for format and usage details.

Shared SHM block buffering, keys, publication and materialization live in artifacts.py and use generic AuxOutput names. Preemption uses the existing deferred request teardown to clear temporary blocks before resumption. Capture follows the model execution contract; row snapshots carry no per-token/source write-validity bitmap. Capture hooks are guarded by actual scoring execution, and existing forced-scoring settings for replay on short dense prefills are retained.

Scheduler and EngineCoreOutput use indexer_topk consistently with frontend output assembly and Rust engine IPC; the positional wire field order is preserved.

AI assistance was used. The human submitter must review every changed line and
run/accept validation before requesting maintainer review or claiming verified support.

items.title: [Spec Decode] Add D-cut: Adaptive Verification Depth Pruning for Batched Speculative Decoding
items.body: ## Purpose This PR adds **D-Cut**, a confidence-based draft-pruning policy for the DFlash parallel drafter, that trims the per-step draft width *after* drafting and *before* target verification. By dropping low-confidence draft tokens, it cuts the number of tokens the target model must verify per step while keeping acceptance length almost unchanged — improving TPOT and end-to-end throughput, especially at higher batch sizes and on harder prompts where the draft is less likely to be accepted. D-Cut is disabled by default (`dflash_dcut=0`); existing DFlash behavior is unchanged unless the option is set. The implementation is small and contained — **+367/-12 across 7 files** (only 12 lines of existing code touched), plus a ~270-line test file. The technique is documented by the AngelSlim team: . ### Why this is not a duplicate of existing dynamic-SD work Dynamic speculative-decoding work in flight operates on **autoregressive** drafters and decides *before/during* drafting: - **DSL (#35301)** early-exits the draft loop at a confidence threshold — requires a step-by-step drafter to "stop early". - **DSD (#32374 family, e.g. #45953, #45963, #46399)** picks the runtime draft length `k` from batch size *before* drafting. DFlash is a **parallel** drafter: it emits all `num_speculative_tokens` in one shot, so there is no draft loop to exit early and no per-step `k` to lower. D-Cut targets exactly that gap — it prunes the already-produced draft based on per-token confidence, reducing **target-side verification** cost rather than draft-side compute. The `auto` policy selects how many drafts to keep per batch size from a warmup-profiled cost table, which none of the above provide. This PR **reuses** the DSD compatibility scaffolding (the `_maybe_override_dynamic_sd_cudagraph_mode` full→piecewise fallback and the v2-unsupported-features list) rather than conflicting with it. ## Design Three policies, selected by a single `dflash_dcut` field on `SpeculativeConfig`: | `dflash_dcut` | Policy | Behavior | |---|---|---| | `0` (default) | `off` | No pruning; standard DFlash. | | float in `(0, 1]` | `fixed_ratio` | Keep a fixed fraction of target-forward query tokens (global top-K by draft score). **Hardware-independent.** | | `"auto"` | `selector` | Keep length chosen at runtime from a warmup full-cost table. **Hardware-dependent.** | The pipeline is intentionally split into a **method-agnostic** transport/apply path and a **DFlash-specific** selection path, so the option can later be extended to other parallel-drafting methods: 1. **Select** (DFlash proposer): from the draft logprobs, compute per-request keep lengths. For `fixed_ratio` the budget is `ceil(value * batch_size * (num_draft + 1)) - batch_size`; `auto` looks the batch size up in a cost table profiled during warmup. 2. **Transport**: keep lengths ride on `DraftTokenIds.dcut_keep_lens`. 3. **Apply** (scheduler): truncate each request's spec tokens to its keep length (the reserved bonus token is always retained), and record kept vs. total draft tokens. 4. **Observe**: `SpecDecodingStats`/`SpecDecodingLogging` report a D-Cut keep ratio alongside the existing acceptance metrics. ### Compatibility D-Cut runs on the V1 model runner with piecewise CUDA graphs. To avoid silent misconfiguration it is gated the same way dynamic SD is: - **Async scheduling**: hard-errors if explicitly enabled, otherwise disabled with a warning (async SD currently assumes a fixed draft width). - **CUDA graphs**: full-graph mode falls back to piecewise (reusing the existing dynamic-SD override). - **Model Runner V2**: listed as an unsupported feature so config resolution falls back to V1. ### Usage ```bash # auto policy (recommended): keep length chosen from a profiled cost table vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash", "model":"", "num_speculative_tokens":7, "dflash_dcut":"auto"}' # fixed-ratio policy: keep ~50% of the draft width vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash", "model":"", "num_speculative_tokens":7, "dflash_dcut":0.5}' ``` Setting `dflash_dcut=0` (default) restores standard DFlash. ## Benchmark **Setup.** 5 target models (dense + MoE), 5 datasets, greedy decoding, 8×H20, serving concurrency swept {4,8,16,32,64}, results reported at **concurrency 32**. The primary metric is **output-token throughput speedup over autoregressive (AR) decoding** — under batched serving a longer draft raises mean accepted tokens (τ) but also enlarges the verification batch, so a higher τ does not necessarily mean higher throughput. `D-Cut (16)` is the `auto` policy on a block-16 drafter; `DFlash (16)` is the same drafter with no pruning. D-Cut keeps **92% of DFlash's τ on average** (85–97%) — it trims the low-confidence tail, not the useful prefix — so the throughput gains below come almost free of accepted-length loss. Speedup vs. AR (AR = 1.00× reference; higher is better; **bold** = best per row). Averaged over the 5 datasets: | Model | EAGLE-3 / MTP † | DFlash (16) | D-Cut (16) | |---|---|---|---| | Llama-3.1-8B | 1.03× | 0.67× | **1.12×** | | Qwen3-4B | 1.29× | 0.98× | **1.35×** | | Qwen3-8B | 1.11× | 0.80× | **1.21×** | | Qwen3.5-27B | **1.31×** | 0.94× | 1.25× | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (MoE) | 1.75× | 2.36× | **2.50×** | † EAGLE-3 for Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen3-4B / Qwen3-8B; MTP for the Qwen3.5 models. `D-Cut (16)` is the `auto` policy on a block-16 drafter; `DFlash (16)` is the same drafter unpruned. D-Cut beats unpruned DFlash on average throughput for **every** model, and beats the EAGLE-3/MTP baseline on 4 of 5. ### Scaling with concurrency The figure below shows absolute output-token throughput as concurrency grows 4→64 (rows = datasets, columns = models; green = D-Cut, blue = DFlash; solid = block-16, dashed = block-8). Throughput rises with concurrency for both, but they diverge at the high end: on dense targets DFlash (16) gains the least from batching (verifying long drafts cancels the accepted-token benefit), while D-Cut sustains the highest throughput, with the gap widening as load grows. Under **temperature-1 sampling** (Qwen3-8B, H20), stochastic decoding shortens accepted drafts and penalizes long fixed-depth proposals: DFlash falls below AR at high concurrency, while D-Cut (auto) sustains a 1.15× speedup over AR (1.68× relative to DFlash — a *larger* relative gain than under greedy decoding, since harsher sampling leaves more low-utility suffix to prune). ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dcut.py -v ``` 26 unit tests covering: keep-count arithmetic and bonus-token accounting, `dflash_dcut_mode` derivation and config validation (including the non-`dflash` method gate), keep-ratio stats accumulation/logging, and the scheduler-side truncation. All pure-logic (no GPU). ## Test Result - `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dcut.py`: **26 passed**. - End-to-end on H20 (Qwen3-4B + DFlash-B16, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, `dflash_dcut=auto`, piecewise CUDA graph, prefix-cache and async scheduling disabled): server boots, warmup cost table builds, inference correct, and the D-Cut keep-ratio metric is reported in the SpecDecoding logs. The three compatibility gates (async, cudagraph, MRv2) trigger as designed. - Benchmark numbers above collected on H20. --- *AI assistance was used in preparing this change (code migration, test authoring, and this description). All changes have been reviewed line-by-line and validated end-to-end on GPU by the submitter.*

items.title: [Feature][KVConnector][DSv4.1] Encoder-only prefill with Mooncake P/D
items.body:
## Purpose

Implement encoder-only Prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D serving with the direct `MooncakeConnector`, following the asymmetric P/D design in RFC #57383 and the full-prompt cache-hit replay design in RFC #57738.

P executes through the L20 pre-mix boundary and produces the transferable Main KV and Indexer K. D receives those regions, replays the bounded tail through the full target, and samples the first token.

## Implementation

This PR is intentionally split into two commits:

1. `13d89a71d0` - feature implementation and streamlined tests
   - Adds `KVTransferConfig.dsv41_encoder_only_prefill` for dedicated Mooncake producer and consumer roles.
   - Adds the V4.1 execution boundary, explicit transfer profile, cache-only zero-token P completion, GPU completion event, request validation, and proxy `cache_only` handoff.
   - P runs L0-L19 plus the L20 pre-mix and canonical Main-KV/Indexer-K writes, then skips L20 attention/FFN, L21-L39, final norm, LM head, sampling, and DSpark.
   - D keeps bounded-replay state and DSpark state local. The validated D path supports DSpark K5 adaptive verification and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs.

2. `8d5b2b21c9` - Mooncake release-only pull fix
   - Bounded replay can discard a short remote hit while Mooncake still needs to release the producer blocks.
   - An empty pull has no local blocks and the consumer never enters `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. This commit releases the producer blocks without reporting a receive completion to the scheduler.

The current boundary is direct `MooncakeConnector`, NVIDIA, model runner V2, PP=1, no PCP or microbatching, SWA bounded replay with a 128-token window, the 40-layer V4.1-Flash topology, text-only requests, and no prompt logprobs. P requires `--no-async-scheduling` and must not configure a speculator.

## Validation

### Latest-main rebase (2026-09-29)

Rebased onto `05d89636fc`. On macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, the focused model-boundary, cache-only, scheduler, config, and Mooncake tests passed (18 passed):

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu /Users/bytedance/Opensource/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_encoder_only_prefill.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_cache_only_prefill.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_dsv41_cache_only_prefill_finishes_without_sampling \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_profile_transfers_global_groups_only \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_profile_rejects_missing_or_mixed_global_state \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_cache_only_runner_waits_for_kv_writes_before_output \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_handoff_requires_bounded_replay \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_handoff_separates_producer_compile_hash \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_handoff_rejects_unsupported_config \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py::test_encoder_only_cache_ready_triggers_mooncake_transfer \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py::test_encoder_only_mooncake_rejects_extra_consumer_cache_regions
```

`uvx ruff check` and `uvx ruff format --check` passed on all 21 changed Python files; `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. The upstream CUDA replay-batch suite could not be collected on this CPU-only machine because it allocates CUDA tensors at import time. The H20 serving and GSM8K measurements below were taken on the earlier nightly and have not been rerun on this rebased head.

### Environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa`
- Hardware: two nodes, each with 8 NVIDIA H20 96 GB GPUs; one node for P and one for D
- Mooncake: 0.3.13.post1 over RDMA
- Baseline: the fixed nightly plus the release-only fix (tested with commit `50dcc87d1c`)
- Candidate: the same nightly with both PR commits

The baseline used conventional Mooncake P/D. Because D used DSpark K5, baseline P also used static DSpark K5 (`enable_adaptive_verification=false`) to keep the registered cache groups aligned. Candidate P did not load DSpark; candidate D used DSpark K5 adaptive verification. Decode used TP1 + DP8 + EP8 and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. DeepEP was disabled: neither arm set `--all2all-backend`, and both selected the default `AgRsAll2AllManager` at runtime.

### Server and router commands

```bash
# Prefill (candidate)
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 \
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=600 \
VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998 \
vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
```

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Preserve grammar-invalid drafts for rejection sampling
items.body:
Co-author: @tomasruizt 
Based on https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/pull/18

## Overview

Fixes output distribution shift under spec decode + structured outputs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60451

Architecture overview at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62818.

Alternative to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60690.

## Claims

Fixes the issue with minor performance gains on the async scheduling path (~2%) and a ~2% regression on the sync path.

## Validation

Correctness:

Most direct validation is `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_distribution_shift.py`, which mirrors the issue's setup.
- Sample 4000 samples with the same prompt and regex grammar but with spec decode on vs off
- Compare the sampled distributions
- Distributions differ significantly on main but don't on this branch

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py   \
       tests/v1/structured_output   \
       tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py

501 passed, 2 xfailed, 56 warnings in 237.92s (0:03:57)

pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_distribution_shift.py   \
       tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/   \
       -k "not dflash2"

9 passed, 1 deselected, 19 warnings in 996.13s (0:16:36)
```

Performance:

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e550d5fb57af73372f57dc0c7c5e694b

`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark` + 15 draft tokens + adaptive verification
Run on 1 H100 80GB

```
.venv/bin/python run.py --output ./bench_res/... --num-repeats 10
```

Results report throughput in tokens/s.
- sync vs async scheduling
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c96: low vs high concurrency
- brackets report 95% confidence intervals

| Case | main | #60690 | this |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sync / broad / c1 | 536.0 [518.8, 553.2] | 526.1 [510.7, 541.6] -1.85% | 524.8 [513.4, 536.2] -2.09% |
| sync / broad / c96 | 10,375.9 [10,349.6, 10,402.1] | 10,161.8 [10,125.0, 10,198.6] -2.06% | 10,176.5 [10,149.4, 10,203.6] -1.92% |
| sync / tight / c1 | 856.9 [823.4, 890.4] | 858.6 [847.6, 869.6] +0.20% | 857.3 [837.8, 876.7] +0.04% |
| sync / tight / c96 | 17,539.1 [17,483.4, 17,594.7] | 17,089.6 [17,026.4, 17,152.9] -2.56% | 17,062.5 [17,007.0, 17,118.0] -2.72% |
| async / broad / c1 | 669.0 [667.4, 670.6] | 663.5 [662.0, 665.0] -0.83% | 666.9 [664.8, 668.9] -0.32% |
| async / broad / c96 | 10,017.3 [10,003.0, 10,031.5] | 9,969.8 [9,908.9, 10,030.7] -0.47% | 10,358.9 [10,340.3, 10,377.5] +3.41% |
| async / tight / c1 | 1,081.6 [1,077.5, 1,085.6] | 1,082.8 [1,077.4, 1,088.2] +0.12% | 1,078.3 [1,077.3, 1,079.2] -0.31% |
| async / tight / c96 | 17,066.4 [17,020.3, 17,112.5] | 16,862.1 [16,622.7, 17,101.6] -1.20% | 17,462.7 [17,411.0, 17,514.5] +2.32% |

## Details

`StructuredOutputManager` changes (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`)
- Rename `validate_tokens` to `trim_spec_tokens`; no longer trim the rejected invalid token
- Allow `grammar_bitmask` to handle unvalidated draft tokens; previously, all draft tokens were already validated by `validate_tokens`

Scheduling changes (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`):
- Remove the `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` call on the async scheduling path

`StructuredOutputGrammar` changes:
- Ensure `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` is atomic on failure: when it returns False (acceptance fails), grammar state is not updated
- Allow `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` to call `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` with unvalidated draft tokens, without an extra `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` call
- Update to XGrammar backend to rollback accepted tokens when `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` fails
- Update to Guidance backend to use `ll_matcher.try_consume_tokens` + rollback vs `ll_matcher.consume_tokens` to not advance matcher state when `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` fails

`EngineCore` changes:
- Comment update only

items.title: [Feature][AuxOutput] Replay ordinary raw indexer selections
items.body:
## Overview

Return ordinary sparse-attention TopK selections through the existing
AuxOutput SHM lifecycle. This is the raw-int32 foundation for #47280; the
Profile/Codec and model-specific formats are split into a dependent PR.

Follow-up: #62915 adds the Profile-described model formats and must merge later.

## Claims

- Capture raw int32 token IDs from DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5.2 and the shared
  reference MLA path, with source planes ordered by actual layer IDs.
- Capture DeepSeek V4's raw C4A TopK compressed-cache indices without a codec
  or expansion to original token positions. HCA/SWA layers add no source planes.
- Reuse AuxOutput hashes, async copies, accepted-token cursors, prefix
  restoration and cleanup; support Indexer-only or combined routed experts.
- Query system/cgroup RAM before allocating SHM, budget all local artifacts,
  and report a GPU KV block limit with concrete configuration advice on failure.
- Return only `indexer_topk`; no Profile, packed output, Pool/QSA/Region codec
  is included here. Compressed coordinates alone do not require a Profile.

These are implementation claims pending behavioral and model validation.

## Validation

Ruff check/format of all changed Python files and `git diff --check` pass.
The split changes the internal raw layout to `[tokens, sources, topk]`; capture,
worker, scheduler, output/HTTP and existing regression fixtures were updated
together. Static audit found no remaining Profile imports or wire fields.
The memory-budget module, shared artifact buffer, capturer and connector/worker also pass focused mypy with
`--follow-imports=skip --ignore-missing-imports`. The CI test-tethering static
check passes; existing Distributed Comm Ops steps now select the AuxOutput suite.

Per the user's instruction, pytest, model evaluation, GPU/H20 E2E and performance
checks remain deferred. Historical tests of the old slot-based PR do not validate
this implementation. Full pre-commit/mypy and Rust fmt/build/test are not passing
or were not completed in this environment; commits skip automatic hooks.

After human review, run:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_indexer_capture.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/ tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py
pre-commit run --files <changed-files>
```

## Details

Indexer capture now uses an explicit source capability and a standalone binder
for discovery, layout validation and sink binding; the capturer owns storage and
snapshot allocation. Existing MLA prefix/TopK metadata is reused, fused V3.2/V4
supply metadata through their common classes, and MTP/shared consumers remain
excluded. Allocation/binding stays in model loading before KV capacity planning
and compilation. The existing CPU suite adds binding and lifecycle coverage;
these new tests remain unexecuted under the user's validation deferral.

This updates the existing #49555 rather than opening a duplicate. Open PRs
mentioning #47280 and Indexer Replay were checked. The follow-up adds distinct
Profile/Codec model semantics and depends on this foundation; it must merge later.

All enabled artifacts share row-count and accepted-range validation in one scheduler extraction call, with independent prompt offsets. Disabled routed output uses None rather than placeholder rows.

The raw capture supports uniform TopK widths, preserving order and invalid IDs.
IndexCache consumers reuse the plane determined by their model configuration.
Dots3 NOTE's overridden forward and sparse GLM4-MoE-Lite's reference MLA share
this raw-token path. V4's raw fixed-width selections share the same path.
V4.1, GLM-5.3 KPool, Qwen QSA, Step5 and HY-V4 are moved
to the follow-up. MiniMax-M3 still has no adapter.

Startup admission covers R3-only as well as Indexer/combined modes: the arena
must cover all KV blocks. It uses current host/cgroup headroom, local DP worker
count, staging and estimated metadata/reserve, then rounds down to complete hash
objects to infer the supported KV block count. An oversized explicit arena needs
`max_bytes` resized/unset as well as any GPU block change. Suggestions use
`--num-gpu-blocks-override N`; no RAM-to-GPU-utilization ratio is guessed.
The admission check is an estimate, not an atomic memory reservation.

MRV2 generate and prefix caching are required. Existing AuxOutput restrictions
on PP/DCP/PCP, adaptive verification and remote PD remain. Rust engine IPC keeps
the raw field; Rust HTTP delivery is not implemented. SHM retains immutable
first-writer semantics. See `docs/training/indexer_replay.md` for use and limits.

Shared SHM block buffering, keys, publication and materialization live in artifacts.py and use generic AuxOutput names. Preemption uses the existing deferred request teardown to clear temporary blocks before resumption. Capture follows the model execution contract; row snapshots carry no per-token/source write-validity bitmap. Capture hooks are guarded by actual scoring execution, and existing forced-scoring settings for replay on short dense prefills are retained.

Scheduler and EngineCoreOutput use indexer_topk consistently with frontend output assembly and Rust engine IPC; the positional wire field order is preserved.

AI assistance was used. The human submitter must review every changed line and
run/accept relevant validation before requesting maintainer review.

---
