items.title: [Spec Decode] Context-length-aware K in DSD (RFC #48627): extend num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size with a ctx axis
items.body:
**Status: on hold pending further validation.**

## What the measurement actually shows

The 2026-07-27 campaign measured four arms, and my [earlier comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48944#issuecomment-5091663057) published all four. What it did not do is carry the static K=3 comparison into the verdict, which was written against A′ alone. All four arms, in output tokens/s, mean of six runs per cell:

| configured prefix len | no-spec | static K=3 | A′ (3-item batch-only) | C′ (6-cell 2D) |
|-----:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 400 | 2711.7 | **2139.8** | 1875.6 | 1890.7 |
| 900 | 1987.1 | 1838.9 | 1453.5 | 1874.6 |
| 1900 | 1815.2 | 1822.4 | 1416.6 | 1848.2 |
| 4000 | 1535.9 | **1692.8** | 1232.8 | 1680.4 |

Against A′, C′ is 1.01× / 1.29× / 1.30× / 1.36×, and that contrast was pre-registered before measurement. Against **static K=3** — `[[1,512,3]]`, no context axis at all — C′ is −11.64% / +1.94% / +1.42% / −0.73%.

**A performance advantage from adding the context axis is not established by this campaign** — which is a failure to establish one, not a demonstration that the axis has no effect. The pre-registered criterion was a throughput-ratio rule against A′, and it was met. It said nothing about static K=3, which is the comparison that matters for whether the extra config surface and scheduler logic buy anything. On this data, that question is unanswered. An earlier version of this body reported the A′ ratios as the result without this control.

Two things worth separating:

- **The hypothesis** — that the favourable K can differ with context at the same batch size — is open and still interesting to me.
- **The case for this implementation** — that routing K on context beats a well-chosen batch-only or static policy — is not supported by this experiment.

Schema expressiveness alone is not a reason to add a config surface upstream, so I am not arguing from it.

<details>
<summary>Arms, setup, and what the numbers do and do not license</summary>

```
A′        [[1,64,3], [65,128,1], [129,512,0]]
C′        [[1,64,1,768,3],   [1,64,769,32768,3],
           [65,128,1,768,1], [65,128,769,32768,1],
           [129,512,1,768,0],[129,512,769,32768,3]]
static K3 [[1,512,3]]
```

A′ selects K=0 in the 129–512 batch tier, which covers the run's nominal concurrency, but it is not a non-speculating arm: `num_prompts=256` with `max_concurrency=256` is a finite batch whose scheduled size passes through the lower, drafting tiers on ramp-up and drain. Draft tokens over the six runs: A′ 1,243 / 1,720 / 5,748 / 10,183, C′ 1,234 / 190,858 / 190,984 / 179,854, static K=3 197,043 / 202,695 / 208,644 / 190,812.

Setup: position-balanced 2 trials, autotune cache wiped per launch, cold-start burn, 3 warmup runs discarded and 3 kept per cell per trial. `vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-prefix-len <N> --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 96 --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 1 --prefix-repetition-output-len 100 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 256 --ignore-eos`. Target `prithivMLmods/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-FP8`, draft `google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized-assistant`, H100 NVL 94GB, driver 580.82.09, CUDA 13.0, vLLM `c5d967c23`, `--max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90`.

Lengths: the table's left column is the configured prefix length. Observed per-request input lengths were 496 / 996 / 1996 / 4096 and the output length was 100. I did not record the per-step `num_computed_tokens` the scheduler reduced over.

Dispersion: coefficient of variation over the six runs per cell is C′ 1.19% / 1.90% / 1.70% / 1.74%, static K=3 1.31% / 1.16% / 1.58% / 1.53%, A′ 1.18% / 1.10% / 1.02% / 0.53%, no-spec 0.94% / 0.41% / 0.36% / 0.52%. This is observed spread, not an equivalence test, and it supersedes the dispersion figures in my earlier comment, which reproduce under neither the per-trial nor the pooled definition.

Against no-spec, C′ reaches 1.02× and 1.09× at prefix 1900 and 4000; static K=3 reaches about 1.00× and 1.10× at the same points. I previously presented the C′ row as independent support for the context axis. It is not, and I am not reading it as a general property of K=3 either.

DSD-mode arms sit below no-spec at prefix 400. Server logs show the DSD arms ran with `PIECEWISE` while no-spec retained full graphs; the contribution of that difference to the gap was not isolated. This predates the context axis and applies to the 3-item API from #32374 too. Tracked in #49986.

Raw per-run data, the aggregation method, and these limits: https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/tree/main/pr48944_replication

</details>

## What the change is

An optional context-length axis on the Dynamic SD schedule (#32374), as a backward-compatible schema extension. A 3-item entry `[bs_lo, bs_hi, K]` preserves the existing K-selection semantics; a 5-item entry `[bs_lo, bs_hi, ctx_lo, ctx_hi, K]` opts in. I am not claiming the execution cost of a 3-item schedule is unchanged — that has not been measured. K is chosen once per scheduler step, not per request: the scheduler reduces `num_computed_tokens` over the scheduled requests to one representative and indexes `dense[batch_size][ctx_bucket]`. The config field is renamed `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size` → `speculative_token_schedule`, with the old name kept as a deprecated alias.

## Local work that is not pushed

The submitted HEAD is unchanged. Three commits exist only locally: they finish the rename at the two CUDA graph call sites (where a stale field name would raise on a real `SpeculativeConfig`), remove the `ctx_agg` option in favour of a fixed mean, and skip the context reduction when a schedule normalizes to a single bucket. A CPU-only test run at that local HEAD shows no failure that is not also present at the merge-base. They are cleanup and change nothing above, so they are being held rather than pushed.

## What would change my mind

Compare several K values at the same batch size to find where the favourable K actually differs with context, build a schedule from that, and evaluate it on a workload that was not used to choose it, against a strong batch-only baseline. If there is no difference there, this implementation should be closed.

## References

- RFC #48627 — the proposal; its performance conclusions are being corrected alongside this body
- PR #32374 — original DSD API (ekagra-ranjan)
- #49986 — DSD baseline tax, follow-up
- MagicDec (Sadhukhan et al., 2024) — *"we propose choosing the amount of speculation as a function of the sequence length"* ([blog](https://infini-ai-lab.github.io/MagicDec-part1/), under *Adaptive Sequoia trees*; the quote is not in [arXiv:2408.11049](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11049))

## AI assistance

This contribution is AI-assisted. An AI coding assistant (Anthropic Claude) wrote the code and tests, ran the CPU test run described above, re-aggregated the raw benchmark results into the table above, and drafted this text. I set the direction, made the design and framing decisions, and am responsible for every claim here. Filing this disclosure per vLLM's `AGENTS.md`.

items.title: [6/N] HiSparse: support direct GPU landing for P/D transfers
items.body:
## Why

HiSparse P/D imports always land in the host tier today. That costs a host round trip even when the decoder has room to keep the whole prefix on GPU. This PR lands a NIXL import directly in resident GPU pages when it fits, and falls back to the host tier otherwise.

## Design

- **Landing choice:** `HiSparseCoordinator` tries GPU landing first. If that admission fails, the retry uses the host tier and keeps it. There is no length threshold, and the generic KV cache manager is unaware of the choice.
- **NIXL alias regions:** NIXL registers each source layer's resident pages as a local-only *alias region* of that layer's host source region. Aliases are not advertised in the handshake.
  - A GPU import sends its resident blocks as `ReqMeta.alias_block_ids`. The existing region-mapped pull then writes those regions into their aliases, and the mixed DRAM/VRAM split still applies.
  - A host import is unchanged from `main`.
- **Review follow-up:** this replaces `HiSparseNixlDestination`, which re-implemented NIXL's host registration, descriptor mapping and read submission ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55398#pullrequestreview-5190836165)). NIXL no longer has a second host path; the only HiSparse-specific input is the source-to-resident layer map from `vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`.
- **Not supported with aliases** (each raises `NotImplementedError`): host staging buffers, Mamba, layer-name routing, kernel block size ≠ logical block size, DCP, and more than one source rank.

## Validation

CPU unit tests (Mac; NIXL suite on H100 because it needs `ray`):
```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  --deselect tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py::test_fewer_blocks_with_hma
```
All pass. `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[gemma]` hangs on that H100 box on `main` too.
- `test_nixl_hisparse_gpu_import_pulls_into_resident_pages` registers a real worker and checks that a GPU import's NIXL read targets resident-page addresses. It fails if the alias remap is removed.
- Two scheduler tests cover GPU landing (alias IDs past the local prefix) and host fallback (source pages, no alias IDs).

**Tiny-model P/D, 1×H100.** DeepSeek-V3.2 with 8 layers and dummy weights. Prefill and decode share the GPU. Greedy, 48 tokens, prompts of 200–3000 tokens. Compared against a HiSparse-only, non-P/D server.

| Decoder pool | Path taken | Matches non-P/D |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 blocks | 5/5 GPU landing | 5/5 (48/48 tokens) |
| 800 blocks, concurrent | 4 GPU, 1 host fallback | 5/5 (48/48 tokens) |

0 failed NIXL transfers. The path taken was confirmed with a probe on `prepare_gpu_import`.

**GLM-5.3 FP8, 2×8 H200, earlier revision `431cf98763`.** That revision used `HiSparseNixlDestination`.
- Setup: prefill TP8 with no HiSparse; decode TP8 with HiSparse, 384 GiB host pool and 16384 GPU blocks; FP8 KV, eager.
- 8K/32K/60K needle-in-haystack retrieval over P/D: correct.
- `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` did not reproduce: 0 failed transfers over ~150 requests.

Decode TTFT, median of 18 sequential requests each:

| Prompt | `main` (host) | PR | Path on PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 0.210 s | 0.198 s | GPU |
| 32K | 0.335 s | 0.288 s (−14%) | GPU |
| 60K | 0.490 s | 0.499 s | host fallback (does not fit) |

TPOT is unchanged at ~144 ms.

**Fixed: garbled answers after GPU-landed imports.** That revision garbled two 60K answers deterministically under a fixed request history; `main` was clean.
- Cause: the default eager host mirror only records page write-backs as complete, but rows NIXL writes into resident pages were never mirrored. Those pages were still published as host prefix-cache entries, so a later request with a one-page prefix hit read an unwritten host page.
- Fix: the NIXL scheduler records the pages a GPU import writes, and those pages' write-backs now copy to host (`SparseKVPageTransfer.unmirrored`).
- Minimal repro (fresh decoder): three 32K needles that land on GPU, then the 61,193-token seed-10 60K needle.
- With the fix, the full 77-request history replay passes 77/77, including both previously garbled prompts.
- That replay ran on an equivalent fix that recorded the import from `HiSparseSourceManager`. The pushed version records it from the NIXL scheduler instead, leaving `vllm/v1/core` unchanged for this fix. A GLM rerun of the pushed head is pending.

AI assistance was used; the submitter reviews every changed line.

items.title: [DSpark] Support PP prefill with KV transfer (disaggregated serving)
items.body:
## What

DSpark pipeline-parallel support, end to end: **aggregated (in-flight-batching) serving with PP targets** and **prefill on a pipeline-parallel producer with KV transfer** (PD-disaggregated serving).

This PR is self-contained: it re-applies #56956 (reverted in #58484 for further streamlining) and builds the PD producer path on top. Happy to iterate on the streamlining with you, @njhill.

Aggregated IFB PP (re-applied #56956):

- `PPHandler` broadcasts the last rank's sampled tokens (and draft tokens, for spec decode) to earlier stages on a side stream; earlier stages apply them `pp_size` steps later in a deferred post-update.
- The deferred post-update Triton kernel is pre-compiled during warmup with the exact serving specialization (int32 `idx_mapping`, 16-byte-aligned `num_sampled`/`num_rejected` via a padded combined buffer) — a mid-serving compile there would deadlock on the in-flight broadcast NCCL kernel.
- DSv4 router: pad the top-k buffer so non-last stages can drop EAGLE read-ahead rows.

PD prefill-only producer (this PR on top):

- `SpeculativeConfig.target_kv_transfer_config` + `is_dspark_prefill_only()`; NIXL is rejected for this mode (it cannot describe packed per-layer KV regions; Mooncake works).
- The scheduler narrows `use_eagle` (and eagle block-drop) for the prefill-only producer so it never does the EAGLE-style read-ahead.
- `DFlashSpeculator.materialize_context_kv()`: precompute and store draft context KV without drafting. `propose()` delegates to it when `is_dspark_prefill_only()` and returns `None`, so the model runner keeps its single call site unchanged and only skips the draft-side subsystems on the producer (rejection sampler, drafter graph capture, EPLB registration, draft-token handler) via one `dspark_prefill_only` flag. The preparation half is shared with `propose()` via `_prepare_draft_inputs()`; on the aggregated path the context-K/V store stays graph-aware as introduced by #57632 (merged here), while the producer stores eagerly (it captures no draft graph).
- The DSv4 draft in this mode builds only the attention submodule needed for prefill (`context_kv_only`) — avoiding transient MoE expert allocation — and loads just the context-KV weights (the merged `context_wkv_proj` plus per-layer `kv_norm`).

Kimi-K3 DSpark additionally relies on the TritonMLA causal multi-token fix from #51065 (merged; included in this branch's base; verified on SM120).

Split from #53577 (reviewer request).

## Tests

- `tests/config/test_dspark_prefill_only.py` (13 tests: mode detection, connector guard, last-stage drafter helper).
- `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py` — broadcast/padding + the warmup-serving specialization match (`_post_update_kernel`).
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` — input-prep kernel behavior incl. `context_only`.
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py` — context-K/V staging buffer stays at the draft hidden size under HC-residual targets (regression test for the fix below).
- `pytest tests/config/test_dspark_prefill_only.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/ -q` and `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py` → all green on this tree; pre-commit green.

## Model evaluation

Validated end-to-end on the pre-split stack (#53577 lineage): DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 DSpark PD disaggregation with PP on both sides — prefill PP2×TP2 (prefill-only DSpark producer) + decode PP2×TP2 with DSpark, Mooncake KV transfer (TCP transport): GSM8K strict-match **0.9447** (1319 samples, stderr 0.0063). This is exactly the P-PP + D-PP DSpark combination previously reported to produce garbled output.

This rebuild rebases that stack onto current main (including the #57632 context-K/V graph-capture refactor and the #58484 revert of #56956, which this PR re-applies); the rebase keeps the aggregated-path behavior and changes no model numerics.

Re-validated on this exact tree (SM120, same both-PP PD configuration, Mooncake TCP): GSM8K strict-match **0.9462** (1319 samples, threshold 0.8) — consistent with the pre-split stack's 0.9447. The re-validation caught one integration bug from the #57632 merge: the graph-captured context-K/V staging buffer was sized by the hc-widened `hidden_size` (that widening exists for MTP-style drafters whose forward eats the target's pre-hc_head residual), while DFlash only ever stores `combine_hidden_states` output there — fixed in `103ffe9e9e` by sizing it from the draft's own hidden size, with a regression test.

After the review-driven streamlining (model_runner.py diff down from 197 to 66 changed lines: the producer branch moved behind `propose()`, and `warmup_pp_decode_update` moved to warmup.py), re-validated again on HEAD `b2952d32d0` (SM120):

- Aggregated IFB PP2×TP2: GSM8K strict-match **0.9545** (1319 samples).
- Both-PP PD, Mooncake TCP: GSM8K strict-match **0.9431** (1319 samples). (Run on a host whose GPU P2P is disabled at the NCCL level for an unrelated IOMMU issue — transport-level only, no effect on the correctness paths under test.)

Infrastructure flakes observed during validation are unrelated to this PR: the known Mooncake bootstrap 5s HTTP timeout (#58543) on cold-start/high-load attempts, and a harness abort-mode teardown racing its GPU-memory cleanup check on one passing run.

AI assistance was used in preparing this PR.

items.title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add GQA DSpark prefill context-KV-only loading
items.body:
## Overview

Add opt-in context-KV-only weight loading for Qwen3 GQA DSpark drafts on
dedicated disaggregated-prefill producers. Keep the complete draft on decode.

## Claims

- Add `prefill_context_kv_only`, default false, for a dedicated MRV2 KV producer.
- Construct and load only the auxiliary-hidden-state projection, hidden norm,
  context K/V and K norm. Do not allocate draft query/output, MLP, embedding,
  vocabulary, Markov or confidence weights on the producer.
- Reuse DFlash fused context-KV computation and the existing cache transfer
  contract. Skip producer draft queries and draft graph capture; leave normal
  consumer drafting, sampling and verification unchanged.

## Validation

PP4 end-to-end validation used the PP-PD integration associated with #56957
(integration fork `65bad2204be2c848652e6f2c1c888239212ed2f2`) and vLLM v0.31.0
native libraries. This validation environment includes the PP-PD patches.

Environment: one eight-GPU CUDA node, compute capability 10.3, 267.69 GiB
CUDA-visible capacity per GPU; PyTorch 2.13+cu130, Mooncake CUDA13 0.3.13.post1,
MRV2 and BLHNC transfer. P: TP1/PP4, layers 22/20/20/16. D: TP1/DP4/EP.
Eight speculative tokens, probabilistic drafting, block verification, adaptive
verification off, target/draft FP8 KV, prefix caching off, decode CUDA graphs on.
Producer batch tokens 32768/max-seqs 8; decode batch tokens 128/max-seqs 32.

Private fixed business workload: reservoir 300 requests from a fixed 800,
seed 20260918, concurrency 8, output cap 1024, natural EOS. Original sampling,
tools and chat-template arguments are retained. Request-body hashes and input
token counts match across producer variants; warmups are excluded and the same
decode processes remain resident. No checkpoint tensors were changed.

| Producer | Acceptance including target | Token-weighted TPOT / ms | Success/errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Complete draft | 4.206129 | 6.1364 | 300/0 |
| Context-KV-only, public option | 4.183596 | 5.9190 | 300/0 |

Acceptance is `1 + accepted_draft_tokens / draft_rounds`; counter windows are
clean. These results show no material observed quality/latency regression, not
bitwise equivalence or a guaranteed speedup. Sampling and timing vary. One
additional prototype context-only run measured 4.196787 and 6.0182 ms; it is not
substituted for the public-option result.

Producer draft-exclusive parameter storage falls from 5.553 GiB to
**0.585950 GiB** (629,159,168 bytes, eight tensors), on the final PP stage.
Removing an additional 240 MiB duplicate fused-KV weight buffer makes the model
load profile fall from 119.58 to 114.38 GiB, about **5.20 GiB**. An already-shared
target vocabulary head is not counted as saved memory. Freed memory can be
reallocated to KV; total `nvidia-smi` usage need not fall by the same amount.

The GQA-only candidate passes **14 targeted CPU regression cases**: selected
weight loading, two-layer fused K/V ordering, optional checkpoint prefixes,
missing/duplicate/shape/dtype rejection, and dedicated producer role checks.
The isolated local wrapper imports the candidate module and runs the selected
suite with `--noconftest --import-mode=importlib`; it does not modify serving
runtime sources.

After rebasing onto upstream `817fa3518cd4bcc94b31e044c534c002e701c801`, all
14 targeted cases and relevant lint/type/config/CI-tethering checks were rerun
and passed. Only the feature-index link placement required conflict resolution;
the GQA feature patch is otherwise unchanged. The business measurements above
are the original local validation, not a new post-rebase model benchmark.

The entry point for a configured source checkout is:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py -k context_only -q
pre-commit run --files <changed-files>
```

The existing basic-model CI job already runs this test file, including its
shared DSpark Markov tests. The private checkpoints/business data cannot run in
upstream CI; the model evaluation above is local validation. The producer was
also exercised with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

## Details

Minimal PD flow:

1. P runs the normal target and captures configured auxiliary hidden states.
2. The partial draft projects/normalizes those states and writes each layer's
   context KV, without executing draft query generation.
3. The existing connector transfers target and draft context KV under unchanged
   layer names and cache geometry.
4. D keeps its complete draft, reconstructs query-tail KV and verifies normally.

The producer model is constructed selectively before loading, rather than
allocating a complete draft and pruning it. GQA K/V weights are loaded directly
into the fused buffer; checkpoint tensors and file formats are unchanged.
Layer count, KV heads, head dimension and per-layer SWA/full attention come from
configuration, not from a hardcoded checkpoint or five-layer layout.

Initial scope: `Qwen3DSparkModel`, bias-free non-quantized BF16 draft weights,
dedicated `kv_producer`, MRV2, target/draft TP1 and PCP1/DCP1. Unsupported
architectures and roles fail closed. Do not enable this option on a consumer or
send standalone multi-token generation to the producer. Omitting the option
retains the existing full-draft behavior and graph-hash factors.

This saves producer weights and query computation, **not context KV storage**.
Cache capacity, stage balance and long-prefill temporary workspace remain
separate constraints. No new CUDA kernels, checkpoint-side runtime files or
connector-protocol changes are included.

This does not duplicate #55654/#60076 (KV insertion without selective weight
construction), #60320 (trailing-window context compute) or #54036 (PCP context
sharding). The implementation isolates partial model construction and weight
loading instead. Open PR duplicate checks were repeated before submission.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used. The human submitter reviewed the
implementation, confirmed running relevant code and approved submission.

---

  selective construction without scheduler or connector changes.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Targeted CPU regressions and matched local
  model/memory evaluations; private CI limitations documented.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Existing model test suite and documentation
  extended; relevant formatting, type, configuration and import checks run.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, PP validation environment, repeated
  measurements, limitations and AI assistance disclosed.

items.title: feat: add windowed hidden-state capture for vLLM rollout
items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds request-local windowed hidden-state capture for rollouts. Consumers can request hidden states for selected response positions instead of collecting the full response.

The MRV2 optimization copies captured rows asynchronously into pinned CPU memory and reuses output completion synchronization to make the results ready before they are returned.

Implements the windowed capture contract discussed in #56916.

## Key results

- Window capture reduces GPU-to-CPU transfer volume by 93.75% in the measured workload.
- With CUDA graphs enabled, window capture achieves **1.0858x throughput on Qwen3.5-0.8B** and a **1.1033x median paired speedup on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**, compared with full-response capture in the same optimized implementation.
- **21 GPU tests passed**, including CUDA Graph output-buffer reuse and completion synchronization.

## Validation

### Qwen3.5-0.8B — CUDA Graph benchmark

**Tested commit:** `5d4cf1e560f645068d8cb49a53c1d381fe58122e` (optimized implementation and GPU regression tests). The complete benchmark script and reproduction commands are provided below.

Configuration: RTX 3090, Qwen3.5-0.8B, BF16, TP=PP=DP=1, CUDA graphs enabled, synchronous scheduling, and prefix caching disabled. Each request has 512 input and 512 output tokens. The benchmark runs 128 requests in batches of 16, with two measured rounds after warmup. The requested response window is `[128, 160)`.

| Capture mode | Generation + export, median [min, max] (s) | Output tokens/s | D2H per request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Disabled | 23.68 [23.62, 23.74] | 2767.97 | 0 |
| Full response | 25.97 [25.87, 26.06] | 2524.01 | 1 MiB |
| Window `[128, 160)` | 23.91 [23.86, 23.97] | 2740.44 | 64 KiB |
| Window beyond response length | 23.91 [23.86, 23.96] | 2740.76 | 0 |

Compared with full-response capture, window capture reduces D2H transfer from **1 MiB to 64 KiB per request (−93.75%)** and improves generation-plus-export throughput by **1.0858x**. Its elapsed time is also within approximately **1%** of capture-disabled execution.

Both capture modes export the same 32 hidden-state rows as Base64. Full capture first transfers the complete response to CPU; window capture transfers only the requested rows. The benchmark measures generation and CPU export after warmup, using the same workload and implementation for all four modes.

#### Correctness

- **21 hidden-state capture tests passed on GPU**, including six CUDA Graph buffer-reuse cases across three capture layouts and two event-wait policies. These verify output readiness and captured-state integrity across buffer reuse.
- **Correctness checks passed:** all four capture modes produced identical generated tokens, and full/window captured hidden states had a **maximum absolute difference of 0** on the checked batch.
- **GPU synchronization check passed** for all four modes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
- **Static checks passed:** Ruff, formatting, and `git diff --check`.

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — CUDA Graph benchmark

**Correctness checks passed.** These measurements extend the performance evaluation to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash using PR source `5d4cf1e560`.

#### Configuration

- **Hardware environment:** two GB200 nodes, four GPUs per node, 184.3 GiB per GPU.
- **Model execution:** TP=4, PP=1, BF16 activations, and the model's original FP8/FP4 weights.
- **Software:** CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, and the nightly image built at 06:15 UTC with its native extensions.
- **Workload:** 512 input tokens and 512 output tokens per request; batch size 16; 128 requests; capture window `[128, 160)`.
- **Measurement:** one warmup batch per mode, followed by five measured rounds. CUDA graphs were enabled; prefix caching and async scheduling were disabled. Elapsed time includes generation and export.

#### Results

The table shows the median across five rounds. D2H volume is reported for the returning TP rank.

| Capture mode | Generation + export (s) | Output tokens/s | D2H per request | TTFT P95 (ms) | Token ITL P95 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Disabled (Off) | 51.087 | 1282.83 | 0 | 187.16 | 12.69 |
| Full response (Full) | 56.778 | 1154.25 | 5 MiB | 191.97 | 14.29 |
| Window `[128, 160)` (Window) | 51.450 | 1273.78 | 320 KiB | 187.72 | 13.28 |
| Window beyond response length (Never) | 51.208 | 1279.79 | 0 | 186.69 | 12.89 |

Window capture achieved a **1.1033x median paired speedup over full-response capture**, equivalent to approximately **10.3% higher throughput**. Its median paired elapsed-time overhead relative to capture-disabled execution was **0.89%**.

These paired statistics are calculated within each round, then summarized by their median. Ratios calculated directly from the elapsed-time medians in the table are **1.1036x** for Full/Window and **0.71%** for Window overhead relative to Off.

#### Profiling

| Metric | Full response | Window `[128, 160)` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| D2H volume per request, summed across all TP ranks | 20 MiB | 1.25 MiB |
| CPU export time per request | 0.191 ms | 0.187 ms |
| CPU copy allocation and submission time per request | 11.111 ms | 0.693 ms |
| GPU copy execution time per 16-request batch, summed across GPUs | 87.71 ms | 5.46 ms |

Window capture reduced D2H data volume by **93.75%**. GPU copy execution times above are sums across GPUs, rather than wall-clock batch times.

A supplementary eager experiment used three rounds with 16 requests per mode and produced a **0.9985x median paired Full/Window speedup**. The throughput improvement above was observed with CUDA graphs enabled.

### Qwen3.5-0.8B reproduction

Check out commit `5d4cf1e560f645068d8cb49a53c1d381fe58122e`, install that vLLM version in `.venv`, and save the complete script below as `benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py`:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
uv run --no-sync --python .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B \
  --input-tokens 512 \
  --output-tokens 512 \
  --window-start 128 \
  --window-size 32 \
  --batch-size 16 \
  --requests 128 \
  --rounds 2 \
  --result capture_graph.json
```

The script requires CUDA, checks generated tokens and selected hidden states, prints metrics for each round, and writes raw measurements and configuration metadata to JSON. CUDA graphs remain enabled; add `--enforce-eager` for a separate eager comparison.

<details>
<summary>Complete GPU benchmark script</summary>

Save as `benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py`.

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project

"""GPU rollout benchmark for PR #57736; same-version full vs window capture.

Run from an editable PR checkout on a CUDA Linux host:
    uv run --no-sync --python .venv/bin/python \
        benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B

Uses fixed-size request batches to compare capture modes under a reproducible
workload. Both capture modes export the same selected window as Base64.
The benchmark records generation, export, and host-copy overhead separately.
"""

import argparse
import base64
import json
import os
import random
import statistics
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD", "spawn")

import numpy as np
import torch

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.v1.hidden_state_capture import HiddenStateCapturePlan

SCENARIOS = ("off", "full", "window", "never")


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="Qwen/Qwen3-8B")
    parser.add_argument("--input-tokens", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--output-tokens", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--window-start", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--window-size", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=16)
    parser.add_argument("--requests", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=5)
    parser.add_argument("--warmup-waves", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=("bfloat16", "float16"), default="bfloat16")
    parser.add_argument("--gpu-memory-utilization", type=float, default=0.85)
    parser.add_argument("--enforce-eager", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1234)
    parser.add_argument("--atol", type=float, default=0.02)
    parser.add_argument("--rtol", type=float, default=0.02)
    parser.add_argument("--result", type=Path, default=Path("capture_benchmark.json"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    for name in (
        "input_tokens",
        "output_tokens",
        "window_size",
        "batch_size",
        "requests",
        "rounds",
        "warmup_waves",
    ):
        if getattr(args, name) <= 0:
            parser.error(f"--{name.replace('_', '-')} must be positive")
    if (
        not 0
        <= args.window_start
        < args.window_start + args.window_size
        <= args.output_tokens
    ):
        parser.error("the window must lie inside the generated response")
    if args.requests % args.batch_size:
        parser.error("--requests must be divisible by --batch-size")
    return args


def plans_for(scenario, count, args):
    if scenario == "off":
        return None
    if scenario == "full":
        start, end = 0, args.output_tokens
    elif scenario == "window":
        start, end = args.window_start, args.window_start + args.window_size
    else:
        start = args.output_tokens + 128
        end = start + args.window_size
    return [
        HiddenStateCapturePlan.from_window(
            request_id=f"bench-{i}",
            prompt_len=args.input_tokens,
            start=start,
            end=end,
            collection_id="gpu-benchmark",
            coordinate="response",
            min_rows=end - start,
        )
        for i in range(count)
    ]


def selected_states(output, scenario, args):
    capture = output.hidden_state_capture
    if scenario in ("off", "never"):
        if capture is not None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{scenario}: unexpected captured result")
        if (
            scenario == "never"
            and output.hidden_capture_skip_reason != "ended_before_window"
        ):
            raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected skip: {output.hidden_capture_skip_reason}")
        return None
    if capture is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"capture failed: {output.hidden_capture_skip_reason}")
    if capture.hidden_states.device.type != "cpu" or capture.copied_bytes <= 0:
        raise RuntimeError("expected actual GPU-to-CPU capture")
    start = args.input_tokens - 1
    if scenario == "full":
        expected = np.arange(start, start + args.output_tokens)
        rows = capture.hidden_states[
            args.window_start : args.window_start + args.window_size
        ]
    else:
        start += args.window_start
        expected = np.arange(start, start + args.window_size)
        rows = capture.hidden_states
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(capture.hidden_positions, expected)
    if capture.hidden_states.shape[0] != len(expected):
        raise RuntimeError("hidden-state row count does not match positions")
    return rows


def generate(llm, prompts, params, plans):
    return llm.generate(prompts, params, hidden_state_capture=plans, use_tqdm=False)


def validate(llm, prompts, params, args):
    reference_tokens = None
    reference_states = None
    max_error = 0.0
    for scenario in SCENARIOS:
        outputs = generate(
            llm, prompts, params, plans_for(scenario, len(prompts), args)
        )
        tokens = [list(out.outputs[0].token_ids) for out in outputs]
        if any(len(ids) != args.output_tokens for ids in tokens):
            raise RuntimeError("generation did not produce the requested token count")
        if reference_tokens is None:
            reference_tokens = tokens
        elif tokens != reference_tokens:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{scenario}: generated tokens differ from capture-off")
        rows = [selected_states(out, scenario, args) for out in outputs]
        if scenario == "full":
            reference_states = [row.clone() for row in rows]
        elif scenario == "window":
            for actual, expected in zip(rows, reference_states):
                torch.testing.assert_close(
                    actual, expected, atol=args.atol, rtol=args.rtol
                )
                max_error = max(
                    max_error, (actual.float() - expected.float()).abs().max().item()
                )
        del outputs, rows
    print(
        f"Correctness PASS: all scenarios, batch={len(prompts)}, "
        f"max_abs_error={max_error:.6g}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return {"batch_size": len(prompts), "max_abs_error": max_error}


def run_round(llm, prompts, params, scenario, args, round_id):
    plans = plans_for(scenario, args.batch_size, args)
    generation_s = export_s = 0.0
    copied_bytes = copy_wait_ms = encoded_bytes = 0
    ttft_ms, mean_itl_ms = [], []
    for offset in range(0, len(prompts), args.batch_size):
        wave = prompts[offset : offset + args.batch_size]
        started = perf_counter()
        outputs = generate(llm, wave, params, plans)
        generation_s += perf_counter() - started

        # Validate outside the measured generation and export regions.
        for out in outputs:
            count = len(out.outputs[0].token_ids)
            if count != args.output_tokens:
                raise RuntimeError(f"expected {args.output_tokens} tokens, got {count}")
            selected_states(out, scenario, args)
            if out.metrics is None or out.metrics.first_token_ts <= 0:
                raise RuntimeError("missing engine timing metrics")
            stats = out.metrics
            ttft_ms.append(stats.first_token_latency * 1000)
            if count > 1:
                mean_itl_ms.append(
                    (stats.last_token_ts - stats.first_token_ts) * 1000 / (count - 1)
                )
            if out.hidden_state_capture is not None:
                copied_bytes += out.hidden_state_capture.copied_bytes
                copy_wait_ms += out.hidden_state_capture.copy_ms

        # Same final window and encoding work for full and window capture.
        started = perf_counter()
        if scenario in ("full", "window"):
            for out in outputs:
                states = out.hidden_state_capture.hidden_states
                if scenario == "full":
                    states = states[
                        args.window_start : args.window_start + args.window_size
                    ]
                byte_view = states.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).numpy()
                encoded = base64.b64encode(memoryview(byte_view))
                encoded_bytes += len(encoded)
                del encoded
        export_s += perf_counter() - started
        del outputs

    total_s = generation_s + export_s
    return {
        "round": round_id,
        "scenario": scenario,
        "generation_s": generation_s,
        "generation_plus_export_s": total_s,
        "generation_output_tokens_s": args.requests * args.output_tokens / generation_s,
        "end_to_end_output_tokens_s": args.requests * args.output_tokens / total_s,
        "ttft_p95_ms": float(np.percentile(ttft_ms, 95)),
        "per_request_mean_itl_p95_ms": float(np.percentile(mean_itl_ms, 95))
        if mean_itl_ms
        else None,
        "d2h_mib_per_request": copied_bytes / args.requests / 2**20,
        "copy_wait_ms_per_request": copy_wait_ms / args.requests,
        "cpu_export_ms_per_request": export_s * 1000 / args.requests,
        "base64_bytes_per_request": encoded_bytes / args.requests,
    }


def git_head():
    try:
        return subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            cwd=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1],
            text=True,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        ).strip()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return "unknown"


def main():
    args = parse_args()
    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.version.cuda is None:
        raise SystemExit("This benchmark requires an NVIDIA CUDA GPU and CUDA PyTorch.")
    import vllm

    metadata = {
        "args": {
            key: str(val) if isinstance(val, Path) else val
            for key, val in vars(args).items()
        },
        "git_head": git_head(),
        "vllm": vllm.__version__,
        "torch": torch.__version__,
        "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),
        "gpu_memory_gib": torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 2**30,
        "environment": {
            key: value
            for key, value in os.environ.items()
            if key
            in (
                "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES",
                "VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD",
                "VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT",
                "VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER",
                "VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND",
                "VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK",
                "CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING",
            )
        },
        "scope": (
            "TP=1 PP=1; fixed-size batches; final hidden state; "
            "Base64 encoding of selected window"
        ),
        "copy_timer_scope": (
            "Host-side allocation/submission for async capture; "
            "blocking capture also includes any associated wait"
        ),
    }
    print(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2), flush=True)
    llm = LLM(
        model=args.model,
        dtype=args.dtype,
        seed=args.seed,
        tensor_parallel_size=1,
        pipeline_parallel_size=1,
        max_model_len=args.input_tokens + args.output_tokens + 16,
        max_num_seqs=args.batch_size,
        gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_memory_utilization,
        async_scheduling=False,
        enable_prefix_caching=False,
        enforce_eager=args.enforce_eager,
        disable_log_stats=False,
    )
    tokenizer = llm.get_tokenizer()
    source = tokenizer.encode(
        "Explain how GPUs accelerate matrix multiplication and model inference. "
        "Give several examples and continue with technical details. ",
        add_special_tokens=False,
    )
    if not source:
        raise RuntimeError("tokenizer produced an empty prompt")
    prompts = []
    for i in range(args.requests):
        shift = i % len(source)
        rotated = source[shift:] + source[:shift]
        ids = (rotated * ((args.input_tokens + len(rotated) - 1) // len(rotated)))[
            : args.input_tokens
        ]
        prompts.append({"prompt_token_ids": ids})
    params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=args.output_tokens,
        min_tokens=args.output_tokens,
        ignore_eos=True,
        detokenize=False,
    )
    correctness = validate(llm, prompts[: args.batch_size], params, args)
    for scenario in SCENARIOS:
        print(f"Warmup: {scenario}", flush=True)
        for _ in range(args.warmup_waves):
            outputs = generate(
                llm,
                prompts[: args.batch_size],
                params,
                plans_for(scenario, args.batch_size, args),
            )
            del outputs

    print(
        "\nround scenario  gen_s    total_s   tok/s     TTFTp95  meanITLp95  "
        "D2HMiB/req  copy_host_ms/req  export_ms/req",
        flush=True,
    )
    records = []
    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    for round_id in range(1, args.rounds + 1):
        order = list(SCENARIOS)
        rng.shuffle(order)
        for scenario in order:
            row = run_round(llm, prompts, params, scenario, args, round_id)
            records.append(row)
            itl = row["per_request_mean_itl_p95_ms"]
            itl_text = f"{itl:.3f}" if itl is not None else "N/A"
            print(
                f"{round_id:5d} {scenario:8s} {row['generation_s']:8.3f} "
                f"{row['generation_plus_export_s']:9.3f} "
                f"{row['end_to_end_output_tokens_s']:9.2f} "
                f"{row['ttft_p95_ms']:8.3f} {itl_text:>10s} "
                f"{row['d2h_mib_per_request']:11.4f} "
                f"{row['copy_wait_ms_per_request']:17.3f} "
                f"{row['cpu_export_ms_per_request']:13.3f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            args.result.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            args.result.write_text(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "metadata": metadata,
                        "correctness": correctness,
                        "records": records,
                    },
                    indent=2,
                ),
                encoding="utf-8",
            )

    print("\nSummary: median [min, max] across rounds", flush=True)
    for scenario in SCENARIOS:
        rows = [row for row in records if row["scenario"] == scenario]
        for key in (
            "generation_plus_export_s",
            "end_to_end_output_tokens_s",
            "d2h_mib_per_request",
        ):
            values = [row[key] for row in rows]
            print(
                f"{scenario:8s} {key:30s} {statistics.median(values):.4f} "
                f"[{min(values):.4f}, {max(values):.4f}]"
            )
    speedups = []
    for round_id in range(1, args.rounds + 1):
        by_mode = {row["scenario"]: row for row in records if row["round"] == round_id}
        speedups.append(
            by_mode["full"]["generation_plus_export_s"]
            / by_mode["window"]["generation_plus_export_s"]
        )
    print(
        "\nWindow vs full, median paired total-time speedup: "
        f"{statistics.median(speedups):.4f}x",
        flush=True,
    )
    print(f"Raw results saved to: {args.result.resolve()}", flush=True)
    print("meanITLp95: P95 of per-request mean ITL.")
    print("copy_wait_ms_per_request: measured host-side copy overhead.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Regression test commands and metric definitions</summary>

GPU validation command used on the benchmark host:

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=/root/autodl-tmp/capture_graph_optimization \
  /root/autodl-tmp/capture_graph_optimization/test_hidden_state_capture.py -q
```

Equivalent command for an editable checkout:

```bash
uv run --no-sync --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/test_hidden_state_capture.py -q
```

For the GPU synchronization check, run with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, 64 input tokens, 64 output tokens, window start 16, window size 16, batch size 4, four requests, and two rounds.

The script also reports TTFT P95, P95 of per-request mean ITL, CPU export time, and host-side copy overhead.

</details>

## Details

MRV2 queues D2H copies into fresh pinned CPU buffers. The existing AsyncOutput completion event ensures that copying finishes before those buffers are read. Other capture-helper callers retain the blocking default.

For single-GPU synchronous scheduling with CUDA graphs enabled, the implementation uses non-sleeping output-event waits. Other configurations retain sleeping waits. Completion is still checked before results are consumed.

All four benchmark modes use the same output-event wait policy, making the full-versus-window comparison consistent. The optimized path combines selective D2H transfer with the MRV2 copy/synchronization improvements.

The Qwen3.5-0.8B benchmark uses a single GPU; the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash benchmark uses TP=4 and PP=1. Both use synchronous scheduling with CUDA graphs enabled.

### Related work

Related PRs #57663 and #59543 explore complementary hidden-state capture paths. This PR focuses on request-local response windows and efficient MRV2 export; shared interfaces and transfer mechanisms can be aligned during review.

---

items.title: [Feature] Batch-invariant support for speculative decoding
items.body:
## 1. Summary

This PR extends batch invariance to stochastic speculative decoding. A seeded
request now follows the same sampling and speculative-decoding path when batch
size, request order, or scheduling changes, including KV-cache preemption.

The implementation has two main parts:

~~1. Independent deterministic RNG streams for proposal sampling, acceptance,
   and residual sampling.~~
**Update on 8.27:** RNG-stream separation is handled separately in woosuk/mrv2-draft-gumbel-decouple branch. In particular, [commit 214a205](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/woosuk/mrv2-draft-gumbel-decouple) separates draft Gumbel noise from acceptance/recovery noise. Since that issue is orthogonal to speculative batch invariance, I’ve removed the RNG-domain changes from this PR.

2. Preemption recovery that reconstructs the discarded proposal at the same
   logical boundary before verification.

The validated methods are EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark with probabilistic draft
sampling and standard rejection sampling. I didn't find a proper model with MTP to
test, because GDN hasn't been supported with batch-invariance now.

An exact open-PR search for speculative batch invariance found no duplicate.
Related issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433. Broader searches 
found adjacent batch-invariance and speculative-decoding work,
but none covering this proposal RNG and preemption-recovery design. No issue
number was provided for an issue-specific duplicate check. AI assistance was
used for implementation, review, testing, and documentation. The human
submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line and reproducing
the reported tests before submission.

## 2. Method

~~### 2.1 Independent deterministic RNG streams~~

~~Proposal, acceptance, and residual sampling use separate RNG domains. Each draw
is derived from the request seed and its logical token position, so unrelated
requests cannot change its random sequence through batching or scheduling. The
bonus target token continues to use the normal target-sampling stream.~~

### 2.2 Preemption recovery and KV-cache boundary

A speculative proposal spans two scheduler steps: one step creates `K` draft
tokens, and the next verifies those tokens plus one bonus target token. If the
request is preempted between these steps, retaining only the request tokens is
not enough: the proposal and the worker-side hidden state used to create it have
been released.

For example, let the request contain `L = 4` committed tokens:

```text
A B C D
```

Before preemption, the proposal is produced as follows:

```text
execute C -> target hidden state h_C
sample D from h_C
draft from (h_C, D) -> P1 P2
```

The logical state is therefore:

```text
computed tokens:       A B C
sampled next token:          D
pending proposal:              P1 P2
```

On preemption, the scheduler records only the proposal length (`K = 2`) and
uses the normal cleanup path to release KV-cache blocks and worker state. On
recovery it performs:

```text
prefix-cache hit:      A B       # at most L - 2 tokens
replay:                    C     # reconstruct h_C
known next token:             D
regenerate:          (h_C, D) -> P1 P2
verify atomically:               P1 P2 + bonus token
```

An `L - 1` hit would cache `A B C` and skip the forward pass for `C`. Its KV
entries are available, but `h_C`, which the drafter needs, is not. Executing
`D` instead would advance to `h_D` and build the proposal for the next logical
position. Limiting the hit to `L - 2` therefore recreates the same `(h_C, D)`
input and, with the position-based draft RNG stream, the same proposal as the
non-preempted execution. Scheduling the subsequent `K + 1` verification as one
unit prevents another partial boundary from being introduced.

## 3. Evaluation

### 3.1 Serving configuration

The two runs for each method use the same target/speculative model pair and
change only `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`.

| Method | Target model | Speculative model | Speculative tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| EAGLE3 | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` | 3 |
| DFlash | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` | 16 |
| DSpark | `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8` | `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` | 7 |

The command below uses placeholders so that the same serving setup can be
reused for each row.

```bash
export TARGET_MODEL="TARGET_MODEL_ID"
export DRAFT_MODEL="DRAFT_MODEL_ID"
export SPEC_METHOD="eagle3"       # eagle3, dflash, or dspark
export SPEC_TOKENS="3"            # 3, 16, or 7 respectively
export SPEC_CONFIG="{
  \"model\": \"${DRAFT_MODEL}\",
  \"method\": \"${SPEC_METHOD}\",
  \"num_speculative_tokens\": ${SPEC_TOKENS},
  \"draft_sample_method\": \"probabilistic\",
  \"rejection_sample_method\": \"standard\",
  \"enable_adaptive_verification\": false
}"

# BI off
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0 \
vllm serve "$TARGET_MODEL" \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config "$SPEC_CONFIG"

# BI on
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 \
vllm serve "$TARGET_MODEL" \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config "$SPEC_CONFIG"
```

For DSpark, the evaluation added `"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"` to
`SPEC_CONFIG`. DFlash used `--max-num-seqs 128` for model warmup.

### 3.2 GSM8K end-to-end results

All 1,319 GSM8K test examples were served twice per configuration: concurrency
32 in natural order and concurrency 64 in reverse order. Every request used a
stable unique seed with temperature `0.6`, top-k `20`, top-p `0.95`, and at most
256 output tokens. Exact BI requires identical token IDs, text, and finish
reason between the two phases. Accuracy and throughput below are from the
concurrency-64 phase.

| Method | BI | Exact BI | Mismatches | Accuracy | Req/s | Output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| EAGLE3 | off | FAIL | 401 | 88.32% | 28.92 | 3468.76 |
| EAGLE3 | on | PASS | 0 | 88.02% | 21.68 | 2614.11 |
| DFlash | off | FAIL | 187 | 87.79% | 11.08 | 1335.24 |
| DFlash | on | PASS | 0 | 87.79% | 10.50 | 1270.43 |
| DSpark | off | FAIL | 118 | 83.17% | 42.67 | 5398.54 |
| DSpark | on | PASS | 0 | 82.94% | 41.28 | 5169.72 |

| Method | Accuracy delta | Req/s delta | Output tok/s delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| EAGLE3 | -0.30 pp | -25.03% | -24.64% |
| DFlash | +0.00 pp | -5.22% | -4.85% |
| DSpark | -0.23 pp | -3.26% | -4.24% |

These throughput runs validate invariance across concurrency and request order;
they did not trigger KV-cache preemption. The focused E2E test below uses a
small KV-cache allocation and asserts that preemption occurred before comparing
serial and batched token IDs.

### 3.3 Minimal tests

The first test checks independent RNG domains, batch splitting, and the target
bonus-token stream. The second forces speculative decoding and KV-cache
preemption, then checks exact batch invariance.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py::test_spec_rng_streams_are_batch_invariant \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_stochastic_batch_invariance.py::test_spec_batch_invariance_with_preemption
```

The E2E test requires one CUDA GPU with at least 32 GB of memory and access to
the configured public model artifacts.

items.title: [Core] Balance padding vs group count when grouping hybrid KV cache layers
items.body:
## Summary

`_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` splits each attention type into equal-sized groups, padding the last group of each type. The group size trades **padding** (reserved-but-unused layers = wasted KV cache memory) against **the number of groups**: every group is a separate attention block table whose metadata is rebuilt each step in `build_attn_metadata` (it loops over groups), so a model with many groups spends a large fraction of every decode step there.

The old heuristic set the group size to the `min` (or `max`, when within 1.5×) layer count across types. That handles clean `n:1` patterns (Gemma3 5:1, LLaMA4 3:1, gpt-oss+eagle), but it degrades badly when one type has very few layers.

This PR replaces it with `_select_group_size`, which scans candidate group sizes and returns the one minimizing `padding + padding_per_group * num_groups`, breaking ties toward fewer groups. `padding_per_group` (default `1.0`) is the number of padding layers we accept to remove one group. The default reproduces the previous grouping on clean `n:1`/eagle patterns while fixing the low-count and irregular cases.

## Motivating example: a Qwen hybrid was *super* slow

The model that surfaced this runs a hybrid Qwen main model with a DFlash speculative draft. Its layers form four distinct KV-cache types — importantly, the main and draft full-attention heads have **different shapes**, so they are separate types:

| type | count |
| --- | --- |
| full attention (main model) | 10 |
| full attention (DFlash draft, different shape) | 1 |
| GDN / linear-attention state (main model) | 20 |
| SWA (DFlash draft) | 5 |

`min(10, 1, 20, 5) = 1` because of the single draft head, and the 1.5× bump does not apply, so the old heuristic sets **group_size = 1** — one group per layer, **36 groups**, 16 of them attention groups. Every one of those 36 groups rebuilt its own metadata on every decode step, so `build_attn_metadata` dominated the profile and the model was extremely slow.

`_select_group_size` ignores the lone single-layer type and picks **group_size = 5**: the 10 + 1 + 20 + 5 layers become 2 + 1 + 4 + 1 = **8 groups** (4 attention groups), padding the draft head up to 5. Attention groups drop from 16 to 4 — a 4× cut in per-step metadata work — at the cost of 4 padding layers on the small draft head.

## Behavior deltas

| layer counts (type:count) | old group_size | new group_size | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gemma3 6 full : 30 sw | 6 | 6 | unchanged (gcd, no padding) |
| eagle 13 full : 12 sw | 13 | 13 | unchanged (bump to avoid padding) |
| 20 full : 30 sw | 20 (3 grp, 10 pad) | 10 (5 grp, 0 pad) | fixes in-code FIXME |
| 3 full : 7 sw | 3 (4 grp, 2 pad) | 4 (3 grp, 2 pad) | one fewer group, same padding |
| 10 : 1 : 20 : 5 (Qwen) | 1 (36 grp) | 5 (8 grp) | avoids one-group-per-layer |

## Key changes

`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`: add `_select_group_size` and the `_PADDING_LAYERS_PER_GROUP` constant, and call it from `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` in place of the `min`/`max`+1.5× heuristic (resolves the `FIXME(Chen)`). The downstream per-type padding warning and the strided `layers[i::num_groups]` split are unchanged.

## Tests

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` — 80 passed. Adds `test_select_group_size` (parametrized), `test_select_group_size_padding_per_group_trades_padding_for_groups`, and `test_select_group_size_ignores_single_layer_outlier` (the Qwen 36→8 group case), and updates `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker` for the 3 full + 7 sliding case.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff-format, mypy) on both changed files — passed.


### qwen run

| head | unpatched | + PR 49472 | PR effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| SWA | 100.5 | 109.1 | +8.6% |

## Output / accuracy impact

None expected: this only changes how layers are partitioned into KV cache groups and the resulting tensor layout, not attention math or numerics.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for "kv cache group size padding", "build_attn_metadata", and "hybrid kv cache groups"; none change group-size selection in `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size`. The nearest results — #38183 (a `build_attn_metadata` refactor) and #35703 (mapping full-attention layers onto a mamba page) — are orthogonal.

## AI assistance

The bucket-selection algorithm was provided by the submitter; AI assistance (Claude) was used to add tests, and draft this description.

items.title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add PARD-2 parallel draft model support with dual mode
items.body:
## Purpose

Add PARD-2 ([arXiv 2605.08632](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08632)) target-aligned parallel draft models as a speculative-decoding method, and fix a draft-input alignment bug that costs most of the acceptance on one of the three released checkpoints.

This builds directly on @ganeshr10's work in #49406 — the first seven commits here are his, unmodified. That PR has been open since July and its benchmarks were run on CPU; I'm one of the PARD-2 authors, and in validating it on GPU I found that the draft is fed a left-shifted sequence, which drops the row PARD-2 was trained to start from. The last two commits fix that and add regression tests. I'm opening this as a separate PR because the fix is not meaningful on its own (it only touches the code path #49406 introduces) and #49406 has had no maintainer review in six weeks; I'd be equally happy for this to land as #49406 plus my two commits, whichever maintainers prefer. Closes/supersedes #49406.

### What PARD-2 is, and why add it

PARD converts an autoregressive draft model into a parallel one at low training cost; PARD-2 adds target alignment, optimizing acceptance length rather than next-token accuracy, plus confidence-adaptive token weighting. Two properties are relevant for vLLM:

- **The draft is a small standalone LM, not a head grafted onto the target.** One draft serves a whole model family.
- **Dual mode.** The same checkpoint runs target-dependent (fusing target hidden states) or target-independent (plain parallel drafting). This PR already handles the fallback when the target's hidden size doesn't match what the draft was trained on.

Measured in vLLM on an RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (greedy, 256 max tokens, 80 prompts per dataset, concurrency 1, PARD-2's own eval prompts), acceptance length / output tok/s. Baseline without speculation is 74 tok/s for both 8B targets:

| target | method | K | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | **PARD-2** `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` | 15 | **7.72 / 398** | **8.09 / 417** | **8.72 / 443** | **4.02 / 214** |
| | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` | 15 | 5.87 / 315 | 7.07 / 374 | 7.77 / 406 | 3.29 / 180 |
| | **PARD-2** | 5 | 4.86 / 255 | 5.00 / 262 | 5.09 / 266 | 3.44 / 183 |
| | EAGLE-3 `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3` | 5 | 2.69 / 150 | 2.53 / 141 | 2.85 / 158 | 2.24 / 125 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | **PARD-2** `amd/PARD2-Llama-3.1-8B` | 15 | **6.83 / 345** | **7.66 / 388** | **8.88 / 439** | **4.25 / 220** |
| | **PARD-2** | 9 | 6.06 / 310 | 6.37 / 326 | 7.12 / 358 | 4.05 / 210 |
| | DFlash `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat` | 9 | 4.19 / 230 | 3.62 / 200 | 5.65 / 306 | 3.61 / 200 |
| | EAGLE-3 `yuhuili/EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B` | 5 | 3.64 / 197 | 3.13 / 171 | 4.16 / 224 | 3.34 / 181 |

EAGLE-3 here is vLLM's chain drafting (no tree) in non-thinking mode, and the AngelSlim Qwen3 draft may be tuned for thinking traces — read those rows as "what the released weights give you in vLLM today", not as the method's ceiling.

### The bug this fixes

PARD-2's draft input for position *t* is `embed(token[t]) + scale · target_proj(feat[t-1])` with `feat[-1] = 0`: the draft sees the whole sequence, starting at token 0 paired with a zero target feature.

The draft goes through the EAGLE input path, which left-shifts the token stream (`shift_input_ids=True`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py`) while mapping hidden states unshifted. Row *i* of the draft input then holds `token[i+1] + feat[i]` — the correct pairing for *t ≥ 1*, but the *t = 0* row is gone. That is right for EAGLE, whose draft starts at token 1, and wrong for PARD-2.

That first row acts as an attention sink for the draft. How much its absence costs is checkpoint-dependent (HF reference, K=1 first-position acceptance, with vs. without token 0): Qwen3-8B 0.933 → 0.512, Llama-3.1-8B 0.937 → 0.917, Qwen3-14B 0.939 → 0.923.

**The fix**: an `ANCHOR` mode in `copy_and_expand_eagle_inputs_kernel`, used for PARD-2 only. A request whose first target position is 0 (its prefill) gets one extra leading row — its first token, position 0, zero hidden state — and its real rows shift by one so they keep true positions. Any other request instead gets one trailing junk row marked rejected, keeping the per-request row count uniform, and its draft `seq_len` grows by one for the anchor entry already in the draft KV cache. The CPU backend swaps this kernel for a C++ op that doesn't know about the anchor, so `cpu_triton_utils` gains a torch implementation of the same layout.

## Test Plan

```bash
# unit: anchored layout, and Triton ANCHOR path vs the CPU backend's torch path
pytest -v -s tests/v1/spec_decode/test_pard2_anchor_kernel.py

# e2e acceptance length (Llama case pre-existing, Qwen3-8B case added here)
pytest -v -s tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/pard2/

# serving
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8010 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B", "num_speculative_tokens": 15}'
```

Acceptance length is read from the `vllm:spec_decode_*` metrics; clients were greedy with `enable_thinking=false`.

## Test Result

Acceptance length before → after the fix, K=15, all three released checkpoints:

| target / draft | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B / `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` | 1.99 → **7.72** | 2.23 → **8.09** | 2.06 → **8.72** | 1.59 → **4.02** |
| Qwen3-14B / `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-14B` | 7.42 → **7.63** | 7.99 → **8.12** | 8.51 → **8.71** | 3.95 → **4.02** |
| Llama-3.1-8B / `amd/PARD2-Llama-3.1-8B` | 6.08 → **6.83** | 6.77 → **7.66** | 7.79 → **8.88** | 3.82 → **4.25** |

All twelve improve; none regress.

Cross-checked against the PARD-2 reference implementation on the same prompts, and against the paper (Table 1, K=16, GSM8K):

| checkpoint | paper | reference impl | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 7.68 | 7.62 | 1.99 | **7.72** |
| Qwen3-14B | 7.65 | 7.61 | 7.42 | **7.63** |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 6.98 | 6.89 | 6.08 | **6.83** |

Across all twelve (model × dataset) settings the fixed path is within 0.25 of the reference implementation, except on the 20-problem MATH-500 subset (±0.5).

Mixed prefill/decode batches, Qwen3-8B GSM8K at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32: acceptance 7.72 / 7.70 / 7.52, throughput 398 / 2351 / 3231 tok/s.

### Target-independent mode

PARD-2's draft is a standalone small LM, so the same checkpoint can drive a target it was never trained for; this PR falls back to plain parallel drafting when the target's hidden size doesn't match what `target_proj` was trained on. To put a number on that, `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` is used **unchanged** as a draft for **Qwen3-4B**, alongside drafts trained specifically for Qwen3-4B.

DFlash2 is not in this branch's base, so those rows ran on a current upstream-main nightly (`0.28.1rc1.dev19`). The `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` row was run on both builds and they agree within 0.12 (0.45 on the 20-problem MATH-500 subset), so the two groups are comparable. Same harness and settings as above; `acceptance / tok/s`.

**K = 15**

| build | draft | trained for Qwen3-4B? | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | **6.10 / 473** | 6.66 / 516 | 6.37 / 494 | **3.32 / 269** |
| this PR | PARD-1 `amd/PARD-Qwen3-0.6B` (parallel) | no | 6.06 / 466 | 6.01 / 464 | 6.10 / 465 | 3.37 / 267 |
| this PR | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` | yes | 5.71 / 484 | **6.87 / 582** | **6.70 / 565** | 3.22 / 285 |
| main | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` (build calibration) | yes | 5.83 / 504 | 6.42 / 557 | 6.70 / 575 | 3.21 / 290 |
| this PR | no speculation | — | — / 127 | | | |

**K = 8 / 7**, each DFlash2 checkpoint at its own trained block size, with PARD-2 at the same K:

| build | draft | trained for Qwen3-4B? | K | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | 8 | 5.27 / 412 | **5.43 / 424** | **5.29 / 409** | **3.19 / 255** |
| main | DFlash2 `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dflash2` (b9) | yes | 8 | **5.36 / 455** | 5.29 / 460 | 4.73 / 412 | 3.08 / 275 |
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | 7 | **5.02 / 394** | **5.23 / 407** | **5.04 / 387** | **3.16 / 251** |
| main | DFlash2 `shanjiaz/dflash2_qwen3_4b` (b8) | yes | 7 | 4.68 / 402 | 4.47 / 390 | 4.42 / 382 | 2.91 / 259 |

A draft that was never trained for this target holds its own against drafts that were: even on GSM8K and MATH-500 with DFlash2 at K=8, ahead of it on HumanEval and MT-Bench, and ahead of the other DFlash2 checkpoint on all four at K=7. DFlash2 is ~10% faster per token, its draft being 5 layers. Note both DFlash2 checkpoints are community-trained with `speculators` (z-lab has not released a 4B DFlash2) and were converted to the `dflash_config` layout to load, so read them as "DFlash2 as trained by the community", not as the method's ceiling.

## Notes for reviewers

- The two anchor commits touch `utils.py`, `llm_base_proposer.py` and `cpu_triton_utils.py` only; the ANCHOR path is a `tl.constexpr` branch, so EAGLE/DFlash/DSpark codegen is unchanged.
- `AutoWeightsLoader` lost its `skip_prefixes`/`skip_substrs` kwargs in #53106, so the PARD-2 draft would not load on current main; the last commit ports that call site the same way #53106 migrated the others.
- The per-dataset tables were measured before rebasing onto current main. After the rebase I re-ran GSM8K on the submitted tree end to end and reproduced it: acceptance 1.976 -> 7.618, throughput 109 -> 398 tok/s (previously 1.986 -> 7.715, 110 -> 398). Unit tests, the Triton-vs-CPU kernel comparison, and lint all pass on the submitted tree.
- Parts of this were written with Claude Code, per the AI-assistance policy in the contributing guide. The analysis, experiments and validation are mine.

items.title: [Feat] GPU KV Cache Pluggable Eviction Policy
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes frequency-blind GPU KV cache eviction that causes unnecessary cache misses under mixed workloads.

### Problem

`BlockPool` currently uses a single-queue LRU implemented in `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue`. Once `ref_cnt` drops to zero, **all blocks are equal eviction candidates regardless of reuse history**. This has two critical blind spots:

1. **No frequency signal** — A system-prompt block reused by 10,000 requests and a one-time block are indistinguishable at eviction time.
2. **Scan pollution** — A burst of unique long-prompt requests floods the free queue tail, pushing high-value cached prefix blocks toward the eviction head. The 64 most valuable blocks can be lost before 1,984 worthless ones.

This is particularly painful for:
- Agents / RAG workloads with long shared system prompts
- High-concurrency multi-tenant deployments where one tenant's burst evicts another's hot prefix
- Disaggregated Prefill/Decode — prefix blocks transferred P→D must survive long enough to be reused

Additionally, the CPU offload layer (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/`) already has a full `ARCCachePolicy`. The GPU `BlockPool` was inconsistent with no equivalent protection.

### Solution

Introduce a **pluggable `GPUCachePolicy` abstraction** and implement three policies behind it:

| Policy | Algorithm | Key Property |
|---|---|---|
| `"lru"` | Single-queue LRU | **Default — zero behavioral change** |
| `"two_queue"` | Hot/Cold 2Q (Linux page-cache design) | Cold queue drains first; hot prefix blocks protected from scan pollution |
| `"arc"` | Adaptive Replacement Cache (Megiddo & Modha, IBM FAST 2003) | Self-tuning `p` adapts recency/frequency balance via ghost lists B1/B2; deployed in IBM DS8000 and ZFS |

All policies expose the same O(1) interface: `insert / insert_n / remove / touch / evict_n / __len__`. The `BlockPool` is refactored to delegate all eviction decisions to `self._policy`, with no changes to callsites outside `block_pool.py`.

### ARC — Key Adaptation for GPU KV Cache

Classical ARC detects ghost hits at **lookup time** (cache miss for a key in B1/B2). In vLLM there is no explicit lookup-miss hook, so ghost-hit detection is adapted to **`insert()` time**:

- Block A (hash H) evicted from T1 → H added to B1. _maybe_evict_cached_block() clears A's hash. A gets new content.
- A later request for prefix P (hash H) arrives → cache MISS. New blocks are allocated; P is recomputed; blocks get hash H.
- Those blocks are freed → free_blocks() calls insert_n([block with hash H]).
- insert() finds H in B1 → B1 ghost hit: p += max(1, |B2| / |B1|) (T1 was too small → grow recency partition) block routed to T2 (this content is worth keeping long-term)


This is semantically equivalent to the original ARC algorithm.

### Changed Files

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `vllm/v1/core/eviction_policy.py` | **New.** `GPUCachePolicy` ABC, `LRUGPUCachePolicy`, `TwoQueueGPUCachePolicy`, `ARCGPUCachePolicy`, `make_gpu_eviction_policy` factory |
| `vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py` | Refactored to use `self._policy`; `_FreeBlockQueueShim` for backward compat of `.free_block_queue.num_free_blocks` |
| `vllm/config/cache.py` | New `gpu_eviction_policy: Literal["lru", "two_queue", "arc"] = "lru"` field |
| `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` | Thread `eviction_policy` through base class + 3 subclasses + factory |
| `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py` | Add `eviction_policy` param, forward to coordinator |
| `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` | Pass `cache_config.gpu_eviction_policy` to `KVCacheManager` |
| `tests/v1/core/test_eviction_policy.py` | **New.** 40+ unit tests for all three policies |

---

## Test Plan

Run the new unit test file:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_eviction_policy.py -v
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -v
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -v
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -v

To manually exercise two_queue or arc with a real model:

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
    gpu_eviction_policy="arc",   # or "two_queue"
    enable_prefix_caching=True,
)

# Shared system prompt to populate T2
system_prompt = "You are a helpful assistant. " * 200
responses = llm.generate(
    [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
     {"role": "user", "content": f"Question {i}"}
     for i in range(50)],
    SamplingParams(max_tokens=64),
)
```

# Test Results
All 40+ unit tests pass:

```text
