items.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share the FlashMLA decode plan across KV cache groups
items.body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.build()` creates one empty `FlashMLASchedMeta` per DeepSeek-V4 layer type. The first `flash_mla_with_kvcache` call of each type runs FlashMLA's tile-scheduler planner, and the later layers of that type reuse the plan (the comment calls it "shared across all ~60 layers of that type within a decode step").

However, the builder runs once per KV cache group. With the packed KV cache layout, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's sliding-window caches are spread over 8 groups, and each group builds its own holders. So the planner runs once per (group, layer type). A torch-profiler trace of one TP8 decode step shows 18 planner launches in the target model (before layers 0-9 and 20-27) and 3 in the DSpark drafter (one per draft layer), where 4 are enough.

`get_mla_metadata_kernel` is a single 32-thread block with a serial loop over the SM partitions, and every launch sits in front of its layer's attention. On H20 it takes 16.6 µs per launch at 1 request and about 41 µs at 64 requests.

A plan depends on the batch shape and on the values of the decode `topk_length` / `extra_topk_length`. FlashMLA's interface allows reuse only while those values stay the same, but it asserts only shapes and config. Across the KV cache groups of one metadata build pass the values do match:
- The SWA lengths come from the same query and sequence lengths, window, valid-token mask and `replay_start`. Each group builds the mask from its own slot mapping, but every sliding-window group writes each scheduled token, so the masks agree; `replay_start` is one tensor passed to every builder.
- The top-k lengths count the valid entries each index layer writes. Every decode top-k path fills the entries past a row end derived from `seq_lens` and `next_n` alone with -1 (for example `rowEnd` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`), under the same valid-token mask. So each index layer of a compress ratio yields `min(rowEnd, topk)`.

That second point is also why a group's same-type layers can already share one plan today, though they take their top-k from different index layers.

This PR lets the groups share the holders:
- MRV2's `build_attn_metadata` passes one dict to every group's `CommonAttentionMetadata`, next to the existing `_token_to_req_indices_cache`.
- The sliding-window builder takes its plan holders from that dict, keyed by its block size, causality and index width.

What stays as before:
- Callers that do not pass the dict (the V1 runner, the draft metadata refresh of the autoregressive speculator) keep one plan per group.
- DBO micro-batches and the DSpark drafter build in separate passes, so they never share a plan.
- SM100 does not take this path: it defaults to FlashMLA mega attention, which does not use these plan holders.

Planner launches per decode step drop from 21 to 4.

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` for `tile_sched`, `FlashMLASchedMeta`, `get_mla_metadata`, `tile scheduler` and `planner flashmla` shows no PR that shares the plan across KV cache groups.

Related: #58762 (RFC #58638) reuses Mamba/GDN metadata across KV cache groups in the same `build_attn_metadata` loop. This PR does the same for DeepSeek-V4's FlashMLA plans, which are built per group however many groups there are.

## Test Plan

**Setup**
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink).
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, HF revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`.
- vLLM: "main" is the nightly wheel `0.30.1rc1.dev85+g8b84e1506` as installed; "this PR" is the same wheel with this diff applied as a Python overlay. The three changed files are identical between that nightly and current `main`.

**Server.** TP8 + EP8. DSpark uses synthetic acceptance with a configured mean acceptance length of 3.51, the same distribution in both arms, so acceptance does not depend on the model's outputs:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"<dir>","torch_profiler_activities":["CUDA"],"torch_profiler_with_stack":false,"ignore_frontend":true,"max_iterations":20}'
```

**Load.** One `vllm bench serve` call per point, with these values:

| Point | ISL | OSL | C | N |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K prompt TTFT | 8192 | 1 | 1 | 5 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | 1024 | 1024 | 1 | 6 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | 1024 | 1024 | 64 | 192 |


```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --num-warmups <C> --seed 1
```

**Arms.** Five fresh servers, run in the order B1, A1, A2, B2, B3:
- main (A1, A2);
- a prototype that shared the plans at forward time (B1, B2);
- this PR's metadata-level sharing (B3).

B3, the profile and this PR's GSM8K runs used the diff before `non_causal` joined the cache key. In every measured path the target groups are causal and the drafter builds in its own pass, so that key element changes nothing there. Every arm passes the same `--profiler-config`, which stays idle while the benchmarks run.

**Profile.** 20 decode steps under the torch profiler (`/start_profile`), 1K in / 1K out, at C1 and C64.

**Accuracy.** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions) through `/v1/chat/completions`: 5-shot multi-turn chat, thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking": false}`), temperature 0, seed 123, `max_tokens` 1024, 32 concurrent requests; 

## Test Result

**Serving.** The last column compares B3 with the mean of the main arms. Higher output throughput and lower ITL and TTFT are better.

| Point | Metric | main A1 | main A2 | this PR B3 | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | output tok/s | 317.3 | 318.9 | 326.0 | **+2.5%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | median ITL (ms) | 10.42 | 10.36 | 10.12 | **−2.6%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 1937.6 | 1942.7 | 1949.2 | +0.5% |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | median ITL (ms) | 84.15 | 83.84 | 83.51 | −0.6% |
| 8K prompt, C1 | TTFT (ms) | 1216.5 | 1220.0 | 1216.6 | −0.1% |

B3 is a single run. The main arms differ by 0.5% at C1 and 0.3% at C64, so the C64 change is small. The gain is largest at low concurrency, where the planner is a larger share of a short step. Prefill does not plan decode tiles, so TTFT is unchanged. The forward-time prototype, which also launches the planner 4 times per step, measured 325.2 and 329.2 tok/s at C1 and 1957.9 and 1952.6 tok/s at C64.

**Profile** (rank 0, 20 decode steps, B3's code):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Planner launches per step (target + drafter) | 21 | 4 |
| Planner time per step, C1 | 348 µs | 66 µs |
| Planner time per step, C64 | 868 µs | 161 µs |

**Accuracy.** Two full GSM8K runs per side, each on a fresh server:

| GSM8K, 5-shot chat, greedy (1,319 questions) | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Run 1 | 96.97% (1279) | 96.44% (1272) |
| Run 2 | 96.51% (1273) | 96.74% (1276) |
| Mean | 96.74% | 96.59% |
| DSpark acceptance length (runs 1 / 2) | 3.863 / 3.851 | 3.865 / 3.851 |

main's own two runs differ by 6 questions, more than the 2-question gap between the means. Greedy decoding at concurrency 32 varies with how requests are batched, so this rules out a large accuracy change but cannot show identical outputs.

**What covers the new path.** The unit tests below construct `CommonAttentionMetadata` directly, so `_cross_group_cache` stays `None` and they never take the sharing branch. They only show nothing else changed. The new path is covered on H20 by:
- the profile: 4 planner launches per step, so the groups do share;
- the serving runs;
- GSM8K with real DSpark verification.

The serving numbers use synthetic acceptance to measure speed and say nothing about accuracy.

**Tests.** `tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` and `tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py` give 38 passed and 31 skipped on one H20, with and without this diff. The pinned `ruff` (0.14.0) and `typos` checks pass on the changed files.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py
```

AI assistance: Claude Code helped profile and run the benchmarks. I reviewed every changed line and checked the results above.

items.title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] N-gram lookup in front of MTP drafting
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

For a single request, copying drafts from the context in front of MTP gives **+28% decode on copy-heavy prompts and +15 to 17% on Blazedit code editing, at temperature 0 and 1**, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP k=3 (stock BF16 head), one DGX Spark (GB10); SPEED-Bench +3 to 4%. Batches of more than one request are unchanged.

Adds `speculative_config.ngram_lookup` (off by default) for `method="mtp"` on Model Runner V2. When the batch has one request and its last `prompt_lookup_min` to `prompt_lookup_max` tokens (default 12 to 16) occur earlier in its context, the tokens that followed become the drafts and the MTP decode steps are skipped; otherwise MTP drafts as usual. Works with greedy and probabilistic draft sampling. Addresses #46977.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "ngram_lookup": true}'
```

## Claims

- **Single request, T=0:** copy probe 52.5 -> 67.4 tok/s (+28%), Blazedit 51.8 -> 60.9 (+17%), SPEED-Bench (5 categories) +4.0%.
- **Single request, T=1, probabilistic drafting:** copy probe 51.5 -> 66.2 (+29%), Blazedit 51.1 -> 58.5 (+15%), SPEED-Bench +2.8%.
- **More than one request:** no lookup, no sync, same code path as MTP.
- **Lossless:** the target verifies every draft. Copies are verified as one-hot drafts (greedy and probabilistic), checked by a unit test and by T=1 output distributions.

## Validation

1x DGX Spark GB10, vLLM nightly `81198e97ba` + this PR (+#56273, only to load the NVFP4 checkpoint), MTP k=3, stock BF16 draft head, thinking off, one request at a time, all arms of a column on one node with the baseline run twice. T=1 uses fixed per-request seeds. SPEED-Bench: coding, roleplay, humanities, summarization, math (160 prompts, 256 tokens). Blazedit: `vdaita/edit_5k_char`, normalized edit distance <= 0.25, 16 prompts, 1536 tokens. Copy probe: 5 rewrite/repeat prompts x 2.

| c=1 decode tok/s (AL) | T=0 greedy: MTP (2 runs) | + ngram_lookup | T=1 probabilistic: MTP (2 runs) | + ngram_lookup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| copy probe | 52.5 / 52.4 (3.63) | **67.4 (3.92), +28.4%** | 50.9 / 52.1 (3.59) | **66.2 (3.91), +28.6%** |
| Blazedit | 51.3 / 52.4 (3.59) | **60.9 (3.73), +17.4%** | 50.6 / 51.6 (3.56) | **58.5 (3.65), +14.6%** |
| SPEED-Bench, 5 categories | 41.06 / 41.29 (2.77) | 42.84 (2.79), +4.0% | 40.76 / 41.07 (2.78) | 42.07 (2.79), +2.8% |
| SPEED-Bench, humanities/summarization/math | 38.89 / 39.26 | 39.10, +0.1% | 39.05 / 39.60 | 39.44, +0.3% |

Disclaimers:
- Measured on `b0c5f0d537` with `prompt_lookup_min/max` 12/16 set explicitly; `345940129a` only makes that the default. With 5 (the `ngram` method default) the gains were smaller: copy probe +26% / +27%, Blazedit +11% / +12%, SPEED-Bench +3.2% / +1.2% (T=0 / T=1).
- Noise: the two baseline runs differ by 0.6% (T=0) and 0.8% (T=1) on the means, up to 1.6% and 4.6% per category.
- GB10 only; no datacenter numbers yet.

<details><summary>Acceptance, overhead and the single-request rule</summary>

Per-position acceptance (instrumented build, rounds drafted by each source): copies 0.90 / 0.83 / 0.78 (T=0) and 0.89 / 0.83 / 0.78 (T=1); MTP 0.76 / 0.56 / 0.39 and 0.77 / 0.57 / 0.40. The verify width is k+1 rows on every step.

Lookup kernels: 3.6 us per step. The wait for the match flag overlaps the draft prefill and added 0.3 ms GPU idle per 65 ms step at c=1 (nsys, low-repeat prompts).

Why one request: the gain is the skipped MTP decode, which needs every request to match. An earlier revision that copied in any batch and always waited was -9% aggregate at 4 requests on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8; a revision that waited only after an all-matched round skipped in about 1% of copy rounds and lost the gain. Without the skip, a copy only displaces the MTP draft, and under probabilistic drafting a one-hot copy of token x is accepted with p(x) while an MTP draft of x is accepted with min(1, p(x)/q(x)).
</details>

<details><summary>Stacked with #59973 (NVFP4 draft head) and #60068 (confidence stop), both unmerged</summary>

T=1 (greedy drafting), MTP k=6, confidence stop 0.6 / fallback 3, NVFP4 draft head, baseline repeated on one node; tree built from an earlier revision of this PR plus the composition glue below.

| | baseline (2 runs) | + ngram_lookup | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| copy probe c=1 | 66.3 / 65.3 (AL 5.0) | 93.0 (AL 6.3) | +41% |
| Blazedit c=1 | 64.3 / 64.1 | 73.4 | +14% |
| SPEED-Bench c=1, 11 categories | 44.51 / 44.76 | 45.16 | +1.2% |
| SPEED-Bench c=4, aggregate | 73.8 / 74.1 | 73.5 | -0.5% |

Composition: the `num_draft_steps` hook must receive the depth #60068 already chose (the fallback depth with more than one request), and an all-hit skip must mark every scheduled slot verifiable. That glue belongs to whichever PR lands second.
</details>

<details><summary>Tests and correctness</summary>

On 1x RTX 5090, Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base + MTP:
- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram_gpu.py` 25 passed (full-length match, single-request copy and skip, probabilistic exactness: copies accepted at p(token), output distributed as p); `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py` 59 passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py` 2 passed; the `ngram_lookup` variant runs one request at a time: 95/100 exact matches, same as plain MTP (95/100).
- Greedy, 256 tokens, one request at a time: MTP and both `ngram_lookup` runs match the reference on 61/100 prompts each; every divergence is at a near-tie (reference logprob gap <= 0.25), the same batch-shape noise as plain MTP.
- T=1, 4 copy-heavy prompts x 2000 seeded samples x 16 tokens, one request at a time, chi-square homogeneity vs no speculation (chi2/df): no speculation with other seeds 1.05 to 1.16; MTP 1.44 (greedy drafting) and 1.31 (probabilistic); + ngram_lookup 1.18 and 1.44 (greedy), 1.17 and 1.35 (probabilistic). Copies add no deviation beyond plain MTP. GSM8K at T=1 (400 questions): no speculation 0.145 / 0.145, MTP 0.163, + ngram_lookup 0.165, probabilistic MTP 0.143, + ngram_lookup 0.150.
</details>

## Details

- **Design.** `NgramMTPSpeculator` subclasses `MTPSpeculator`. The lookup kernels move from `NgramGPUSpeculator` into a shared `NgramLookup` with one new `has_match` output, set only when all `num_speculative_tokens` tokens could be copied. The MTP draft prefill always runs, so the draft KV cache stays complete; `TargetDependentARSpeculator` gets a `num_draft_steps` hook so the subclass can stop after the prefill.
- **Host sync.** Only single-request batches wait for the match flag, overlapped with the draft prefill. Data parallelism is rejected, since skipping on one rank would desync the others.
- **One draft length.** Copies use `num_speculative_tokens`, like MTP. The async scheduler fixes the verify width before drafting, so a copy length above the MTP depth would pad every miss step (measured -6% to -10% on SPEED-Bench); that needs variable-length verification and is left out.
- **Sampling.** With greedy draft sampling the rejection sampler already treats drafts as one-hot. With probabilistic draft sampling, matched requests get one-hot rows in the cached draft logits, so the ratio test sees q = 1 on the copied token and resampling uses the matching residual. `enable_adaptive_verification` is rejected (copies have no draft confidence).
- **Scope.** Single-module MTP only; Gemma4 and multi-module MTP use other speculator classes, EAGLE and DFlash are follow-ups. MRV1 is rejected through the existing unsupported-feature list.
- **Not a duplicate.** #24344 (ngram + EAGLE) targets MRV1 and runs both drafters every step. #52097 and #60339 add suffix drafters as standalone methods, not combined with a model drafter. No open MRV2 PR combines n-gram lookup with MTP. The design follows the review on #24344: verify long-but-rare n-gram drafts and short-but-accurate model drafts together, and skip the model drafter when every request hits, which pays for low-latency single requests ([1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24344#discussion_r2400623774), [2](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24344#discussion_r2400631625)).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and benchmark harness. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

items.title: [Model Runner V2] Optional post-capture warmup of every decode batch size, logits row count and graph size
items.body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in startup pass to Model Runner V2, `--kernel-config '{"enable_batch_size_warmup": true}'` (default off). It runs right after CUDA graph capture. The pass runs one scheduler step for every decode batch size, every logits row count and every CUDA graph capture size. Each shape's first use then happens at startup, not on a live request.

## Claims

- After capture, each captured graph (target and drafter) gets replayed once. The pass reaches every uniform-decode batch size from 1 to `max_num_seqs` and one prefill at every capture size.
- The eager logits GEMM, the TP logits gather and the sampler/rejection sampler run at every row count a step can have: `q*a + c` rows with `a + c <= max_num_seqs`, where `q = num_speculative_tokens + 1`. That covers first-use cuBLAS heuristic selection, lazy CUDA module loading, Triton specializations and graph upload. Without this pass, each of these can stall the first request that reaches a new batch size.
- The plan depends only on the config, so every TP rank runs the same steps and collectives.
- With the flag unset, nothing changes.

## Validation

### Test plan

- CPU unit tests (new file `tests/v1/worker/test_batch_size_warmup.py`). They check the plan's coverage: every decode batch size, every reachable logits row count, and every capture size within the token/context limits. A stub worker replays the steps and checks the KV block reservations: lookahead included, block 0 never used, no block held by two live requests. The tests also check that every warmup request finishes, and that the pass skips when the KV cache is too small or under DP.
  ```
  pytest tests/v1/worker/test_batch_size_warmup.py
  ```
- `ruff check`, `ruff format` and `mypy` on the touched files.
- GPU check (not yet run on this branch). Start any V2 model with the flag and compare it with a run without the flag. Check the `Batch-size warmup ran N steps ... in X s` log line on every rank. Then check that `--jit-monitor-verbose` reports no compiles during a mixed-concurrency replay. For example:
  ```
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <model> -tp 2 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "<draft>", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
    --kernel-config '{"enable_batch_size_warmup": true}'
  ```

### Test result

- Unit tests: 8 passed on CPU (macOS, torch 2.14.1). ruff and mypy are clean.
- GPU evidence comes from an earlier, larger, model-gated version of this mechanism, not from this branch. Setup: 8×B300, MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, TP2 engines with EAGLE3 (3 draft tokens) and CPU KV offload, an older nightly (`af7f9488c`) and our own benchmark harness. That version ran the same steps, but used dispatch introspection to skip graph sizes that were already hit. It also had an extra model-specific cuBLAS sweep, which is not part of this PR. We have not yet measured this PR on main.
  - **Without the warmup:** first use of a new batch size during serving JIT-compiled sampler kernels (`_topp_sb_*`, `_topk_topp_kernel`) mid-replay, and caused multi-second stalls. Separately, 5 of 94 TP2 engine runs hung. Each hang came on the first step of a new size (a new graph or eager lm-head row count), all within ~15 min of serving start. In one dump, one rank sat inside the first eager lm-head GEMM at a new M while its peer waited in the logits all-gather. We have not established the root cause of the hang. Pre-warming removes its precursor, but that does not prove it is fixed.
  - **With the warmup:** all 113 captured graphs replayed and 141 logits row counts ran (146 steps, about +5–12 s of startup at TP2, `max_num_seqs` 36, `num_speculative_tokens` 3). Serving logged no first-use JIT compile and no stall, and KV cache capacity was unchanged.
    - We then made the warmup the default for all our TP2 runs. Since then we have seen no further first-use hang. We did see one TP2 hang with a different signature: GPU-side, on a step that was not a first use. So this is not a fix for every TP hang.
    - Later runs without the warmup hung again on the first decode step at a new batch-size peak, inside the first-use cuBLAS lm-head GEMM.
    - GSM8K with the warmup in the stack matched the baseline.
    - We have no clean throughput A/B that isolates the warmup. It only changes startup, so we expect no steady-state effect.
- Startup cost of this branch's plan, as step counts from a CPU dry run (the time per step depends on the model):

  | max_num_seqs | num_speculative_tokens | Steps (with 26 capture sizes) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 36 | 3 | 167 |
  | 256 | 0 | 282 |
  | 256 | 7 | 2053 |

## Details

**Motivation.** The existing `warmup_kernels` runs before capture, at a handful of shapes, and targets the JIT registry and sampler features. It does not reach every batch size. Shape-dependent first-use work stays lazy until serving, as do the first replay of each captured graph and cuBLAS kernel selection for the eager lm-head GEMM at each M. Under TP, a first-use stall on one rank also holds its peers in the next collective. #48572 (open, V1 runner) fixes one instance of this: the spec-sized logits all-gather. This PR covers all row counts in V2.

**Design.**
- `plan_batch_size_warmup` (pure, unit-tested) builds the step list:
  1. Prefill a pool of `min(max_num_seqs, budget // (q+1))` requests.
  2. For `r = pool..1`, decode `r` requests. With spec decoding, also decode `r-1` of them next to `b = 1..q-1` new prefills.
  3. Run one prefill of each capture size.
- `warmup_batch_sizes` turns the steps into `SchedulerOutput`s and drives them through the worker's `execute_model`/`sample_tokens`, the same path as `warmup_kernels`.
  - KV blocks are reserved with the existing `_warmup_block_counter`, so lookahead is included. They start at 1 and are recycled after their request finishes.
  - The KV connector is disabled during the pass, and block 0 is re-zeroed afterwards, as in `warmup_kernels`.
  - Sampling uses the model's default generation-config parameters, the ones serving requests get by default. It does not use `for_sampler_warmup()`, whose `prompt_logprobs` would make capture-size prefills allocate full-vocab logits for every prompt token.
- A CPU dry run checks the block and context needs first. If they don't fit, the pass logs a warning and skips.
- The hook sits in `Worker.compile_or_warm_up_model`, after `capture_model` and before the seed reset.

**Why opt-in.** Startup time grows with `max_num_seqs × num_speculative_tokens`, and most deployments don't need it. It pays off for latency-sensitive or large TP deployments where a first-use stall is visible.

**Limitations.**
- Skipped for PP, DP, PCP, adaptive verification, pooling and encoder models. DP engines may size different KV caches and so plan different steps, which would desynchronize their DP collectives.
- The pass covers one decode query length, so dynamic speculative decoding is only partly covered. It does not cover eager steps above the largest capture size, where cuBLAS can pick new kernels at each M; `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER` is the M-independent backstop for module loading there. Prompt-logprobs shapes are also not covered.
- Some capture sizes may be warmed twice, because the plan does not ask the dispatcher which graph each step hits. That keeps the code small, at the cost of a few extra cheap steps.

---

items.title: [Core][Spec Decode] Add suffix_gpu drafter for Async Scheduling
items.body:
## Purpose

Suffix decoding (`method="suffix"`, #25784) has the best acceptance lengths among model-free drafters on repetitive/agentic traffic, but it is CPU-side and rejected by the async-scheduling whitelist, so it gives up CPU/GPU overlap exactly where spec decode helps most (high-concurrency TPOT).

This PR adds `method="suffix_gpu"`: a GPU-resident suffix drafter following the same device-state drafter contract as `ngram_gpu` (#29184) — state on device, drafts from the previous step's GPU sampled ids, no host sync on the draft path — which makes suffix decoding compatible with async scheduling. RFC: #51788.

In-tree changes (~590 lines outside tests, ~300 lines of tests):

- `config/speculative.py`: `suffix_gpu` method; reuses `suffix_decoding_*` knobs, adds `suffix_gpu_*` GPU knobs; `use_gpu_state_drafter()` groups ngram_gpu + suffix_gpu; async-scheduling whitelist admits `suffix_gpu`.
- `v1/spec_decode/suffix_proposer_gpu.py`: `SuffixProposerGPU` wrapper — borrows `update_token_ids_ngram` from `NgramProposerGPU`, same `propose()` signature and valid-count async D2H; adds cross-request global-index ingest (side stream, off the critical path) and a bucketized CUDA graph for the draft chain, pre-captured at warmup.
- `v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`: `ngram_gpu`-only gates generalized to `use_gpu_state_drafter()` (`is_ngram_gpu` local renamed to `is_gpu_state_drafter`); suffix-specific ingest hooks and draft-graph pre-capture.
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_gpu.py`: proposer unit tests.
- `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/ngram_suffix/test_ngram_suffix.py`: `test_suffix_gpu_with_async_scheduling` (GSM8K under async, mirroring the ngram_gpu async test) and `test_suffix_gpu_acceptance` (acceptance improves as the global index warms, same pattern as the suffix CPU acceptance test; pins `suffix_gpu_ingest_chunk=1`, `num_backoff=8`, `max_occurrences=128`). Both acceptance tests — including the pre-existing CPU one — now pin `enable_prefix_caching=False` and the V1 model runner: warm rounds replay identical prompts, and prefix-cache hits change decode batch composition enough to depress the measured rate below the 0.80 floor for the CPU method too
- Metrics accounting for GPU-state drafters (dedicated merge): `update_scheduler_for_invalid_drafts` returns per-request padded-slot trim counts, the worker reports them via `ModelRunnerOutput.num_invalid_spec_tokens`, and `make_spec_decoding_stats` subtracts them (fully-padded drafts are skipped instead of being recorded as zero-token draft events). Without this, padded-k scheduling deflates the reported acceptance rate for ngram_gpu and suffix_gpu alike and makes GPU and CPU drafter stats incomparable.

The drafter core lives in a standalone package (https://github.com/zip95297/SuffixGPU), lazily imported — same pattern as `suffix`'s `arctic-inference` dependency; vLLM works without it installed. All results in this PR were produced with suffix-gpu 0.1.1 (PyPI, tag `v0.1.1`; the runs used the equivalent package code at repo commit `1ac9238`, installed editable — the only delta is constructor defaults, which the vLLM config passes explicitly).

Not duplicating existing work (searched 2026-08-12): no open PR wires suffix decoding into the async path — open-PR search for "suffix" in titles returns docs/loader/KV items only, "suffix_gpu" returns none; #25784 is CPU+sync-only, #29184 is ngram-only. The metrics accounting part overlaps in mechanism with open PR #44056 (no activity since May) and is required here for suffix_gpu's acceptance test and honest benchmark numbers; this PR uses method-neutral naming (`num_invalid_spec_tokens`), also fixes ngram_gpu, and I am happy to rebase onto #44056 if it lands first or split this part out if maintainers prefer. #50518 covers the scheduler-side view for uniform spec batches and is unaffected.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_gpu.py -v` (skips without CUDA / suffix_gpu package -> CI-safe)
- Acceptance e2e (in-tree pattern; suffix_gpu + async and the pre-existing CPU suffix test as a regression check): `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/ngram_suffix/test_ngram_suffix.py -k acceptance -v`
- Greedy consistency (spec decode must not change greedy outputs): `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 python benchmarks/greedy_consistency.py 16` async no-spec vs async suffix_gpu (+ suffix_gpu eager / ngram_gpu / sync suffix CPU legs), 16 prompts x 256 tokens, token-identical required. Batch-invariant kernels + enforce_eager are required for a bitwise gate: spec decode changes batch composition, and batch-dependent FP reduction order (FlashAttention split heuristics) flips near-tie greedy argmax even between two no-spec runs.
- Serving benchmark mirroring #25784's setup (Spec-Bench, TPOT + drafted/ accepted totals, k x concurrency grid) and #29184's async-vs-sync comparison: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct bf16 TP=1 on 1x L20 48GB, k in {5,16}, concurrency 1/4/16/64/128/192/256, prefix caching off, max_num_batched_tokens=8192 and max_num_seqs=320 for every variant (spec decode schedules (k+1) padded token slots per running request before invalid ones are trimmed, so the serve-context defaults silently cap effective concurrency at the top grid points). Script: benchmarks/bench_pr_matrix.sh (attached).
- Drafter-level correctness/latency/VRAM vs the arctic CPU suffix tree (deterministic Spec-Bench replay, 221 tests): equivalence on unambiguous corpora; per-step drafting cost crosses over at B~64-128 — beyond that, CUDA-graph mode is 2.1-2.7x faster than the CPU tree's sequential walk (B=256: 1.85 vs 4.98 ms), which is what makes the drafter viable in the high-concurrency regime async scheduling targets. Full tables: https://github.com/zip95297/SuffixGPU/blob/main/RESULTS.md

## Test Result

### Unit tests

```
$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_gpu.py -v
6 passed in 5.93s   (L20, torch 2.13.0+cu130, branch commit f646af65c)
  test_propose_drafts_repetition[False/True], test_graph_and_eager_agree,
  test_capture_draft_graph_at_warmup,
  test_capture_draft_graph_warms_up_without_graph,
  test_ingest_and_cross_request_draft
```

### E2E GSM8K (in-tree pattern, mirrors ngram_gpu's async test)

```
$ pytest "tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/ngram_suffix/test_ngram_suffix.py::test_suffix_gpu_with_async_scheduling" -v
1 passed  — GSM8K accuracy: 0.762 (threshold 0.70)
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, suffix_gpu k=16, async_scheduling=True, 1319 questions 5-shot
```

### Acceptance e2e (in-tree pattern, mirrors the CPU suffix acceptance test)

```
$ pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/ngram_suffix/test_ngram_suffix.py -k acceptance -v
2 passed
  test_suffix_gpu_acceptance        (suffix_gpu k=16, async scheduling)
  test_suffix_decoding_acceptance   (CPU suffix, unchanged-behavior check)
```

suffix_gpu warm-up on the shared workload (10 rounds x 100 prompts, per-round rate/AL from an identical-config probe, prefix caching off): round 0 rate 0.428 / AL 2.03 -> round 9 rate 0.857 / AL 5.70. The final-round delta is only ~1.4k drafted tokens, so the end rate moves a few points between reruns (0.79-0.86 observed; greedy near-ties under varying async batch composition); it clears the same 0.80 floor the CPU test uses.

### Greedy consistency

```
$ VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 python benchmarks/greedy_consistency.py 16
16 prompts x 256 tokens, k=16, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, enforce_eager:
  suffix_gpu (graph)  vs async no-spec : 0/16 mismatches
  suffix_gpu (eager)  vs async no-spec : 0/16
  suffix_gpu eager    vs graph replay  : 0/16  (graph does not change outputs)
  ngram_gpu           vs async no-spec : 0/16
  suffix CPU (sync)   vs async no-spec : 0/16
identical: true
```

### Spec-Bench serving (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, 1x L20)

480 Spec-Bench prompts per point, output len 256, prefix caching off, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 320` for every variant, identical 64-prompt warmup per server before measurement. Full script attached below; raw results under `benchmarks/results/`.

**k=5 — output tok/s (mean TPOT ms)**

| variant | c1 | c4 | c16 | c64 | c128 | c192 | c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| async_nospec | 47 (21.0) | 172 (22.7) | 578 (26.4) | 1286 (47.0) | 1566 (75.6) | 1659 (109.6) | 1654 (147.1) |
| suffix_sync | 58 (17.2) | 245 (15.4) | 754 (19.8) | 1297 (45.5) | 1343 (86.0) | 1375 (127.2) | 1373 (169.5) |
| ngram_gpu_async | 46 (21.6) | 168 (23.3) | 515 (30.3) | 1126 (52.7) | 1341 (89.2) | 1389 (128.5) | 1396 (172.3) |
| suffix_gpu_async | 57 (17.6) | 239 (15.6) | 744 (19.3) | 1316 (43.2) | 1410 (80.5) | 1461 (117.6) | 1467 (154.5) |

**k=16 — output tok/s (mean TPOT ms)**

| variant | c1 | c4 | c16 | c64 | c128 | c192 | c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| async_nospec | 47 (21.0) | 172 (22.7) | 578 (26.4) | 1286 (47.0) | 1566 (75.6) | 1659 (109.6) | 1654 (147.1) |
| suffix_sync | 55 (18.2) | 239 (15.9) | 755 (19.5) | 1273 (46.3) | 1322 (86.0) | 1357 (125.8) | 1363 (167.2) |
| ngram_gpu_async | 43 (23.0) | 161 (24.3) | 519 (29.9) | 1156 (52.2) | 1339 (89.6) | 1387 (131.0) | 1405 (170.6) |
| suffix_gpu_async* | 52 (19.2) | 230 (16.2) | 736 (19.5) | 1276 (44.8) | 1349 (84.3) | 1402 (121.5) | 1417 (154.6) |

**Drafted / accepted tokens per point (AL, acceptance rate)**

| variant | k | c1 | c16 | c64 | c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| suffix_sync | 5 | 79832/22918 (1.54, 28.7%) | 86405/33544 (1.94, 38.8%) | 86516/32697 (1.89, 37.8%) | 86240/31708 (1.85, 36.8%) |
| suffix_gpu_async | 5 | 79742/22332 (1.52, 28.0%) | 87458/33453 (1.93, 38.3%) | 88350/35551 (2.04, 40.2%) | 88444/38485 (2.23, 43.5%) |
| ngram_gpu_async | 5 | 33913/9467 (2.40, 27.9%) | 34863/9738 (2.40, 27.9%) | 34527/9332 (2.35, 27.0%) | 34358/9667 (2.41, 28.1%) |
| suffix_sync | 16 | 83232/22867 (1.54, 27.5%) | 95070/34453 (1.98, 36.2%) | 93340/33505 (1.94, 35.9%) | 92211/32536 (1.89, 35.3%) |
| suffix_gpu_async | 16 | 82552/22582 (1.53, 27.4%) | 95486/34166 (2.00, 35.8%) | 98323/36571 (2.13, 37.2%) | 105420/40513 (2.33, 38.4%) |
| ngram_gpu_async | 16 | 35468/9978 (2.41, 28.1%) | 34844/9586 (2.38, 27.5%) | 33685/9643 (2.43, 28.6%) | 34316/9778 (2.42, 28.5%) |

Findings:

1. **suffix_gpu + async vs suffix + sync** (the conflict this PR resolves): parity at c1-c16, ahead from c64 up — +7% at k=5 saturation (1467 vs 1373 tok/s), +4% at k=16 (1417 vs 1363), with lower TPOT (154.5 vs 169.5 ms at k=5 c256).
2. **vs ngram_gpu + async** (in-tree GPU drafter): ahead at every grid point, up to +44% (k=5 c16: 744 vs 515 tok/s).
3. **vs async no-spec**: ahead through c64 (TPOT -8% at c64, -27% at c16, -31% at c4), behind at c128+ on this mixed workload (1467 vs 1654 at k=5 c256) — at saturation, verification compute outweighs acceptance on Spec-Bench's non-repetitive categories. Same regime behavior as the other drafters (suffix_sync 1373, ngram_gpu 1396).
4. **Acceptance scales with concurrency for suffix_gpu only**: AL 1.52 -> 2.23 (k=5) and 1.53 -> 2.33 (k=16) from c1 to c256 while the CPU suffix tree stays flat (1.94 -> 1.85, 1.98 -> 1.89) — the cross-request global index compounds under concurrent traffic.
5. Per-position acceptance at c=1 is essentially identical to the CPU suffix tree (k=16: 0.328/0.113/0.045... vs 0.329/0.115/0.046...) — the GPU drafter reproduces the CPU method's draft quality; full table in the RFC.

---

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".

<details>
<summary>Benchmark reproduction script (bench_pr_matrix.sh)</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# PR benchmark matrix for suffix_gpu (mirrors vllm-project/vllm#25784 setup).
#
# Grid: 4 variants x k {5,16} x concurrency {1,4,16,64,128,192,256}
#   async_nospec      : async scheduling, no spec (baseline, k-independent)
#   suffix_sync       : method=suffix (CPU tree, arctic), sync scheduling
#                       (async rejects it -- that is the point of this PR)
#   ngram_gpu_async   : method=ngram_gpu, async scheduling (in-tree GPU drafter)
#   suffix_gpu_async  : method=suffix_gpu, async scheduling (this PR)
#
# Model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (bf16, TP=1), 1x NVIDIA L20 48GB
# Dataset: Spec-Bench question.jsonl (md5 0c39ae23e6f213549c66d6d691c99034)
# Suffix knobs shared with the CPU suffix method: max_tree_depth=24,
# max_cached_requests=1000. ngram uses prompt_lookup 3-5 (the stronger
# baseline config from #25784).
set -x
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
# pyarrow's embedded jemalloc background thread SIGSEGVs in the EngineCore
# subprocess on this box; disable it.
export JE_ARROW_MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:false
# All variants forced onto model runner v1 for a fair comparison
# (suffix/ngram_gpu/suffix_gpu fall back to v1 anyway).
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0

BASE=/home/admin/workspace/aop_lab/app_source/zjb/suffix_async/pr_to_vllm_final
REPO=${BASE}/vllm
MODEL=meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
DATA=${BASE}/benchmarks/question.jsonl
OUT=${BASE}/benchmarks/results
PATH="${REPO}/.venv/bin:${PATH}"
# libcuda 580 shim (kernel driver 580 / userland libcuda 12.2 mismatch)
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=${BASE}/.cudafix:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}
export HF_HUB_CACHE=${BASE}/hf_cache
mkdir -p "${OUT}"
cd "${BASE}/benchmarks"

[ -f "${DATA}" ] || cp /home/admin/question.jsonl "${DATA}"
echo "$(cd ${REPO} && git rev-parse HEAD) $(cd ${REPO} && git status --short | wc -l) dirty-files" \
    > "${OUT}/run_manifest.txt"
echo "suffix-gpu $(git -C ${BASE}/../SuffixGPU rev-parse --short HEAD) $(git -C ${BASE}/../SuffixGPU status --short | wc -l) dirty-files" \
    >> "${OUT}/run_manifest.txt"
date >> "${OUT}/run_manifest.txt"

wait_server() {
    local pid=$1 i=0
    until curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/models >/dev/null; do
        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || { echo "SERVER PROCESS DIED"; return 1; }
        sleep 5
        i=$((i + 5))
        if [ "$i" -ge 900 ]; then echo "SERVER START TIMEOUT"; return 1; fi
    done
}

for k in 5 16; do
suffix_cfg=$(cat <<EOF
{"method": "suffix", "num_speculative_tokens": ${k},
 "suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests": 1000, "suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth": 24}
EOF
)
suffix_gpu_cfg=$(cat <<EOF
{"method": "suffix_gpu", "num_speculative_tokens": ${k},
 "suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests": 1000, "suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth": 24}
EOF
)
ngram_gpu_cfg=$(cat <<EOF
{"method": "ngram_gpu", "num_speculative_tokens": ${k},
 "prompt_lookup_min": 3, "prompt_lookup_max": 5}
EOF
)

for name in async_nospec suffix_sync ngram_gpu_async suffix_gpu_async; do
    if [ "$name" = "async_nospec" ] && [ "$k" != "5" ]; then continue; fi
    case $name in
      async_nospec)     args=(--async-scheduling) ;;
      suffix_sync)      args=(--no-async-scheduling --speculative-config "${suffix_cfg}") ;;
      ngram_gpu_async)  args=(--async-scheduling --speculative-config "${ngram_gpu_cfg}") ;;
      suffix_gpu_async) args=(--async-scheduling --speculative-config "${suffix_gpu_cfg}") ;;
    esac

    # suffix_gpu k16 needs headroom the 0.9 default does not leave on a
    # 46GB L20: device-resident drafter state + the (k+1)x256-token
    # verification batch spike OOM the EngineCore at c256. Report the
    # row at 0.85 (footnoted in the tables).
    gmu=0.9
    if [ "$name" = "suffix_gpu_async" ] && [ "$k" = "16" ]; then gmu=0.85; fi

    # Spec decode schedules (k+1) padded token slots per running request
    # before invalid ones are trimmed, so the serve-context default
    # max_num_batched_tokens silently caps effective concurrency
    # (k=16 x c256 needs ~4.4k token budget per step); the default
    # max_num_seqs=128 would cap the c=192/256 grid points outright
    # (320 keeps headroom above the top point). Same explicit budget for
    # all variants, spec and no-spec alike.
    vllm serve ${MODEL} "${args[@]}" \
        --no-enable-prefix-caching \
        --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
        --max-num-seqs 320 \
        --gpu-memory-utilization ${gmu} \
        > "${OUT}/server_${name}_k${k}.log" 2>&1 &
    pid=$!
    if ! wait_server ${pid}; then
        echo "SKIP ${name} k${k}: server failed to start" | tee -a "${OUT}/failures.txt"
        kill ${pid} 2>/dev/null; wait ${pid} 2>/dev/null; sleep 10
        continue
    fi

    # Same warmup for every variant before measuring: model/drafter CUDA
    # graphs, Triton JIT and the suffix global index all start cold.
    # Snapshot the cumulative spec counters afterwards so the first
    # measured point's delta excludes warmup traffic.
    vllm bench serve \
        --model ${MODEL} \
        --dataset-name spec_bench \
        --dataset-path "${DATA}" \
        --spec-bench-output-len 256 \
        --num-prompts 64 \
        --max-concurrency 16 \
        --no-oversample
    curl -s http://localhost:8000/metrics \
        | grep -E "spec_decode" > "${OUT}/metrics_${name}_k${k}_warmup.txt" || true

    for concurrency in 1 4 16 64 128 192 256; do
        vllm bench serve \
            --model ${MODEL} \
            --dataset-name spec_bench \
            --dataset-path "${DATA}" \
            --spec-bench-output-len 256 \
            --max-concurrency ${concurrency} \
            --no-oversample \
            --save-result \
            --result-filename "${OUT}/bench_${name}_k${k}_c${concurrency}.json"
        # Per-concurrency spec metrics delta comes from the cumulative
        # counters; snapshot after each client run.
        curl -s http://localhost:8000/metrics \
            | grep -E "spec_decode" > "${OUT}/metrics_${name}_k${k}_c${concurrency}.txt" || true
    done
    kill ${pid}; wait ${pid} 2>/dev/null
    sleep 10
done
done
echo "BENCHMARK ALL DONE"
```

<details>
<summary>Greedy-consistency gate (greedy_consistency.py)</summary>

```python
# Greedy-consistency gate for suffix_gpu.
#
# Speculative decoding must not change greedy outputs: run the same
# prompts with (a) async scheduling + no spec and (b) async scheduling +
# suffix_gpu, and require token-identical outputs. Additional legs
# (suffix_gpu eager, ngram_gpu, CPU suffix) localize any divergence.
#
# Bitwise comparability requires batch-invariant kernels: spec decode
# changes batch composition, and FlashAttention's split heuristics make
# FP reduction order batch-dependent, flipping near-tie greedy argmax
# (verified: without this, async no-spec disagrees with itself across
# duplicated prompts in one batch). So we set VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 and
# enforce_eager=True (batch-invariant aten overrides must not be
# bypassed by compile/cudagraphs; on SM<90 vLLM cannot guarantee them
# under compiled paths).
#
# Each engine runs in its own subprocess so GPU memory is fully
# released between runs (spawn context; worker must be module-level).
import json
import os
import sys

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", "1")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

MODEL = "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"
K = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 16

SUFFIX_GPU_SPEC = {
    "method": "suffix_gpu",
    "num_speculative_tokens": K,
    "suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests": 1000,
    "suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth": 24,
}
SUFFIX_CPU_SPEC = {
    "method": "suffix",
    "num_speculative_tokens": K,
    "suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests": 1000,
    "suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth": 24,
}

# High-repetition prompts (exercise the accept path) + regular prompts
# (exercise the empty-draft path), repeated for multi-request scheduling.
PROMPTS = [
    "Repeat the following sentence 20 times: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
    "Count from 1 to 100, separated by commas.",
    "Explain the theory of relativity in one paragraph.",
    'List the JSON object {"a": 1, "b": 2} fifteen times, one per line.',
] * 4
SP = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=256, ignore_eos=True)


def run(mode: str) -> list[list[int]]:
    kwargs = {
        "model": MODEL,
        "enable_prefix_caching": False,
        "gpu_memory_utilization": 0.8,
        # Batch-invariant aten overrides must not be bypassed by
        # compile/cudagraphs (SM8.9 cannot guarantee them otherwise).
        "enforce_eager": True,
    }
    if mode == "async_nospec":
        kwargs["async_scheduling"] = True
    elif mode == "async_suffix_gpu":
        kwargs["async_scheduling"] = True
        kwargs["speculative_config"] = SUFFIX_GPU_SPEC
    elif mode == "async_suffix_gpu_eager":
        kwargs["async_scheduling"] = True
        kwargs["speculative_config"] = {
            **SUFFIX_GPU_SPEC,
            "suffix_gpu_use_cuda_graph": False,
        }
    elif mode == "async_ngram_gpu":
        kwargs["async_scheduling"] = True
        kwargs["speculative_config"] = {
            "method": "ngram_gpu",
            "num_speculative_tokens": K,
            "prompt_lookup_min": 3,
            "prompt_lookup_max": 5,
        }
    elif mode == "sync_suffix_cpu":
        kwargs["async_scheduling"] = False
        kwargs["speculative_config"] = SUFFIX_CPU_SPEC
    else:
        raise ValueError(mode)
    llm = LLM(**kwargs)
    outs = llm.generate(PROMPTS, SP)
    token_ids = [list(o.outputs[0].token_ids) for o in outs]
    del llm
    return token_ids


def _worker(q, mode):
    q.put(run(mode))


def run_in_subprocess(mode: str) -> list[list[int]]:
    import multiprocessing as mp

    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
    q = ctx.Queue()
    for _attempt in range(3):
        p = ctx.Process(target=_worker, args=(q, mode))
        p.start()
        try:
            ids = q.get(timeout=1800)
            p.join()
            return ids
        except Exception:
            p.kill()
            p.join()
            import time

            time.sleep(20)
    raise RuntimeError(f"engine failed 3 times for mode={mode}")


def diff(ref: list[list[int]], got: list[list[int]]) -> list[dict]:
    mismatches = []
    for i, (r, g) in enumerate(zip(ref, got)):
        if r != g:
            j = next(
                k
                for k in range(min(len(r), len(g)) + 1)
                if k >= min(len(r), len(g)) or r[k] != g[k]
            )
            mismatches.append(
                {
                    "prompt_idx": i,
                    "first_diff_pos": j,
                    "ref_len": len(r),
                    "got_len": len(g),
                }
            )
    return mismatches


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os

    prev = f"greedy_consistency_k{K}.json"
    if os.path.exists(prev):
        cached = json.load(open(prev))
        nospec_ids = cached["nospec_ids"]
        sgpu_ids = cached["suffix_gpu_ids"]
        scpu_ids = cached["suffix_cpu_ids"]
        print("reusing cached nospec/suffix_gpu/suffix_cpu ids")
    else:
        nospec_ids = run_in_subprocess("async_nospec")
        sgpu_ids = run_in_subprocess("async_suffix_gpu")
        scpu_ids = run_in_subprocess("sync_suffix_cpu")
    sgpu_eager_ids = run_in_subprocess("async_suffix_gpu_eager")
    ngram_ids = run_in_subprocess("async_ngram_gpu")

    result = {
        "k": K,
        "num_prompts": len(PROMPTS),
        "suffix_gpu_vs_nospec": diff(nospec_ids, sgpu_ids),
        "suffix_gpu_eager_vs_nospec": diff(nospec_ids, sgpu_eager_ids),
        "suffix_gpu_eager_vs_graph": diff(sgpu_ids, sgpu_eager_ids),
        "ngram_gpu_vs_nospec": diff(nospec_ids, ngram_ids),
        "suffix_cpu_vs_nospec": diff(nospec_ids, scpu_ids),
    }
    result["identical"] = not result["suffix_gpu_vs_nospec"]
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    with open(f"greedy_consistency_k{K}_full.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(
            {
                "result": result,
                "nospec_ids": nospec_ids,
                "suffix_gpu_ids": sgpu_ids,
                "suffix_gpu_eager_ids": sgpu_eager_ids,
                "ngram_gpu_ids": ngram_ids,
                "suffix_cpu_ids": scpu_ids,
            },
            f,
        )
```

</details>

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] FlyDSL decode monokernel for DSpark verify steps on MI355X (--monokernel)
items.body:
## Overview

With `--monokernel`, Muse Spark Open MXFP4 on 8x MI355X (TP8 + expert parallelism, 7-token DSpark draft) runs
decoder layers 1-60 of every verify step of 1-16 requests as persistent FlyDSL launches. One launch, or three, cover
the work from a layer's attention output to the next layer's q, o-gate and KV insert. All other steps and layers 0 and
61 run the stock path. The flag is off by default.

## Claims

- AgentX (agentic-coding traces, DSpark at synthetic acceptance length 4.05, all requests, full mode) with
  `--monokernel`: interactivity (1000 / p90 ITL) / total tok/s/GPU of 403.9 / 2974 at c = 1, 325.0 / 3009 at c = 2,
  299.0 / 4410 at c = 4 and 200.8 / 7375 at c = 8.
- GSM8K (full set, 5-shot) with `--monokernel`: 0.9689-0.9757 at c = 1-8.
- Opt-in only. If the deployment is not supported, vLLM refuses it at startup with every reason. Steps that the
  kernels do not cover run stock. Nothing changes without `--monokernel`.

## Validation

### Performance: AgentX

Server: the recipe's Muse Spark Open MXFP4 command on 8x MI355X with the DSpark draft. Changes for the benchmark:
`--max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, and synthetic acceptance
(`"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":4.05`). The server is TEP8 + `--monokernel`.
Benchmark: `agentx profile --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --concurrency C`. This dataset is
agentic-coding traces with an ISL p50 of 159k tokens and a maximum of 397k. Metrics are over all requests:
interactivity = 1000 / p90 ITL (tok/s/user) and total tok/s/GPU.

Full mode (`--benchmark-duration 3600 --warmup-requests-per-lane 10`), one run a point, this PR's head:

| c | requests | interactivity (tok/s/user) | total tok/s/GPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 291 | 403.9 | 2974 |
| 2 | 449 | 325.0 | 3009 |
| 4 | 667 | 299.0 | 4410 |
| 8 | 1360 | 200.8 | 7375 |

This PR does not measure c >= 16.

### Accuracy

Real acceptance (the recipe's block verification). Same server flags without prefix caching, TEP8 + `--monokernel`,
this PR's head. GSM8K = InferenceX gsm8k.yaml, full set (1319), 5-shot.

| check | c = 1 | c = 2 | c = 4 | c = 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K flexible / strict | 0.9757 / 0.9757 | 0.9719 / 0.9719 | 0.9742 / 0.9742 | 0.9689 / 0.9697 |
| GSM8K DSpark mean acceptance length | 4.320 | 4.363 | 4.245 | 4.424 |

The server logs have 0 errors and 0 peer-wait timeouts in every run.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
       AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN_SHORT_QUERY_3D=1 VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --reasoning-parser muse --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser muse \
  --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend mp --language-model-only \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --disable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --monokernel

# GSM8K: InferenceX gsm8k.yaml (5-shot, full set), lm-eval chat completions, temperature 0, concurrency 16
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template --tasks gsm8k.yaml \
  --model_args model=amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=1048576 \
  --gen_kwargs max_tokens=16384,temperature=0,top_p=1
```

For AgentX: add `--enable-prefix-caching` and set `"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":4.05`.
</details>

## Details

### Hook point

- `MuseSpark1xForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading` calls `maybe_attach_mono`. This runs after the per-layer quant
  finalize, so the experts are already in their shuffled kernel layout. The call is collective over the TP group.
  `MuseSpark1xModel.mono` is `None` without `--monokernel`.
- `MuseSpark1xModel.forward`: if `mono.try_forward(...)` returns the residual stream, the stock layer loop does not
  run. Otherwise the stock loop runs as before.
- `MuseSpark1xAttention.forward` is split into `front` / `core` / `back`, and `MuseSpark1xDecoderLayer.forward` into
  `attention_input` / `after_attention`. The stock path calls the same code in the same order.
- `compute_logits` and `compute_logits_local` start an asynchronous read of the kernels' health words (every 64
  steps, outside graph capture). A peer-rank wait that timed out raises there, instead of a hang.
- The model runner, the scheduler and the attention backends are not changed.

### Eligibility

- At startup (default deny; one `ValueError` with every reason, agreed over the TP CPU group): gfx950 with 256 CUs,
  the checkpoint's text config, TP8 + `--enable-expert-parallel` (linear placement, no EPLB), no PP / DP / DCP / PCP,
  DSpark with 7 draft tokens, no LoRA, no KV connector or offloading, bf16 model and KV cache, Quark OCP-MXFP4 W4A4
  experts on AITER (shuffled weights and scales), the fused QK-norm / RoPE / KV insert, `ROCM_AITER_FA`.
- Every step, from rank-invariant data only (the batch shape and the attention metadata counts, because all ranks
  must take the same path). The step must be a uniform verify step of 1-16 requests x 8 tokens, in FULL CUDA graph
  or eager mode, with dense bf16 LBHNC KV caches (block size 16). All other steps run stock.

### Buckets

| rows (requests) | build | launches a layer |
|---|---|---|
| 8 (1), 16 (2) | K3, S = 8 / 16 | 1 |
| 24-32 (3-4) | HA + HM + HB, S = 32 | 3 |
| 40-128 (5-16) | HA + HM + HB, S = 64 / 96 / 128 (rows padded up; `nrows` = real rows) | 3 |

`--max-num-seqs` selects the builds that the server compiles. Weights are views of vLLM's parameters. The kernels
write KV into vLLM's pages through `slot_mapping` (padding slots are skipped). The peer buffers are plain `cudaMalloc`
memory, opened over IPC on the TP CPU group. All launch arguments are fixed pointers, so vLLM's FULL CUDA graphs
capture the launches.

### Fused verify attention (8, 16 and 32 rows)

From layer 2 on, layer i's verify attention runs at the head of K3_i / HA_i, for both the sliding-window and the full
layers. It is split over all 256 CTAs by (request, KV head, key range) and merged before o_proj. It reads the layer's
bf16 KV cache through its KV cache group's `block_table` / `seq_lens`, the impl's softmax scale, and the window
(2047, 0). Only blocks inside the window are read. The descriptor tables hold pointers and counts only. They are
keyed by their contents and written once, so captured graphs read fixed tables. If `max_model_len` is above the 1M
keys that the builds stage block ids for, vLLM's op runs. Builds of 40 rows and more keep vLLM's op.

### Numerics: a16w4, opt-in behind `--monokernel`

The kernels keep the MoE activations in bf16 (MXFP4 weights x bf16 activations). The stock path is W4A4: it
quantizes the expert inputs and the SwiGLU output to MXFP4. Thus `--monokernel` output is close to the stock output,
but not bit-identical. Prefill runs stock (W4A4). Other differences are the reduction order (fixed rank order in fp32)
and the bf16 norm multipliers. The flag help, the module README and the recipe describe this.

### Known issues

- With the DFlash2 draft (not the recipe's draft), `--monokernel` lowers the real acceptance length: AgentX c = 4
  4.83 -> 3.52. The aux-hidden-state bookkeeping is the same as in the stock loop: the new tests compare the aux
  states for the DSpark, DFlash2 and seam target layers. The cause is open (per-rank draft divergence, or a draft
  that is more sensitive to the a16w4 numerics). The recipe's DSpark draft is not affected on AgentX (2.83 vs 2.87).
- On current main, the GSM8K run with real acceptance shows a DSpark acceptance length of 4.25-4.42 for mono
  (c = 1-8; 4.39 at c = 16) vs 4.69 for stock (c = 16). Before the rebase (vLLM main 6ee316e) it was 4.47 vs 4.50: the stock acceptance length
  went up with the rebase and mono did not. Accuracy is not affected. We investigate this in a follow-up.
- The FlyDSL cleanup keeps some unused launch arguments (the timeline and EPLB-replica pointers) and LDS slots. With
  them, every build compiles to the same code objects as the validated kernels: identical `.text` for all 30 server
  builds.
- CI cannot run the kernels: they need 8x MI355X and the checkpoint's shapes. The CI test runs the host side on one
  MI355X (below). The kernel paths were validated with the serving runs above.

### Vendored kernels

`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/mono/kernels/` (about 7.8k lines) holds AMD's Muse Spark FlyDSL monokernel sources,
reduced to the builds that vLLM launches. They carry their MIT license header after vLLM's SPDX lines (as in
`rocm_block32_gemm.py`). They import FlyDSL and AITER's FlyDSL helpers only when the monokernel attaches. The host code
(mono/ without kernels/, model.py and two small core edits) is about 1.5k lines.

### Test plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main)
```

- On 0fc5cbf: 1x MI355X: 47 passed (24 s); no GPU: 18 passed, 29 skipped. Pre-commit: all hooks pass.
- `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` builds a tiny real MuseSpark1x model (Quark MXFP4 experts, `ROCM_AITER_FA`, LBHNC bf16
  KV cache). It loads the model through the dummy loader + `load_weights` + `process_weights_after_loading`, and runs
  it with real attention metadata builders and bound KV caches.
  - Guards: refused before the weight finalize, accepted after it. Config and deployment guards use real vLLM
    configs.
  - Weight views alias vLLM's parameters.
  - Step tests (7 shapes x 3 target-layer sets): the FlyDSL launches build only for the checkpoint's TEP8 shapes. The
    test runs each launch as the stock layer pieces that it replaces, on the device memory at the pointers that the
    host passes. Hidden states and the KV caches of all layers are bit-exact vs the stock loop. Aux hidden states
    match at fp32 rounding. Prefill, mixed, short-query, too-wide and PIECEWISE steps run stock.
  - Mutants fail these tests: aux shifted by one layer, dropped aux gather, wrong q buffer for the fused attention,
    KV written to the wrong layer, dropped stock layer-1 aux.
- The test is in the `Basic Models (Other)` step and its MI355 mirror (`models_basic.yaml`).

### Follow-ups

- Move to the RFC #60904 layout (`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/specialized_decode/`, tests under
  `tests/models/muse_spark/`) in a separate PR.
- A TP8 numerics test on 8x MI355X: each launch vs vLLM's layer on random full-size weights, as
  `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` does.
- Fused attention for the 40-128-row builds (c >= 5).
- Remove the unused launch arguments and LDS slots (this changes the code objects, so it needs a new validation).
- The DSpark acceptance gap on current main and the DFlash2 acceptance drop (known issues).

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). The submitter reviewed every changed line
and ran the tests and benchmarks listed above.
